citations.title: Microsoft 365
citations.text:
Microsoft 365

Using the data management and protection services offered by Rubrik Security Cloud, you can protect Microsoft 365 data operations.

For all Microsoft 365 data management operations, including backup and restore, Rubrik Security Cloud (RSC) uses Azure cloud computing services. All Microsoft 365 data management operations run within an Azure
 account hosted either by you or by Rubrik. The
 protected data is always held within the hosting Azure tenant, which ensures data
 security and privacy.

RSC backs up the data from Microsoft 365 objects by creating a
 snapshot of the corresponding data source, such as Exchange (mailboxes, calendars,
 and contacts), OneDrive, SharePoint, and Teams. This first full snapshot is a
 complete backup of the Microsoft 365 data. RSC then creates incremental
 snapshots based on the changed information, such as deleted or modified email messages
 or files.

The data in every user account protected by Rubrik requires a license. Each user license
 automatically protects a shared mailbox at no extra cost.

Microsoft 365 deployments on RSC require:* In customer\-hosted mode, firewall rules configured for communication among RSC, Microsoft 365, and Microsoft Azure.
* Administrator access to the Microsoft 365 subscription you want to protect.
* An enterprise AAD app. The enterprise AAD app creates apps
 required for authorizing RSC to act as a control plane for
 accessing Microsoft 365 and Azure accounts.
* A working secret for the enterprise AAD app, required for
 communication with Microsoft 365 data.

After configuring the enterprise AAD app and the secret, you can contact Rubrik Support
 to apply the secret to the AAD app and enable Microsoft 365 support for RSC. You can then set up a Microsoft 365 subscription on the RSC deployment.

Microsoft 365 user accounts derive protection from the SLA Domain assigned to the
 Microsoft 365 subscription.

citations.title: Microsoft 365 Backup Storage
citations.text:
Microsoft 365 Backup Storage

With the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage feature, you can back up Microsoft 365
 applications such as SharePoint sites, OneDrive user accounts, and Exchange mailboxes. You
 can also restore large volumes of data during ransomware attacks, accidental deletion, or
 malicious data deletion and overwrite events.

To safeguard the data of your organization and ensure easy data recovery, Microsoft has
 introduced the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage feature. This feature provides the ability
 to back up all or specific Microsoft 365 applications such as SharePoint sites, OneDrive
 user accounts, and Exchange mailboxes. You can also restore large volumes of data during
 ransomware attacks, accidental deletion, or malicious data deletion and overwrite
 events.

Microsoft offers the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage feature through two options:* Microsoft 365 admin center
* Rubrik as a partner

Note: You can use only one of these options at a time.
RSC can integrate with the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage APIs to provide
 backup and storage solutions.

When you choose to protect your Microsoft 365 applications using Microsoft 365 Backup
 Storage through Rubrik, RSC acts as a controller, which means RSC has permissions to perform backup and recovery using Microsoft 365
 Backup Storage.

The Microsoft 365 Backup Storage feature is in addition to the Microsoft 365 Data
 Protection solution and requires purchasing separate licenses.

citations.title: What is Datto SaaS Protection?
citations.text:
What is Datto SaaS Protection?
Services that are backed up

Datto SaaS Protection provides data backup capabilities for the following M365 services: OneDrive, Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams. Key points for each service are described in the following table. Other services, such as Microsoft Planner, are not supported.

| Service | Key points |
| --- | --- |
| OneDrive | * All documents in each individual's OneDrive account are backed up. * Regular images files (.jpg) are backed up. * A snapshot is saved for each of the daily backups.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* Image libraries (e.g., smart albums, face/location albums, and UI groups) are not captured. * Shared and group documents are not backed up as this is not allowed by the M365 API. |
| Exchange | Mail:* Shared mailboxes can be backed up. * Group emails can be backed up. * [Microsoft 365 Exchange In\-place archives](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/enable-archive-mailboxes) (Online Archives) can be backed up (see [Protecting Exchange online archives](../Managing_your_organization_environment/protect-online-archives.html)). * Notes in Exchange can be backed up but can only be restored as messages. The messages can be converted back into notes.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example, public folders are not backed up. Contacts:* A user's contacts are backed up.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* Shared and group contacts are not backed up as this is not allowed by the M365 API. * Contact profile pictures are not backed up. * Attachments that are references to OneDrive objects through the API cannot be accessed and backed up.  Calendar:* Team calendar events can be backed up through attendee Exchange backups (each attendee has a copy of the event in their calendar).  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* Shared and group calendars are not backed up as this is not allowed by the M365 API. * Attachments that are references to OneDrive objects through the API cannot be accessed and backed up. |
| SharePoint | The following SharePoint site data is backed up:* Documents * Templates * Assets * Pages * Collections: Microsoft sites that administrators have created that do not fall into the SharePoint Root Site collections. * Lists: Custom lists, document libraries, Wiki page libraries, task lists. To identify a list type, right\-click the three\-dot menu and click **Details**.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* SharePoint metadata is not backed up. * SharePoint archive data is not backed up because it cannot be accessed from the cold storage tier within SharePoint. * The following are not backed up due to M365 API limitations: contacts, calendars, forms, image libraries, and event lists.  NOTE  Datto SaaS Protection only supports the cloud version known as "M365 SharePoint". Local installations of M365, such as SharePoint 2010 and 2013, are not supported. |
| Teams | Public channels:

  * Content (Team sites, files, and documents) is backed up * Calendar meetings are backed up * Public channel conversation messages are backed up  Private channels (found under SharePoint sites): * Content (Team sites, files, and documents) is backed up * Conversations are backed up  Shared channels: * Content (Team sites, files, and documents) is backed up * Conversations are backed up  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* 1\-1 chats (e.g., personal direct messages) are not backed up. * Per single Teams message/conversation, 1000 is the maximum number of replies that can be backed up. |

Exchange backup exceptions
If you are using Datto SaaS Protection for M365 and your mail service is disabled or not provisioned, Datto will not be able to back up contacts and calendars.

The Exchange service encompasses mail, contacts, calendars, and tasks but will fail backups if the mail service isn't present because Exchange in 2\.0 is linked directly to Exchange in 1\.0\. 

Exchange backups include online archives only if the online archive backup feature has been enabled for the organization. For details, see [Protecting Exchange online archives](../Managing_your_organization_environment/protect-online-archives.html).

Datto does not back up the rules for M365 Exchange services.

OneNote backup exception
Due to a Microsoft limitation, backup of OneNote sections larger than 2 GB may fail. If you experience this issue, you can opt to split the section into smaller ones that are less than 2 GB.

Backing up Microsoft 365 tenant data

 You can configure a backup job for Microsoft 365 tenants. For primary backups, the Forever Incremental, Consolidate full, and Custom full templates only support deduplication disk storage. Duplicate backups can be targeted to any supported storage. When you create a forever incremental backup, a full backup is taken followed by incremental backups. A Consolidate Full backup is run by consolidating the previous set of full and incremental backups. Subsequent incremental backups use the consolidate full backup as a baseline to determine changes.

1. On the Backup and Restore tab, select a Microsoft 365 tenant from the list of servers.
2. Do one of the following:

	* In the **Backups**group at the top of the screen, click**Backup \> Create Microsoft 365 Backup**.

citations.title: Back up Microsoft 365
citations.text:
Back up Microsoft 365

With ActiveProtect, you can proactively safeguard your organization's Microsoft 365 data, ensuring that a backup is always available for restoration when required.

How backup works
ActiveProtect utilizes Microsoft Entra ID applications to exchange data with your Microsoft 365 organization during backup and restore sessions. When you add a Microsoft 365 tenant to your ActiveProtect site, the system will automatically register a new Entra ID application to access your organization's data.

Automated backup strategy
Auto-backup rules are crucial for Microsoft 365 backups. Set rules to automatically protect existing and newly added objects that meet your criteria. Likewise, if any protected accounts, sites, or teams are removed from your Microsoft 365, they will no longer be backed up. Their previously backed-up data will be stored on the assigned backup servers according to the designated retirement plan for retention.

This approach makes backups effortless and maintains synchronization with the source Microsoft 365 tenant.

Data deduplication
ActiveProtect uses global source-side deduplication to minimize data transfer and optimize storage efficiency across all workloads.

citations.title: Things you should know...
citations.text:
Things you should know...
**What Office365 Features do you support backing up?**

We support the below named functionalities of Microsoft 365:

* Exchange Online
* SharePoint
* OneDrive
* Teams
* Planner (Group Plans)
* Entra ID (a P1 license is required for at least one user)

In addition, we do not support Office 365 Germany, Office 365 US Government, Office 365 operated by 21Vianet in China.

Click[here for a full list](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/19687847835793) of supported features.

**Microsoft 365 Subscription Plans**
The below Microsoft 365 plans have been QA tested and are known to be fully supported:

* Business Basic
* Business Standard
* Business Premium
* E1, E3 and E5
* A1, A3, A5 Faculty and Student Plans
* F3

Microsoft continuously update their list of available subscription plans, so if your plan is not listed above, however supports Exchange/SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams/Planner functionality then this should still work but has not yet been fully tested.

If Office 365 plan does not support specific features such as SharePoint or OneDrive, we cannot back up that specific feature from the Backup Source. 

**Can I schedule backups at a specific time or take manual backups?**
TLDR; backups are taken **automatically**and there is no need to set up schedules or take manual backups on your end. More information [can be found here](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/19687873472401).

**How long is the backup data retained?**
TLDR; you have the option to retain everything that has been backed up ever since you starting backing up, provided that the account's Subscription is paid and active. Otherwise, there is the option to set up a **retention** and a **purge** **policy**. More information[can be found here](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/19687793161489).

**Where are the backups stored?**
Read more on [where your backups are stored](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/19687831989009) here.

**How is it billed?**
### 

Read more on the [O365 Total Backup Subscription plan](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/19687860407441) here.

**Can I archive or delete a backup?**
Yes, if you choose to **\[Exclude User from Backups \& Delete Backup Data]**, this will stop backup and restore operations from taking place and delete all Backup Data for this user. You will still be charged a monthly fee for this User, if the user still holds a valid M365 license.

If the user does not hold a valid M365 license during the billable month, it will not be billed for and will retain any backup data for free.

If you would like to Backup this User again in the future you may include it again but older backup versions will not be available. You can also go further and specifically select if you would like Mailbox/OneDrive/Teams Chats/Group Mailboxes/SharePoint Files/Group Plans via the **\[Advanced Options...]**

If you choose **\[Disable this User]**, there won't be any further backups for that mailbox thereby archiving it. You will continue to be billed for this user.

**Skipped Files**
In certain cases items will be skipped during a backup operation and these will get retried multiple times. However in some cases these items are actually returned to us an inconsistent/corrupted when requested from M365\. If these items are not backed up for an extended period of time after multiple retries, they will automatically be excluded from backup going forward unless that item is changed/updated.  

[**Self Service**](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/30297611963537)
The M365 Tenant must be synchronized with the Control Panel for Self Service Recovery to be available to end users. You can do this from the Total Protection screen and choose Generic Onboarding or Plan 1/2/3/4\.

Protecting SharePoint data

Spanning Backup for Microsoft 365 protects the document libraries and files contained within site collections in SharePoint. As part of the backup, Spanning discovers all site collections in SharePoint, including Team Sites, Group Sites, and Microsoft Teams, and then conducts a backup of the document libraries and files in your tenant. 

To start running backups, the SharePoint backup type must be enabled and you must enable backups for each site collection you want to protect. The SharePoint backup type is enabled by default. (To check your current setting, see [Backup \& Security tab settings](settings.htm#Backup_&_Security_tab).) Once enabled, backups run automatically each day, and you can run a manual backup at any time. 

You can enable backups for all site collections or select individual site collections to include in the backup process. This is great for scenarios where you don't want to include specific site collections in your backups. You can also choose to backup all new site collections, which preserves your existing site collection settings and protects any newly discovered site collections automatically.

SharePoint backup is only accessible to Spanning administrators. Select the SharePoint tab on the left to manage your SharePoint backups.

Define a backup selection[](https://documentation.atempo.com/tina-4.9.5/tina-4.9.5-en/administration-guide/backup/microsoft-365#define-a-backup-selection)

Tina is equipped with a wizard to define a backup selection for Microsoft 365. When creating a new selection, you can choose to back up:

*   The Exchange Online component or selected paths.

*   The OneDrive for Business component or selected paths.

*   The Microsoft Teams component or selected paths.

*   The SharePoint Online component or selected paths.

*   The OneNote for Business component or selected paths.

> **Important**: The user defined in the catalog must be authorized to modify backup selections. Ask an administrator of the Web Admin Console to grant you the required right if needed.

**To grant a user the right to modify backup selections**

1.  Sign in to the Web Admin Console as an administrator.

2.  In the navigation pane, click the **Settings** tab.

3.  Click the **Users and Groups** tile.

4.  In the list of defined users, click the row of the user you want to grant the right to.

5.  In the **Backup and Restore** section, select the **Backup selection (add, modify, or delete)** checkbox (Figure 1).

6.  Click **Save**.

![](/media/bf70969a-9c60-455e-9766-eef025a56ded/a12a8fa5b87ea386.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'User profile' dialog for a user named 'collector_user', showing custom permission settings under the 'Other' tab. The interface displays checkboxes for various administrative, media, backup, and archive permissions, with options like 'Administer and supervise' and 'Backup selections' being selected.

    **Image** : User profile options

**To define a backup selection**

1.  Sign in to the Web Admin Console.

2.  In the navigation pane, click the **Agents** tab.

3.  Click the row corresponding to your Microsoft 365 application. The **Application Details** window is displayed.

4.  In the left-hand pane, click **Backup Selections.**

5.  Under **Backup Selections**, click the **Add a new backup selection** button. The **Backup Selection Configuration** wizard is displayed (Figure 2).

![](/media/bf70969a-9c60-455e-9766-eef025a56ded/8ff9b20c4c26d24c.png)

> **Figure:** This screenshot shows the 'Backup selection configuration' wizard screen, specifically step 1 of 1. It depicts the initial state for defining a backup selection for an agent (M365), with options to browse agents/users or add paths manually, and a section to select backup strategies.

6.  Provide the backup selection information:

    1.  Click **Browse agent** to display agents in a tree structure or Browse users to display a list of users.

    2.  Enter the user name, domain name (Windows OS only), and password.

    3.  Click **Connect**.

    4.  Select the users to back up.

    5.  Click **OK**. A path for each selected folder appears in the backup selection's list of paths.

    **Or**

    • Click **Add a path manually** and enter the path of the backup selection in the field that appears.

7.  Under **Strategies**, select the strategies to manage the backup selection.

8.  If needed, select the following options:

    1.  **Parallelize the backup when possible**. This option allows several backups to be launched at the same time.

    2.  Compress files.

9.  If needed, enable the **Advanced Options** button and select the following options:

    1.  Whether or not to encrypt data before writing to tape.

    2.  Specify files to exclude from the backup selection.

    3.  Specify files to include in the backup selection.

    4.  Select the maximum size of files to back up.

    5.  Select the maximum age of files to back up.

10.  Click **Finish** to create the backup selection.

If you are deploying self-service restore, see the Configure self-service restore in your \\ Microsoft 365 application section.

To optimize the backup window and avoid network bandwidth issues, it is recommended to roll out the backup of Microsoft 365 data gradually. Mailbox backups can be parallelized depending on the number of available drives. A mailbox backup uses one drive. Each mailbox is treated as an individual job, and in case of an error, only the affected mailbox will be restarted. In some cases, a full backup of the affected mailbox will be triggered.

Value Proposition and Data Sheet
Overview

This article covers x360Cloud for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace. x360Cloud for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace ensures that the data within an organization’s instance is backed up, protected, recoverable, and compliant. Data loss happens, even in the cloud. But can your clients afford to lose important emails, contacts, calendars, and work documents? citations.title: How Keepit processes data in Microsoft 365
citations.text:
How Keepit processes data in Microsoft 365

Keepit uses 3 different APIs to process (back up and restore) Microsoft Office 365 data:

* EWS (Exchange Web Services) API is used to back up Exchange (Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Tasks, In\-Place Archive) and Public Folders.
* SharePoint REST \+ CSOM is currently used to process OneDrive, Sites (Legacy), and some parts of the new SharePoint.
* Microsoft Graph is used to back up Microsoft 365 Groups \& Teams (Calendar, Conversations, Channels, Chats, Planner, Files) and parts of SharePoint.

On a high level, the Keepit backup consists of several services that collaborate with each other in order to process, store, and show backed up data to the end user. Keepit communicates with Microsoft 365 through a gateway, which is also part of our system. In order to back up and restore Office 365 data, we make HTTPS calls to the Microsoft public APIs mentioned above and then we save the data to our secure storage systems. Since the data is stored in a special encoded format, it cannot be displayed to the user as is. For this reason, we use other internal services for data transformation, indexing, and the search function. This both improves user experience as well as makes our system more flexible and robust.

Additionally, we support the backup of all file types and extensions across the Microsoft 365 environment.

citations.title: Overview
citations.text:
Overview
Overview of Microsoft 365 Backup > Scenarios and value proposition

Overview of Microsoft 365 Backup
Microsoft 365 Backup is designed to ensure your organization's data is always protected and easily recoverable. With the ability to back up all or select SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Exchange mailboxes, Microsoft 365 Backup provides comprehensive coverage for your critical data.

Note

Microsoft 365 Backup is now available for Government Community Cloud (GCC) organizations. Microsoft 365 Backup also supports PowerShell cmdlets. You can find the associated PowerShell cmdlets in the [Microsoft 365 Backup Storage Graph APIs](/en-us/graph/api/resources/backuprestoreroot) reference guide.

Business continuity assurance is a top\-of\-mind concern for many companies. Microsoft 365 Backup delivers business continuity peace of mind by providing performance and reliable restore confidence. When evaluating a backup and restore offering, what really matters isn't solely the backup, but the ability to restore your data to a healthy state quickly when you need to do so. Recovering large volumes of content is difficult when copying data at a scale from a remote, air\-gapped location requiring weeks or even months to get your business back up and running.

In cases of a ransomware attack that encrypts large swaths of your data, or instances of an internal accidental or malicious data deletion or overwrite event, you need to be able to get your business back to a healthy state as soon as possible. This is what the Microsoft 365 Backup product offers, both through the Microsoft 365 admin center, and via partner applications built on the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage platform.

To summarize, applications built on top of the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage platform deliver the following benefits regardless of the size or scale of the protected tenant:

* Fast backup within hours.
* Fast restore (see [performance expectations](#performance-expectations) later in this article).
* Full SharePoint site and OneDrive account restore fidelity, meaning the site and OneDrive are restored to their exact state (excluding, for example, taxonomy mastered outside the site scope) at specific prior points in time via a rollback operation.
* Full Exchange mailbox item restores or granular item restores using search, for modified or fully deleted items.
* Consolidated security and compliance domain management.

citations.title: Overview
citations.text:
Overview
Overview of Microsoft 365 Backup > Architectural overview and performance expectations > Architecture

Microsoft 365 Backup provides ultra\-fast backup and restore capabilities by creating backups within the protected services' data boundaries.

Microsoft 365 Backup not only provides uniquely fast recovery from common business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR) scenarios like ransomware or accidental or malicious employee content overwrite or deletion. More BCDR scenario protections are also built directly into the service. For example, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Exchange Online have a proprietary architecture design for resiliency with replicated copies of customer data to failover to live active copies seamlessly without the need for end customer intervention.

Our backups are protected from malicious overwrites because OneDrive, SharePoint, and Exchange use Append\-Only backup storage. This means that SharePoint can only add new content blobs and can never change old ones until they're permanently deleted. The Exchange items are backed up in a similar append\-only manner and can't be accessed by a client process (such as Outlook, OWA, or MFCMAPI). This process ensures that items can't be changed after an initial save, protecting against attackers that try to corrupt old versions. For more information about the built\-in service and data resiliency, see [SharePoint and OneDrive data resiliency in Microsoft 365](/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-sharepoint-onedrive-data-resiliency) and [Exchange Online data resiliency in Microsoft 365](/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-exchange-data-resiliency).

Key architectural takeaways:

* Data never leaves the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary and honors the geographic locations of your current data residency. Limited metadata (for example, tenantID and siteIDs) sent to Azure for billing purposes only.
* The backups are immutable unless expressly deleted by the Backup tool admin via product offboarding.
* OneDrive, SharePoint, and Exchange have multiple physically redundant copies of your data to mitigate the impact of physical disasters.

![Diagram showing the Microsoft 365 data trust boundaries.](/media/6f8e0591-421f-4465-850b-d15cdb1e4396/6e81299af4815450.png)

> **Figure:** Diagram showing the Microsoft 365 data trust boundaries, with the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage platform at the center, supporting OneDrive, Exchange, and SharePoint within the Microsoft 365 trust boundary, and connecting to recognized partner solutions above.

citations.title: Considerations and Limitations
citations.text:
Considerations and Limitations

* To back up public folder mailboxes, Veeam Backup account must have a valid Exchange Online license and an active mailbox within the Microsoft 365 organization.
* Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 supports backup of public folder and discovery search mailboxes and determines correctly object type for shared mailboxes in Microsoft 365 organizations with modern app\-only authentication. To back up these objects, Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 needs access to Exchange Online PowerShell. To do this, a Microsoft Entra application requires the Exchange.ManageAsApp permission and the Global Reader role. It is recommended to grant both the permission and the role to the Microsoft Entra application after upgrading Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 to version 8. For more information, see [Configuring Backup of Public Folder and Discovery Search Mailboxes](after_upgrade.html#pf_mbx).
* To back up user mailboxes, make sure that a mailbox has a valid Microsoft 365 license. Otherwise, such unlicensed mailbox will not be backed up.
* Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 backs up public folders that are located under the IPM\_SUBTREE folder only.
* You can select only the root public mailbox when backing up public mailboxes. The child folders of the selected public mailbox will be backed up as well.
* If you modify a retention policy tag for a folder, Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 will perform full synchronization of that folder during the subsequent backup job session. For more information, see [this Microsoft article](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/Exchange/policy-and-compliance/mrm/retention-tags-and-retention-policies).
* When backing up Microsoft Exchange mailboxes, Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 does not create a new version of an item if the Read/Unread property of such item was changed. That said, the Read/Unread property of each of the backed\-up items always remains exactly the same as it was during the initial backup.
* Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 does not back up permissions for sharing mailbox folders and Calendar.

SharePoint and OneDrive Data

* To back up SharePoint and OneDrive objects, make sure that a user account has a valid Microsoft 365 license with SharePoint plan enabled. Otherwise, a backup job will fail with the following error: "User %name% does not have a valid Microsoft 365 license with SharePoint plan enabled".
* A SharePoint Site Collection hierarchy is not supported if the root site was not configured. Make sure to configure the root site in advance using a SharePoint site template of your choice. Otherwise, the following error occurs: "Error: Failed to find web template ID for: STS\#\-1\. This organization account might be missing a valid SharePoint license. Web configuration is not complete".

* If a SharePoint item has several versions with identical owshiddenversion values, only the latest version of this item is backed up, all the rest versions are skipped from processing.

* Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 does not guarantee backup of OneNote notebooks if their size is greater than 2 GB. For more information, see [this Microsoft article](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/restrictions-and-limitations-in-onedrive-and-sharepoint-64883a5d-228e-48f5-b3d2-eb39e07630fa#onenotenotebooks).

* When you perform backup of SharePoint data, Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 does not back up the following objects:

* External SharePoint lists.

For more information, see [this Microsoft article](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/differences-between-native-and-external-lists-6601eda9-b722-4bf8-a2bf-ce25cf3d2fd0).

* SharePoint folder attachments.
* SharePoint site collection recycle bin.
* SharePoint sites created by Microsoft Loop.

* Archived SharePoint sites.
* SharePoint sites with blocked access.
* Sensitivity labels applied to SharePoint sites and lists.

Microsoft Teams Data

* As part of Microsoft Teams data backup, Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 backs up only the following types of channel tabs: Website, Planner, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, PDF, Document Library, OneNote, SharePoint, Stream, Forms, Power BI, Power Automate (ex Flow) and Azure DevOps.

* Team posts (formerly team chats) backup is only supported for Microsoft 365 organizations with modern app\-only authentication. For more information, see [this Veeam KB article](https://www.veeam.com/kb4340).

* When you perform backup of Microsoft Teams data, Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 does not back up the following objects:

* One\-on\-one and group chats.

For more information about chats in Microsoft Teams, see [this Microsoft article](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/first-things-to-know-about-chat-in-microsoft-teams-88ed0a06-6b59-43a3-8cf7-40c01f2f92f2).

citations.text:
Considerations and Limitations

* To back up user mailboxes, make sure that a mailbox has a valid Microsoft 365 license.
* Backup and restore of public folders requires the Variable License Model.
* To back up public folder mailboxes, a valid Microsoft Exchange Online license and an active mailbox within the Microsoft 365 organization is required.
* Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 only backs up and restores public folders located under the IPM\_SUBTREE folder.
* When backing up public mailboxes, only select the root public mailbox. Any child folders of the selected public mailbox will be backed up as well.
* When backing up Microsoft Exchange Online mailboxes, Veeam Data Cloud does not create a new version of an item if the Read/Unread property of such item was changed. That said, the Read/Unread property of each of the backed\-up items always remains exactly the same as it was during the initial backup.
* Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 does not back up permissions for sharing mailbox folders and calendar.
* Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 does not support backup of dynamic distribution groups. Members of dynamic distribution groups cannot be resolved.
* Resource/equipment mailboxes are presented and available for backup with the general User type.
* Microsoft 365 group owner data backup is not supported if the group owner is not a member of the Group.
* The Type property for discovery search, resource and equipment mailboxes is not resolved. Such mailboxes are available for backup with the general User type.
* Grouping of lists with To Do tasks is ignored during backup.
* The TeamsMessagesData folder is not supported for backup.

OneDrive and SharePoint Online Backup

* To back up SharePoint Online and OneDrive objects, make sure that a user account has a valid Microsoft 365 license with a SharePoint Online plan enabled.
* If a SharePoint item has several versions with identical owshiddenversion values, only the latest version of this item is backed up. All the other versions are skipped from processing.
* SharePoint web parts can only be backed up if their ‘exportmode’ property is enabled. Non\-exportable web parts are not supported. For more information, see [this Veeam KB article](https://www.veeam.com/kb3146).
* SharePoint web parts export mode can only be changed automatically if such type of a property is supported and can be modified in the source SharePoint Online site or OneDrive account.
* To back up and restore SharePoint sites with certain specific templates, such as Business Intelligence Center, Product Catalog, and Visio Process Repository, an organization must have a valid SharePoint license.
* SharePoint Online personal site and OneDrive account backup will fail if the site has reached its storage space quota and if your service account is not granted with the Site Collection Administrator (site admin) permissions for this site.
* A backup of a SharePoint site created within the last 24 hours before the backup policy run may be performed with an error because of the time required for its configuration update.
* Version history backup is not supported for the Microsoft SharePoint .aspx web pages.
* Backup of the SharePoint App Store applications added to a site is not supported.
* Backup of the SharePoint App Store applications that use JavaScript redirects is not supported.
* In organizations with the renamed SharePoint domain, sites explicitly selected for backup need to be re\-added to a backup policy.
* After a SharePoint site URL has been changed, a site with an old URL can still be selected for backup. Processing of a site with an old URL will fail with the warning: Site was moved to another URL. As a workaround, to suppress the unwanted warnings, you can exclude these sites from a backup policy.
* Backup of personal SharePoint sites that use the SPSPERS\#1–SPSPERS\#10 templates and are not associated with any user fails with the warning: Cannot resolve personal site owner. The user may not have a valid Microsoft Office 365 license with SharePoint plan enabled.
* Backup of a SharePoint team site that has the information barriers mode set to Implicit fails with error: Exception from HRESULT: 0x87FA0080.
* Items count in a backed\-up OneDrive folder is not updated on incremental backup policy runs. When exploring OneDrive backups, you will see the item count as it was at the time of the first full backup run.
* When you perform backup of SharePoint data, Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 does not back up the following objects:

* External SharePoint lists

For more information, see [this Microsoft article](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/differences-between-native-and-external-lists-6601eda9-b722-4bf8-a2bf-ce25cf3d2fd0).

citations.title: About Microsoft 365 Backup Policies
citations.text:
About Microsoft 365 Backup Policies

This page is for Data Protection.With a Microsoft 365 backup policy, you choose which users, SharePoint sites, and teams Eon backs up from your tenant.
Eon backs up the tenant daily, and the **Back up all users** and **Back up all Teams** options pick up new users and teams as Eon discovers them.

This article explains what a Microsoft 365 backup policy backs up and how its schedule works.

A Microsoft 365 backup policy protects one Microsoft 365 tenant, and a tenant can be assigned to only one Microsoft 365 backup policy at a time.

Users and sites
Within the tenant, you choose whose Exchange mailbox and OneDrive account to back up:

* **Back up all users**: All current users are included, and new users are included automatically as they’re discovered.
* **Back up direct members of specific groups \& teams**: Only users who are direct members of the groups or Microsoft Teams you select are included.
Nested group members aren’t included, and the group or team itself isn’t backed up as a distinct object.
See [Group and team selection](/data-protection/saas-workloads/microsoft-365/microsoft-365#group-and-team-selection) in *Microsoft 365 Support* for how Eon backs up a group’s members.

You also choose which SharePoint sites to back up:

* **Back up all sites**: All sites are included by default. You can optionally exclude specific sites.
* **Back up specific sites**: Only the sites you select are included.
* **Don’t back up sites**: No SharePoint sites are backed up.
Mailboxes and OneDrive accounts are still backed up according to your user selection.

Teams
The policy’s Microsoft Teams section is a separate selection from **Users**, and it controls whose channel messages Eon backs up:

* **Back up all Teams**: Every team in the tenant is included, and teams discovered later are included automatically.
You can optionally exclude specific teams in **Optionally exclude Teams**.
* **Back up specific Teams**: Only the teams you select are included.
Unlike **Back up all Teams**, this option doesn’t add teams discovered after you save the policy, so a new team isn’t backed up until you select it.
* **Don’t back up Teams**: No channel messages are backed up.

Channel files aren’t part of the Microsoft Teams selection.
They’re stored in SharePoint, so your SharePoint sites selection covers them instead.

See [Microsoft 365 Support](/data-protection/saas-workloads/microsoft-365/microsoft-365) for what Eon backs up from a team and what it leaves out.

Schedule
A Microsoft 365 backup policy has exactly one schedule that always runs daily.
The frequency can’t be changed.
When you create the policy, you choose a start time, a retention period (including unlimited retention), and the vault to store snapshots in.

To set up a policy, see [Create Microsoft 365 Backup Policies](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/microsoft-365/create-microsoft-365-backup-policies).
For what data Eon backs up and restores, see [Microsoft 365 Support](/data-protection/saas-workloads/microsoft-365/microsoft-365).

Additional information

* [Backup Policy Overview](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/backup-policy-overview)

citations.text:
Overview

This page is for Data Protection.Restoring from Eon recovers Microsoft 365 data without relying on Microsoft’s retention window.

This article links to the restore instructions for every Microsoft 365 service Eon supports.

Before you restore, connect a Microsoft 365 restore tenant: a connected tenant, paired with a dedicated Azure subscription, that Eon restores into.
Every Microsoft 365 restore goes only to the tenant the data was backed up from.
See [Microsoft 365: Connect Restore Tenants](/data-protection/saas-workloads/microsoft-365/connections/connect-restore-tenants) for the one\-time setup steps.

Restore your data

citations.title: Getting started
citations.text:
Getting started

Last Updated: 2026\-07\-31
With IBM Storage
Protect™ for Mail: Data Protection for Microsoft™ Exchange Server, you can back up and restore Microsoft Exchange Server databases to IBM Storage
Protect storage or local shadow
volumes. A  local shadow volume contains data that is stored on shadow
volumes, which are local to a disk storage system.

Data Protection for Exchange Server provides a connection between
an Exchange Server and an IBM Storage
Protect, which allows
Exchange Server data to be protected and managed by IBM Storage
Protect. Data Protection for Exchange Server protects Exchange Server data and improves
the availability of Exchange Server databases.

Data Protection for Exchange Server backs
up and restores Microsoft Exchange
Server databases to IBM Storage
Protect storage
or local shadow volumes.
You can use a command\-line interface or graphical user interface
(GUI) to back up and restore Exchange Server databases.

Microsoft no longer supports the Microsoft Legacy application programming interface (API) for
streaming backup and restore operations. Microsoft
supports the use of Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) technology for backup and restore operations. 

Data Protection for Exchange Server uses
the IBM Storage
Protect API
to communicate with the IBM Storage
Protect, and the
Exchange API to communicate with Exchange Server. 

In addition to these APIs, Data Protection for Exchange Server 
 VSS operations require the IBM Storage
Protect backup\-archive
client (VSS Requestor) and Microsoft VSS
to produce an online snapshot (point\-in\-time consistent copy)
of Exchange Server data.

You must install Data Protection for Exchange Server on
the same system as the Exchange Server. Data Protection for Exchange Server also
supports backup and restore operations in a Database Availability
Group (DAG) environment.

* **[Data Protection for Microsoft Exchange Server capabilities](/docs/en/SSERBW_8.2.2/mail-exc/dpe_con_info_features.html)**  
Data Protection for Microsoft Exchange Server helps you to protect and manage Exchange Server environments by facilitating the backup, restore, and recovery of Exchange Server data.
* **[Volume Shadow Copy Service framework](/docs/en/SSERBW_8.2.2/mail-exc/c_dpfcm_vss_service_exc.html)**  
Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) provides a common interface model to generate and manage online snapshots of Exchange Server data.
* **[Data backup processing](/docs/en/SSERBW_8.2.2/mail-exc/dpe_con_backup_overview.html)**  
Data Protection for Exchange Server can use the Microsoft Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) framework to produce a point\-in\-time, consistent, online copy of Exchange Server data.
* **[Data restore processing](/docs/en/SSERBW_8.2.2/mail-exc/dpe_con_res_overview.html)**  
Data Protection for Exchange Server can use the Microsoft Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) framework to complete fast and instant restores of database backups. You also restore VSS backups to an alternate database and complete Exchange mailbox restore operations.
* **[Data Protection for Exchange Server with IBM SAN Volume Controller and IBM Storwize V7000](/docs/en/SSERBW_8.2.2/mail-exc/c_dpfcm_svcstwz_using_exc.html)**  
The way in which you configure the VSS provider for IBM® SAN Volume Controller and IBM® Storwize® V7000 controls the type of FlashCopy® operation that runs when you create a VSS snapshot.
* **[Automated IBM Storage Protect server failover for data recovery](/docs/en/SSERBW_8.2.2/mail-exc/c_dpfcm_autoclientfailover_exc.html)**  
If you use IBM Storage Protect SnapshotData Protection for Exchange ServerData Protection for SQL Server with the IBM® Storage Protect configuration, IBM Storage Protect SnapshotData Protection for Exchange ServerData Protection for SQL Server can automatically fail over to the failover server for data recovery when there is an outage on the IBM® Storage Protect server.

citations.title: Backup with Global Admin
citations.text:
Backup with Global Admin
Backup with Global Admin

1. Select Add Backup and Sign in with Microsoft 365 . In Add Microsoft 365 Backup window select Authorize with Global Admin . Use Global Admin and accept the requested permission that Microsoft 365 prompts you for.

![Image](/media/e4714e79-c7b8-4883-a470-47d7253e95aa/079760a81897283f.png)

2. A new non-licensed global admin account is created for backup purposes. The username created starts with ' backupadmin ' . Copy and save the username and credentials to use them in next steps.
3. The next step is device authorization, where you configure Microsoft Exchange Online Remote PowerShell access with OAuth token:
- a) Copy the user code, open the link provided, and use the backup admin account created in previous steps to sign into Exchange Online Remote PowerShell.
- b) You need to provide additional security verification (using a mobile app) and enter the generated verification code. If the procedure takes too long, the user code might expire, and you need to repeat the previous step after regenerating the user code.
- c) Once logged in, an additional MFA verification of the backup admin is requested.
- d) When you see a message that you have signed into Microsoft Online Remote PowerShell application on your device, you can close the window.

After these steps are performed, verification of authorization is done when you click Verify & Continue . If the verification fails, the steps must be repeated.

4. The final step is the re-authentication of the backup admin and granting the Email Backup the Oauth token access.

citations.title: How the Agent Backs Up and Restores Exchange Server Data
citations.text:
How the Agent Backs Up and Restores Exchange Server Data

The Agent for Microsoft Exchange Server integrates with Arcserve Backup to let you back up and restore Exchange Server databases and database components (such as mailboxes). It also integrates with the Exchange Server's backup and restore functions, enabling you to perform online backups.

The agent offers many benefits, such as:

* Manage backups of Exchange Server databases, mailboxes, and public folders from a remote location.
* Perform online database backups and restores using Exchange Server's backup and restore APIs.
* Schedule Exchange Server backups using the Backup Manager.
* Note: For Exchange Server 2010, 2013, 2016, and 2019, Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) APIs are used.
* Schedule Exchange Server backups using the powerful Backup Manager.
* Back up to a wide array of storage devices.
* Push agent technology
* Multi\-threading
* Multi\-streaming support
* Enhanced cluster support (on Exchange Server versions prior to 2010\)

The agent lets you perform Database level Exchange Server backups and restores.

question: Management wants backup status reports delivered automatically on a schedule. Which products can do that, and where do the reports end up?
answer:
Nakivo (Nakivo Backup & Replication): Automatic reports (job reports, Failed Item Protection, Overview, Protection Coverage) are emailed to specified recipients on a configured schedule, with optional PDF/CSV attachments [1]; reports can also be created manually and saved to a chosen location [2].
N-Able (Cove Data Protection): Scheduled Reports are configured in the Management Console and emailed to internal and external recipients on chosen days and times, with selectable dashboard views and email layouts [3]; schedules can be edited, disabled, or deleted afterward [4].
Veeam (Veeam Data Cloud): Scheduled reports are configured per tenant with a name, recipients, and daily/weekly/monthly/custom frequency; recipients receive an email with a link to download the report, which is valid for 7 days [5].
Veeam (Veeam Service Provider Console): Backup reports (e.g., Protected VMs, Protected data, Protected computers) can be generated and sent by email as PDF attachments, with a configurable schedule for automated generation [6].
AWS (AWS Backup): AWS Backup Audit Manager delivers daily jobs or compliance reports to an Amazon S3 bucket in CSV or JSON format via a report plan, with on-demand reports also possible [7][8].
NinjaOne (Dropsuite) (SaaS Backup): The Backup Summary Report is automatically generated on the fifth of each month and delivered via email to partner-registered addresses, or can be downloaded from the portal [9][10].
Keepit (Keepit): Backup coverage reports can be scheduled on the Data Protection Dashboard with daily, weekly, or monthly frequency; recipients receive a download link and a CSV file per selected data area [11][12].
Datto (SaaS Protection for M365): The Daily Backup Success Report is automatically generated each day in PDF and CSV formats and sent to specified recipient email addresses at approximately 1 AM in the selected time zone [13][14].
Afi.ai (Afi.ai): Periodic status reports can be enabled with daily, weekly, or monthly frequency and delivered via email, Slack, Teams, or Google Chat notification channels [15][16].
Synology (Active Backup): Reports can be generated on a customized schedule and sent via email (after enabling DSM email notifications) [17].
Synology (ActiveProtect Manager): Scheduled data protection summary reports can be enabled with a chosen frequency, summarizing backup and restore activities for recipients [18].
Arctera (Backup Exec): Standard and custom reports can be scheduled to run once or on a recurring schedule, with optional email notification that can include a copy of the report [19][20].
CloudAlly (CloudAlly for MS 365): Daily backup task failure reports can be sent to a provided email address via the Autotask integration, starting from the next backup cycle [21]; summary notifications with configurable daily/weekly/monthly frequency are delivered to configured recipients as a CSV attachment or download link [22].
HYCU (R-Cloud Hybrid Cloud Edition, HYCU for Azure): Reports can be scheduled to generate automatically daily, weekly, or monthly and delivered by email to recipients in PDF, PNG, or CSV format [23][24].
Commvault (CommCell Console, Commvault Cloud): Automated reporting in the Commvault Console generates and emails scheduled reports regularly, with predefined reports such as the Backup Summary Report [26].
AvePoint (Elements (MSP Administration)): Report templates can be set to scheduled and automatically generated with weekly to annual frequency, sent at 12:00 UTC to customers and/or internal users via email link or attachment [27].
Acronis (Cyber Protect On-premises): Reports can be scheduled to be sent via email and/or saved to a folder in .pdf and/or .xlsx format on selected days and times [29][30].
Barracuda (Data Inspector): Reports can be scheduled for creation and email delivery daily, weekly, or monthly in CSV or PDF format to specified recipients [31].
Barracuda (Barracuda Backup): Daily Backup Summary Reports can be configured for users or non-user recipients, and customized Backup Summary Reports can be sent to any email recipient [32].
Arcserve (Arcserve Backup): Advanced reports can be scheduled to run immediately, at a specified time, or on a repeat interval, and can be sent by email [33][34].
Microsoft (Azure Backup): The Email Report feature in Backup Reports creates automated tasks (via a deployed logic app) to receive periodic reports via email [35].
IBM (Storage Protect): Capacity Licensing XML reports are generated automatically at the end of backup operations at a configurable interval (1–365 days) into a specified network shared folder [37].
IBM (Storage Defender): Reports can be scheduled to run at periodic intervals and sent by email to recipients at specified times [38].
Rubrik (Rubrik Security Cloud): Report schedules deliver RSC reporting data as HTML email with a PDF document and CSV file at a scheduled date and time to any registered email address [39][40].
Bacula (Bacula): A third-party Python script (baculabackupreport.py) run via cron sends an HTML email report of jobs run in the last 24 hours [41].
Druva (Druva): Report subscriptions can be configured to send reports of activities, including errors or unsuccessful backups and restores, to administrators' email on a scheduled basis [43].
Google (Google Cloud Backup and DR): Prebuilt daily backup schedule compliance and backup/restore job reports are available in BigQuery and Data Studio after executing a prebuilt script that routes logs through a log sink [45][46].
Axcient (x360Recover): Client Executive Summary Reports can use Scheduled Delivery on a recurring basis (e.g., monthly) to up to ten specified email recipients [47].
Axcient (Axcient (General)): A daily email notification can be configured containing data from the 30-Day Trending report and individual Detailed Machine-Specific Usage reports [48].
Hornetsecurity (Altaro) (Backup & Recovery): Reports (e.g., Backup Status Report) can be exported as CSV or via an API link (JSON) from the Monitoring & Alerts tab, with alerts and recipients managed for backup and restore operations [49].
Atempo (Lina): Report templates include a Reports tab used to schedule automatic reports [50].
Dell (PowerProtect Data Manager): Reports can be scheduled from the Report Browser to automatically send to one or more email recipients on a recurring schedule as CSV attachments [51].
Salesforce (Own): The Weekly Backup Report surveys active Salesforce backup services from the last seven days, informing of successes, warnings, and errors [52].
Unitrends (Unitrends Unified Backup): Reports can be generated from report categories and exported as PDF or CSV, with email reports available such as Appliance Status and Schedule Success/Failure reports [55].
Storware (Backup and Recovery): Reporting functionality provides backup and restore statistics with date ranges and filtering, including transfer size reports for chargeback [56].
Spanning (User Guide): Backup status is viewable on the Dashboard, and backup status information can also be received via Chatter posts and status notification emails [57].
Cohesity (NetBackup IT Analytics): The Job Summary Report can be generated from customizable templates with scope filters to analyze backup and restore job status [59].
No supporting passage found for: CloudCasa, Eon, Flosum, GRAX, Gearset, Portworx, Red Hat, Slide, Trilio, Velero, Zerto.

citations.title: Notifications & Reports
citations.text:
Notifications & Reports
Notifications \& Reports > Automatic Reports

To set automatic reports, fill out the fields in the Automatic Reports section:

* **Job reports**: If this option is selected, NAKIVO Backup \& Replication will send an HTML report after the completion of every job (regardless of the job success or failure) to email addresses specified in the text field. Use a semi\-colon to separate multiple email addresses.
* **Failed Item Protection report**: Contains information about all items which had failed to be protected by backup and/or replication jobs, and the error message. Additionally, configure **Report info in the last** option by entering the number of days you want to get the report for.
* **Overview report**: If this option is selected, NAKIVO Backup \& Replication will generate the Overview report (which includes information about all jobs and groups in the product) on the date and time specified in the scheduler and will send the report to the recipients specified in the text field. Use a semi\-colon to separate multiple email addresses.
* **Protection Coverage**: If this option is selected, NAKIVO Backup \& Replication will generate the Protection Coverage report. This includes information about all VMs \& instances protected by backup and/or replication jobs as well as the information about all unprotected VMs \& instances. The report will be sent to the recipients specified in the text field on the date and time specified in the scheduler. Use a semi\-colon to separate multiple email addresses.
* **Schedule**: Configure the schedule at which you want to get the reports.
* **Attach PDF copy to all automated reports**: Select this option to get the additional attached copy of the report in the PDF format.
* **Attach CSV copy to all automated reports**: Select this option to get the additional attached copy of the report in the CSV format.

> **Note**
> 
> 
> 
> NAKIVO Backup \& Replication supports the following special characters in reports:
> 
> 
> * US special characters
> * Characters in the following languages:
> 
> 
> 	+ Vietnamese
> 	+ Japanese
> 	+ Korean
> 	+ Chinese
> 	+ Arabic

citations.text:
Managing Jobs
Creating Job Reports

To create a general report for all your jobs:

1. Select **Overview** in the **Data Protection** menu.
2. Click **Create Report**.
3. Choose one of the following reports:

	* **Overview report**: Contains information about the status and errors of all jobs.
	* **Recovery points report**: Contains information about the recovery points of backups/replicas for the chosen job or jobs created within a specific period.
	* **Protection coverage report**: Contains information about all VMs and instances protected by backup/replication jobs, as well as about all unprotected VMs and instances. Choose either the PDF or CSV format for the  **Protection coverage report** and click **Create**.
4. Choose a location to save the report and click **Save**.

[

![](/media/f5060300-fb45-474e-9183-ca36d2de97de/a402a83c3ec4.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Jobs' section in a backup management interface, showing a dropdown menu opened from the '+' button with options for creating backup, copy, replication, and site recovery jobs. A sub-menu for 'Monitoring Report' displays options: Overview report, Recovery points report, and Protection coverage report. The background shows a job overview table with 19 successful jobs listed.

](../../Resources/Images/Create Monitoring Report.png)

To generate reports from for an individual job, do the following:

1. Go to the list of jobs.
2. Select the job that you need to generate a report for and right\-click it or click **Create**.
3. Select one of the following reports from the **Create Report** menu:

	* **Last run report**: Provides data on the last run of the job.
	* **Job history report**: Provides data on job runs that occurred during a specified time period. To generate a report, pick a start date on the left and finish date on the right side of the popup and click **Create**.

	Job history reports feature the **Calendar View** hyperlink. Clicking on it opens the high\-level calendar view page with the summary of the backup status of every backup item within a single job.

	The report data is organized in separate blocks of weeks each consisting of two columns:

		+ **Item Name** \- displays the job object(s) name as ordered in the corresponding job
		+ **Day of the week (Date)** \- displays the status for processing each job object

		Possible statuses:

			- Successful – displayed for successful object processing
			- **Failed**  – displayed for failed object processing
			- **Skipped**  – displayed for skipped object processing
			- **Stopped**  – displayed for stopped object processing
		+ The status field is empty if no object processing was scheduled on a particular day.
		+ The columns representing weekdays that are not included in the reported range are empty.
		+ Weekdays are displayed when there is at least one run on the week.
	> **Notes**
	> 
	> 
	> 
	> 
	> 	+ The enhanced **Calendar View** report data is displayed from old to new for all reports where the **Job Runs** block is shown except for the **Monitoring** area and the **Point\-in\-time report**.
	> 	+ To customize the first day of the week, go to the **Settings \> General tab \> System Settings \> Regional Format** tab and select the needed day in the **First day of week** selector.

	[

![](/media/f5060300-fb45-474e-9183-ca36d2de97de/82bc56796275.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the System Settings page under the Settings menu, displaying the Regional tab with options for clock format, first day of week, decimal symbol, short and full date formats, and default time zone.

](../../Resources/Images/Managing+Jobs/Regional Format.png)
	* **Point\-in\-time report**: Provides data on a particular job run. To generate a report, choose a date in the popup and click **Create.**
	* **Recovery points report**: Contains data of recovery points created within specific period.
	* **Protection coverage report**: Contains information about all VMs and instances protected by backup/replication jobs, as well as about all unprotected VMs and instances.
	* **Failed item protection report**: Contains information about job objects for which processing failed during the last job run. Only backup and replication jobs are included.

Scheduling Reports

You can schedule reports in Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365\. When you schedule a report, you specify the frequency and email recipients. Reports run at 12:00 AM UTC on the scheduled day and email notifications are sent when complete. Once a scheduled report runs, the recipients receive an email from Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 with a link to download the report. The report is valid for 7 days.

To schedule a report, do the following:

1. On the Microsoft 365 page, click the name of the tenant you want to manage.
2. Select Reports.
3. Click Add a Scheduled Report.

[

![Scheduling Reports](/media/dacfd41b-aba7-471c-9246-c9dfa8d089f4/135f8f41f6cc5de9.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Reports page in Microsoft 365 Org, showing an empty list of scheduled reports and a highlighted 'Add a Scheduled Report' button.

](images/m365_reports_schedule.png "Scheduling Reports")

1. Select the report you want to schedule. The available reports are the following:

* [Protected Objects Snapshot](m365_reports_protected_objects_snapshot.html). This report lists the status of protected and unprotected Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams objects at a given point in time.
* [Protected Objects History](m365_reports_protected_objects_history.html). This report lists the history of protected Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams objects over time, to surface persistent gaps.
* [Backup Activity History](m365_reports_backup_activity_history.html). This report lists backup policy runs across a time period, with outcomes and objects processed.
* [Restore Activity](m365_reports_restore_activity.html). This report lists Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams restore operations across a time period.
* [User Protection](m365_reports_user_protection.html). This report lists every user with their portection status, last backup date, email and organization.

1. Specify the settings for the report. For more information on the settings, see the dedicated section for each report.
2. In the Schedule Name field, specify a name for the scheduled report.
3. In the Recipients field, specify the email addresses of the report recipients. Use one line for one email address. Your own email address is added by default. The specified users will receive an email from Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 with a link to Veeam Data Cloud to download the report. The report is valid for 7 days.

| Tip |
| --- |
| * You can also specify email addresses outside of your organization. The recipients must be able to log in to Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 to download the reports. * To receive the scheduled report email, make sure to include no\-reply@mail.cloud.veeam.com in your allowed, approved or safe senders list in your email client. |

1. In the Generate section, select whether to receive the scheduled report daily, weekly, monthly or create a custom frequency.

* Daily. The report will run every day.
* Weekly. The report will run every week. From the Day of the week drop\-down, select which day of the week you want to receive the report.
* Monthly. The report will run every month. In the Select day section, choose one of the following:

* Day of the week. Select which day of the month you want to receive the report. For example, when you select First Monday, you will receive the report on the first Monday of the month.

* Calendar date. Select the day of the month from the 1st to the 31st from the drop\-down list.

* Custom. Select the check box next to the month and day you want to receive the report.

1. Click Schedule Report.
