citations.title: View daily schedule compliance reports for vaulted backups in Cloud Logging.
citations.text:
View daily schedule compliance reports for vaulted backups in Cloud Logging.

This page provides an overview of prebuilt daily backup schedule policy reports,
which are available in BigQuery and Data Studio. These reports
are displayed for resources that are protected using [backup plans](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/cloud-console/backup-plan).

You can access these reports after you [execute the prebuilt script](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/logs-route-vault-bigquery#sink) in the
same project where the logs are being routed through the log sink.

**Note:** If you want to learn about the daily backup schedule policy report that
are protected using the [backup template](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/create-plan/create-template)
in the appliance management console, see [Daily Schedule Compliance reports](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/compliance-reports-bigquery).
The daily backup schedule compliance report includes the following fields.

* **date**: The date that the compliance status is reported on.
* **resource\_type**: The type of resource, for example, a Compute Engine
instance.
* **resource\_name**: The name of the resource that is associated with the daily
schedule backup policy.
* **resource\_project\_name**: The name of the project where the resource exists.
* **backup\_plan\_name**: The name of the backup plan that is associated
with the source resource.
* **rule\_name**: The name of the backup rule used to backup jobs.
* **backup\_window**: The backup window where you have defined the timeframe of
when backup jobs can start. The backup window uses the 24\-hour clock format,
with start and end times between 00 and 24 hours, and a minimum of six hours
for the window.
* **backup\_window\_time\_zone**: The timezone of the daily schedule backup
policy window.
* **backup\_schedule\_compliance\_status**: The compliance status of the daily
schedule backup policy. The status can be pending, successful, or failed.
* **comment**: A description explaining the compliance status of the daily
schedule backup policy.
* **backup\_vault\_name**: The name of the backup vault that is used for
daily schedule backup policy.
* **backup\_vault\_project\_name**: The backup vault project that is used
for daily schedule backup policy.
* **backup\_vault\_location**: The location of the backup vault.
* **resource\_location**: The location of the protected resource.

What's next
* Learn how to [Execute prebuilt reports script](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/logs-route-vault-bigquery#sink)
* Learn how to [Write custom queries in BigQuery](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/custom-query)
* Learn how to [View prebuilt reports in Connected Sheets](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/view-reports-sheets)
* Learn how to [View prebuilt reports in Looker Studio](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/view-reports-lookerstudio)
* Learn how to [Download prebuilt reports](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/view-reports-sheets#download)

citations.title: Backup and restore job reports for vaulted backups
citations.text:
Backup and restore job reports for vaulted backups
Backup job details report

This page provides an overview of prebuilt backup and restore job reports, which
are available in BigQuery and Data Studio. These reports are
displayed for resources that are protected using [backup plans](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/cloud-console/backup-plan).

You can access these reports after you [execute the prebuilt script](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/logs-route-vault-bigquery#sink) in the
same project where the logs are being routed through the log sink.

**Note:** If you want to learn about the backup and restore job report that are protected
using the [backup template](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/create-plan/create-template)
in the appliance management console, see [Job reports](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/monitor-reports/backup-recovery-reports).

The backup job details report provides a summary of the backup jobs and includes
the following fields.

* **job\_name**: The name of the backup job.
* **resource\_name**: The name of the protected resource.
* **resource\_project\_name**: The project name of the resource.
* **job\_status**: The status of the job, which can be `SUCCESSFUL`, `FAILED`,
`RUNNING`, or `SKIPPED`.
* **error\_type**: The description of the error type. For example,
`PERMISSION_DENIED`. The error type is displayed as `Null` if no error
occurred for the job.
* **error\_code**: The error code associated for the failed job. The error code
is displayed as `Null` if no error occurred for the job.
* **error\_message**: The error message for the failed job. The error message is
displayed as `Null` if no error occurred for the job.
* **job\_start\_time**: The start time of the job, which is in the
`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS UTC` format.
* **job\_end\_time**: The end time of the job, which is in the
`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.SSS UTC` format.
* **duration**: The duration taken to complete the backup job.
* **incremental\_backup\_size\_in\_gib**: The amount of incremental backup data
copied in GiB.
* **backup\_consistency\_time**: The timestamp when the backup was successfully
taken, which is in the `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.SSSZ` format.
* **backup\_plan\_name**: The name of the backup plan that is associated to backup
the resource.
* **backup\_rule**: The name of the backup rule that triggered the backup job.
* **backup\_vault\_name**: The name of the backup vault where the backups
are stored.
* **backup\_vault\_project\_name**: The name of the backup vault project
where the backups are stored.
* **backup\_vault\_location**: The location of the backup vault where the backups
are stored.
* **resource\_location**: The location of the protected resource.
* **resource\_type**: The type of resource. For example, a Compute Engine instance.
* **resource\_id**: The resource ID associated with a job.
* **job\_category**: The category of job, which can be `SCHEDULED_BACKUP`,
`ON_DEMAND_BACKUP`, or `RESTORE`.
* **job\_id**: The ID associated with the backup job.

Backup jobs summary
The backup jobs summary report provides a daily summary of backup jobs and
includes the following fields.

* **date**: The backup job date, which is in YYYY\-MM\-DD format.
* **resource\_project\_name**: The project name of the resource.
* **job\_category**: The category of job, which can be `SCHEDULED_BACKUP` or
`ON_DEMAND_BACKUP`.
* **success\_percent**: The percentage of backup jobs that are successful.
* **total**: The total number of backup jobs that ran.
* **successful**: The total number of backup jobs succeeded.
* **failed**: The total number of backup jobs failed.
* **skipped**: The total number of backup jobs skipped.

citations.title: Generate a Client Executive Summary Report
citations.text:
Generate a Client Executive Summary Report
How to Generate a Client Executive Summary Report

1. Log in to your [x360Portal](https://partner.axcient.com/login) and open your x360Recover dashboard.  

 From the **Reports**page, select the **Executive Summary**tab.   

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/e57394905afee032.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Reports' section in Axcent x360Recover, showing the 'Executive Summary' tab selected. The form for creating an Executive Summary Report includes fields for selecting a client and specifying a report date range.
2. Select a **Client**.
3. Define the **Report Schedule**by selecting either****Generate Now****or ****Scheduled Delivery****.  

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/539d13aaa82d3119.jpg)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Create Executive Summary Report' screen in Axcient x360Recover, showing the 'Client' dropdown set to 'Casey Co' and the 'Report Schedule' options with 'Generate Now' selected. A green arrow points to the 'Client' field.

* **Generate Now**: A report will be generated immediately that can be downloaded so you can manually share results.
* **Scheduled Delivery:** A report will be scheduled on a recurring basis, so you can send it to specified recipients.  

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/2f6c04291b29b502.jpg)

> **Figure:** A section titled 'Report Schedule' with two radio button options: 'Generate Now', selected, which generates the report once for manual download; and 'Scheduled Delivery', unselected, which sends the report to recipients on a defined schedule.

3. If selected **'Generate Now',** define **Report Date Range.**
4. Specify the start date and end date for this report.  

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/004a9831ae0dc432.jpg)

> **Figure:** A form field labeled 'Report Date Range' with a required asterisk, prompting the user to specify a start and end date for a report. The date range must be at least 7 days and no more than 1 quarter. Two date input fields are shown with 'mm/dd/yyyy' placeholders, separated by 'to', with a calendar icon next to the start date field.
5. If you selected **Scheduled Delivery**, this is where you can set up the delivery frequency.
6. Define **Delivery Frequency**  

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/4f2e352eaf41fe60.jpg)

> **Figure:** A settings section labeled 'Delivery Frequency' with a dropdown set to 'Monthly' and an informational message stating the report will be sent monthly starting July 1, 2025.
7. Select your preferred delivery frequency
8. Select the desired**Level of Detail**. The level of detail can be either:
	* Summary Only or
	* Protected System Listing  

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/3a1f4c03da752b7a.jpg)

> **Figure:** A screenshot of a software dialog box titled 'Level Of Detail' for configuring report settings. It shows two radio button options: 'Summary Only', which is currently selected, and 'Protected System Listing'. A 'Preview Report' button is visible at the bottom right.
9. Click **Preview Report.**
**Note**: The report will take longer to generate for clients with large numbers of protected systems, or if a date range greater than one month is selected. 

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/109414c9128ffc20.jpg)

> **Figure:** A screenshot showing the Executive Summary Preview interface on the left, with fields for Summary Overview and Suggested Actions, and a preview of the generated Executive Summary Report on the right. The report includes metrics like Average Backup Score, Storage Growth, Protected Systems Health History, and Protected System Counts, with arrows indicating how the preview text maps to the report sections.
10. (Optional) From the Preview page, you can choose to add custom comments or instructions for your clients and select their estimated internet speed for RTO estimation.
11. If you selected **'Scheduled Delivery'**in **STEP 3**, Add **Report Recipients**
12. Add up to ten recipients by entering their emails here and clicking **Submit.**  

![undefined](/media/a04d20fe-be62-44ce-a217-9c24e0204180/65135f4aa43fd298.jpg)

> **Figure:** A form field labeled 'Report Recipients' with a text input box for adding email addresses, a 'Submit' button, and an informational message stating the report will be sent monthly starting July 1, 2025.
13. If you selected **Scheduled Delivery**in **Step 3**, remember to click the **Schedule Report** button. If you were looking to generate and download immediately, go back to **Step 3** and select **Generate Now**.

citations.title: ShadowProtect: Customer reports
citations.text:
ShadowProtect: Customer reports
Two New Methods to Launch Customer Reports

Overview
Axcient's detailed monitoring and reporting for BDR for ShadowProtect Cloud vaults includes machine\-level reports and access to detailed views from a variety of convenient locations in the Axcient portal. Email notifications are also available to proactively alert partners and customers.

Details about the Axcient BDR for ShadowProtect monitoring and reporting are found below.

Three Locations to Access Customer Reports
1\. Open the Axcient Backup Portal by navigating to <https://backup.securewebportal.net/> and logging in using your account credentials.

2\. New reports can be accessed from your choice of ****three locations**** within the Axcient Backup Portal:

![2.jpg](/media/22ab2a6c-b9c9-4acd-abc2-edaffc43b61e/e77dfa9e4d03ee52.jpg)

> **Figure:** A composite screenshot of the eFolder interface demonstrating three navigation paths: accessing the 'Dash Panel' from the Reports tab, the 'Account Center' from the Accounts tab dropdown, and the 'Account List' view within the Accounts section.

![Method1.jpg](/media/22ab2a6c-b9c9-4acd-abc2-edaffc43b61e/36db2f1467b59e73.jpg)

> **Figure:** This screenshot shows the eFolder Account Center interface, illustrating a three-step process to access account data: first, navigating to the Account Center via the Accounts tab; second, using the Actions menu to select 'Show/Hide Details' to reveal the bottom tabs; and third, locating an account in the list and clicking the graph icon within the Account Summary tab.

****NOTE:****If you do not see this “graph” icon in the Account Center or on the Dash Panel, it means this account is not currently associated with any Axcient Cloud replicated machines.

Please contact Support if you have questions about this.

****Email Notifications:****

When your account enters a warning or error state, an “event alert” will notify you that action is needed. The event alert can take the form of an email or it can be a notification pushed to a PSA.

You can configure an email notification to be sent once per day containing data from the 30\-DayTrending report and all individual Detailed Machine\-Specific Usage reports.

1\. Select the****My Account \> Notifications**** menu item. Note: If an administrative login has been used, and notification changes are needed to a specific account, the account in question must first be impersonated **before** selecting ****My Account \> Notifications****.

![Email1.png](/media/22ab2a6c-b9c9-4acd-abc2-edaffc43b61e/b0add59981a3bae3.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the eFolder software interface showing the 'My Account' menu expanded with the 'Notifications' option highlighted.

2\. Check the ****ShadowProtect Cloud Replication Notification**** checkbox.

3\. Then click ****Save Changes.****

![Email3.png](/media/22ab2a6c-b9c9-4acd-abc2-edaffc43b61e/2f66a28359e53a92.png)

> **Figure:** The image displays the 'Notifications' configuration page within a software interface, likely for a backup or cloud service. It highlights options for setting up email alerts related to ShadowProtect Cloud Replication, disk usage, and backup status, with a red box emphasizing the 'ShadowProtect Cloud Replication Notification' checkbox.

**NOTE:**These instructions apply when you are logged in as an administrator to a current account. (Be aware that when you are using an administrative login to make changes to notifications, the account in question must first be impersonated.

citations.title: Monitoring & Setting up Alerts
citations.text:
Monitoring & Setting up Alerts

**Note:** The default sender address for alerts is **\<control@hornetsecurity.com\>**. This can be modified within the CP: **\[Customization]** \> **\[Email Information]** \> **\[Sender Address for Email Templates]**  

To access the Monitoring \& Alerts tab, from the CP, launch 365 Total Backup and browse to **\[Alerts]** \> **\[Monitoring \& Alerts]**  

![](/media/de1128cd-58f8-40ce-af2a-5b2068d1856d/b45bd4807507.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Hornetsecurity 365 Total Backup Control Panel, showing the 'Alerts' section with the 'Monitoring & Alerts' option highlighted in the main content area. The left sidebar displays navigation options including Dashboard, Customers, Backup, Recovery, and Configuration & Audit.

From the **\[Monitoring]** tab, one can export 3 different types of reports through CSV or an API link. Any reports created through an API link can be monitored from **\[Manage shared API links]**.

To export a report, follow the steps below:

1. Select which type of report you wish to export  

![](/media/de1128cd-58f8-40ce-af2a-5b2068d1856d/2c59a41bce8d.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Export a report' dialog showing the 'Backup Status Report' selected from a dropdown menu. The interface includes an informational section about the report, an IP address input field for API link restrictions, and a 'Create report API Link' button.
2. Select the customer from which the data will be exported  

![](/media/de1128cd-58f8-40ce-af2a-5b2068d1856d/24b4febcb9a0.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Export a report' dialog showing options to generate a Backup Status Report. The user can select a report type, choose a customer (with 'All customers' selected and one customer option visible), and configure IP restrictions for the API link. A yellow 'Create report API Link' button is present.
3. Select whether you want to download the report as **CSV**or through an **API Link (JSON)**
4. When selecting to download the report through an API link, to enhance security, you can limit access to this API endpoint by specifying allowed IP addresses. For more information on how to use the API key, check the following [article](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/24042036274833)  

![](/media/de1128cd-58f8-40ce-af2a-5b2068d1856d/b8603ce85065.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Export a report' dialog showing options to generate a Backup Status Report. The user has selected 'Create report API Link (JSON)' and entered an IP address (10.2.185.105) in the restricted IP field for API link access.
5. Once done, select 'Generate and Download Report'  

![](/media/de1128cd-58f8-40ce-af2a-5b2068d1856d/ef901f685eda.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Export a report' dialog showing options to select a report type (Backup Status Report), choose a customer, and select a download format (CSV or JSON). The 'Generate and download report' button is highlighted.

On the other hand, the **\[Alerts]** tab is used to manage alerts and recipients. You can toggle alerts for any backup and restore operations. As well as any alerts related to new discovered items and new organisations.  

![](/media/de1128cd-58f8-40ce-af2a-5b2068d1856d/e99ca33b5c93.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Alerts' tab in the Monitoring & Alerts section, showing various alert categories including Backup operations, Data recovery, Organization alerts, and Workload alerts. Each alert has a toggle switch to enable or disable notifications, with some enabled (e.g., Backup issues, New Microsoft 365 organization onboarded) and others disabled.

To set this up, toggle the alerts that you would like to be notified for. You can then manage the recipients who will be receiving these alerts.   

![](/media/de1128cd-58f8-40ce-af2a-5b2068d1856d/e8aad9c52eb3.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Manage email alerts recipients' dialog, showing options to select or add recipients for email alerts. The 'Add contact' section includes fields for Contact Type, First Name, Last Name, and Email, with 'John Doe' and an email address entered. Two administrator recipients are selected, and no contact recipients are selected.

citations.title: Reports
citations.text:
Reports
Report templates[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#report-templates) > Creating a report template[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#creating-a-report-template)

A report template can be configured during or after its creation, using four tabs:

*   **The Report Templates tab**: Lets you define general information for the report.

*   **The Backup tab**: Used to define backup information for the report.

*   **The Restore tab**: Used to define restore information for the report.

*   **The Reports tab**: Used to schedule automatic reports.

**Step 1: Define a name for the report template**

1.  In the **Server** tab, go to **Activity Reports**.

2.  In the report templates list, click ![](/media/c4876b83-3c83-4782-9246-cf04f37037c3/80b21362fad2de13.png).

3.  Set a name for the report template. By default, the name is **New report template**.

A report template's name can be set during or after its creation.

**Step 2: Define general options for the report template**

1.  **Optional**: Include the product name in the report title.

2.  Set a language for the report template. Reports can be sent in English or French. By default, the language used is the one used for the Lina Administration Console.

3.  **Optional**: Select a retention period for generated reports.

By default, the retention period is unlimited, but you can change the retention period.

**Step 3: Define backup options for the report**

\> Enable one or more options in **Restore > Content** (Table 35).

**Table 35:** Options in the Content section

**Show storage**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#show-storage)

Displays the remaining or used space for the backup. This option is only accessible to superadministrators.

**Show performance indicators**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#show-performance-indicators)

Displays deduplication and compression rates, as well as the volume of protected and restorable data. This option is only accessible to superadministrators.

**Show activity status**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#show-activity-status)

Displays backup activity.

**Show recently backed-up agents**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#show-recently-backed-up-agents)

Displays data about agents that have been recently backed up.

**Show agents not recently backed up**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#show-agents-not-recently-backed-up)

Displays data about agents that have not been recently backed up.

**Show agents not recently connected**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#show-agents-not-recently-connected)

Displays data about agents that have not recently connected.

**Show agents never connected**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#show-agents-never-connected)

Displays data about agents that have never connected.

**Agent inactivity threshold**[](https://documentation.atempo.com/lina-7.4/lina-7.4-en/administration-guide/monitoring/statistics-and-reports#agent-inactivity-threshold)

Sets the inactivity threshold for agents that have been recently backed up or connected. This threshold is set in days.

**Step 4: Define the agent information to include in the report**

Enable one or more options in **Backup** > **Agents** tab (Table 36).

You can select/deselect all options displayed under this option. An additional column appears in the report when one of these options is selected.

citations.title: Report Browser
citations.text:
Report Browser
Data collection frequency

The reporting engine collects report data at regular intervals. The following table provides information about the type of data that the reporting engine collects and the data collection frequency.

- NOTE: Data collection only starts after the reporting engine is deployed. Events that occurred before the reporting engine is deployed are not shown in the Report Browser or reports.
- NOTE: Report data is not live and is only as up-to-date as the last successful data collection request. Therefore, reports should be used for historical purposes only.
- To view live jobs data, go to the Jobs window and then select the Protection Jobs tab.
- To view live asset data, go to Infrastructure > Assets .
- For a high-level view of the overall state of the PowerProtect Data Manager system, go to Dashboard .

Table 68. Data collection frequency

| Type of data    | Description                                                                                                                   | Data collection frequency   |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Status          | Overall status of the PowerProtect Data Manager server.                                                                       | Every 15 minutes.           |
| Configuration   | Information about assets.                                                                                                     | Every 5 minutes.            |
| Protection jobs | Information about data protection activities, including Anomaly Detection , Protect , Archive , Restore , and Replicate jobs. | Every 5 minutes.            |

Detailed report information and report timing
When you view detailed information by clicking the chart in a summary report, a new report is run and the latest data is displayed. Depending on when the two reports are run, this can result in the detailed report providing a job count that is different from the job count provided by the summary report. If the job counts are different, the job count provided by the detailed report is accurate. You can refresh the summary report page to update its information.

Report Browser options
From the Report Browser pane, click to configure options for your reports.

The following table describes the menu items for reports:

Table 69. Report options
| Menu item     | Select the menu item to:                                                               |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Edit          | Configure filters and customization options.                                           |
| Email         | Email the report to one or more recipients.                                            |
| Export        | Export the report to a CSV or PDF file.                                                |
| Save Template | Save the template of this report.                                                      |
| Schedule      | Automatically send the report to one or more email recipients on a recurring schedule. |

Emailing a report to one or more recipients
To send a report as a CSV file attachment, perform the following steps:

NOTE: SMTP must be configured before performing these actions. For more information, see Set up the email server.

1. From the Report Browser pane, select the tab of the report.
2. Click and select Email . The Email Report window opens.
3. Provide information for Report Name .
4. Provide information for To , Subject , and Body .
5. Click Send .

Checking backup status

As an administrator, you can view the status of your org’s backups at a glance and quickly drill down to find any problems— so you can resolve issues 
before they impact future restore attempts. You can also view the number of records that were 
updated, added, deleted, and undeleted for each backup. 

NOTE  You may also receive backup status information via Chatter posts to your Salesforce account and status notification emails. See [Working with notifications and alerts](SF-notifications.htm) for details.

See these topics for details:

question: We still have some IBM AIX servers. Which of these vendors can protect AIX machines?
answer:
Veeam (Veeam Backup & Replication): Protects IBM AIX computers with Veeam Agent for IBM AIX, supporting AIX 7.1–7.3 with file-level backup and restore, bare metal recovery, and recovery media creation [1].
Cohesity (DataProtect): Protects AIX servers as physical servers and Oracle databases running on AIX using the Cohesity Java Agent, installed via installp from a .bff package, with file-based protection groups [3]; also protects IBM Db2 on AIX via the db2_plugin_ctl.sh control script or native Db2 commands using the Cohesity vendor library [4].
Commvault (CommCell Console): Uses Commvault software to back up and restore AIX file systems [5].
Arcserve (Arcserve Backup, Arcserve RHA, Arcserve UDP): Arcserve Backup's agent integrates with AIX among UNIX operating systems [7]; Arcserve RHA installs an Engine daemon and xofs kernel module on AIX to track file system changes and propagate them per replication scenario [8].
Rubrik (Rubrik Security Cloud): RSC protects IBM Db2 databases running on AIX hosts with automated discovery, application-consistent backups, and point-in-time recovery, using an agent-based architecture with Rubrik Backup Service and its Vendorlib client [10][11].
Unitrends (Unitrends Unified Backup): Requires installing an AIX agent on the AIX server, which enables backup, verify, and restore of AIX server data before adding the asset to the Unitrends appliance [12].
Atempo (Tina): Supports AIX 7.2, 7.1, and 6.1 (PPC64) with Tina server, storage node, agent, and cluster components, including IBM Db2 on AIX and SAP on Oracle on AIX using BACKINT [14][15].
IBM (Storage Protect): Data Protection for Oracle can be installed on an AIX 64-bit operating system [16], and an IBM Storage Protect server can be installed on AIX with minimum hardware and software requirements [17].
Dell (NetWorker, Avamar): The NetWorker client can be installed on the AIX platform [20]; the Avamar Plug-in for Sybase and the Avamar Plug-in for DB2 can be installed, upgraded, and uninstalled on IBM AIX [21][22].
No supporting passage found for: AWS, Acronis, Afi.ai, Arctera, AvePoint, Axcient, Bacula, Barracuda, CloudAlly, CloudCasa, Datto, Druva, Eon, Flosum, GRAX, Gearset, Google, HYCU, Hornetsecurity (Altaro), Keepit, Microsoft, N-Able, Nakivo, NinjaOne (Dropsuite), Portworx, Red Hat, Salesforce, Slide, Spanning, Storware, Synology, Trilio, Velero, Zerto.

citations.title: IBM AIX Computers
citations.text:
IBM AIX Computers

A computer that you want to protect with Veeam Agent for IBM AIX must meet the following requirements:

**IBM AIX Computers**

| Specification | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | Memory: 1 GB RAM (for standard backup and restore operations) / 4 GB RAM (for bare metal recovery). Disk space: 1\.5 GB free disk space for product installation. Network: 10 Mbps or faster network connection to a backup target. |
| OS | IBM AIX 7\.1 – 7\.3 TL3 are supported. Note:* Only GA versions of the IBM AIX operating system that have been released before the Veeam Agent for IBM AIX 13\.1 are supported. * Backup of a Virtual I/O Server (VIOS) is not supported. |
| File System | All file systems supported by the supported operating systems. Consider the following:* Total size of all file systems included in a file\-level backup must not exceed 216 TiB. * Size of a file in a backup must not exceed 16 TiB. * Name of a file in a backup must not be larger than 254 bytes.  Keep in mind that characters that you can use in the file name may be encoded in 2 bytes or more.* Sparse files are not supported. Veeam Agent backs up and restores sparse files as regular files. * JFS2 snapshots are not supported. * Backup of clustered systems (including IBM PowerHA SystemMirror) is not supported. * Veeam Agent supports backup and restore of NFSv4 Access Control Lists (ACLs). For more information, see [Backup of ACLs](agents_backup_unix_acl.html). |
| Software | IMPORTANT! The user account used to work with Veeam Agent for IBM AIX installed on the protected computer must have the /bin/bash shell set as the default shell. The following utilities must be installed on the machine:* mlocate — required for file system indexing. You must use the mlocate utility that is provided with Veeam Agent in the product installation media.  If you upgrade to Veeam Agent for IBM AIX version 12\.1 and you have the mlocate utility provided with one of the previous versions of Veeam Agent for IBM AIX installed in your system, you must replace the existing mlocate utility with the mlocate utility provided with Veeam Agent in the product installation media.* tar — required for file system indexing, exporting and rotating logs. It is installed with the product. * gzip — required for file system indexing, exporting and rotating logs. It must be installed separately. * mkisofs — required for creating Veeam recovery Media.  \[For IBM AIX 7\.3, 7\.2 and 7\.1 TL1 or higher] This utility is pre\-installed in the OS and does not require separate installation. \[For IBM AIX 7\.1 TL0] You must install version 1\.13 of the mkisofs utility.* \[For IBM AIX 7\.1] bos.rte.libc version 7\.1\.5\.0 or later must be installed. |

citations.title: Install and Manage the Cohesity Java Agent on AIX Servers
citations.text:
Install and Manage the Cohesity Java Agent on AIX Servers
Install and Manage the Cohesity Java Agent on AIX Servers

You can install the Cohesity Java Agent on AIX server to protect:

- l AIX server as a physical server
- l Oracle database running on AIX server

Prerequisites
Ensure that the AIX physical server meets the following requirements:

- l To use the AIX agent (Java based), Java Runtime Environment (JRE) 8 needs to be installed on the source system.
- l AIX agent (Java based) being installed should be a higher version than the existing version of GoAgent.
- l Install 64-bit version 8 of IBM-supported AIX compatible Java.
- l 1.5 GB of free RAM (at run time) to account for JRE overhead.
- l Sudo package must be installed.
- l Latest version of Bash must be installed. For more information, see AIX Toolbox for Linux Applications.
- l Java version for the Agent must be JRE 1.8.0 AIX ppc-64 bit.

Considerations
- l Only file-based Protection Groups are supported.
- l IVM (Instant Volume Mount) is not supported.
- l Cohesity does not support source-side deduplication of AIX server.
- l AIX clustering is not supported.

Install the Cohesity Java Agent
For information on supported AIX versions on Cohesity cluster, see Supported Software.

To install the Cohesity Java agent:
You can download the Cohesity agent installer from the Cohesity UI or manually download the agent from the Cohesity Package Download and install the agent using CLI.

1. Download the installer:
2. a.
3. Using the Cohesity cluster UI Navigate to Data Protection > Sources and click Download Cohesity Agent .
- b. Using the Cohesity Package Download site
5. Download the Cohesity Java Agent package (a .bff file) from Cohesity Package Download. Ensure the Java Agent is on the AIX server you want to protect.
2. To Install the Custom certificates, follow the below steps:

echo ENFORCE\_USE\_CUSTOM\_CERTS=true >> /usr/local/cohesity/set\_env.sh

If you are using a Cohesity certificate then run the following commands to install the user certificate:

echo AGENT\_CERT\_FILE=<path-to-agent-certificate-in-Cohesity-format> >> /usr/local/cohesity/set\_env.sh

Note:
- l ENFORCE\_USE\_CUSTOM\_CERTS, if this parameter is set to true, then the agent will try to load the specified certificate and fail to start in case of an invalid file or files.
- l AGENT\_CERT\_FILE specifies the path to the agent certificate file in the Cohesity format
3. Install the package:

Log in to the AIX server as a root user and run the following command to install the package:

installp -ad <path\_to\_downloaded\_agent\_package> all

For example:
installp -ad cohesity\_agent\_6.6\_aix\_java.bff all

The Cohesity Java Agent starts automatically. Now you can register the server with the Cohesity cluster. Reboot is not required. The Cohesity Java Agent starts after any future reboots.

Prerequisites
Before you install the AIX Java agent on the server, make sure the following software is installed on the server:

- l The latest Bash package. For more information, see AIX Toolbox for Linux Applications.
- l Java version, JRE 1.8.0 AIX ppc-64 bit for the agent.

Note: Before installing the AIX Java agent, Cohesity recommends logging in to SQL Plus and RMAN using appropriate credentials (OS Auth or User Based). If the login is successful, proceed with the installation. If not, obtain the required user credentials and verify that you can log in.

Considerations
The mount point used for Oracle DB cloning is not persistent across reboots. To resolve this issue, manually update the /etc/filesystem file using any editor and update the mount path information.

To install the Cohesity Java agent on Oracle AIX sever:
You can upgrade the Cohesity agent installer from the Cohesity UI or manually download the agent from the Cohesity Package Download and install the agent using CLI.

1. Follow steps 1 and 2 from Install the Cohesity Java Agent section to download the agent and install Custom certificates.
2. 2.
3. Install the package:

Log in to the AIX server as an Oracle ROOT user and run the following command to install the package.

sudo install\_with\_oracle\_adapter\_support=true installp -ad <path\_to\_ downloaded\_agent\_package> all

citations.title: Installing and updating the AIX agent
citations.text:
Installing and updating the AIX agent

Before adding an AIX asset to the Unitrends appliance, you must install an agent. 

Once the agent is installed, you can update to a newer agent version using these same installation procedures. It is not necessary to remove the old agent. If an agent is already installed, you have the option to save any custom agent settings during installation.

Use the procedures in this section to install or update the AIX agent.

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)Preparing to install the AIX agent](#)

The AIX agent enables you to back up, verify, and restore AIX server data. The AIX agent cannot be used to protect encrypted file systems.

Before installing an AIX agent:

●   Make sure your AIX system is running a supported version listed in the [Unitrends Compatibility and Interoperability Matrix.](https://www.unitrends.com/products/backup-and-disaster-recovery/compatibility-matrix)

●   Add the name and IP address of the Unitrends appliance to the hosts file on the AIX server.

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)To install the AIX agent](#)

 1\.  Log in to the AIX machine as user root.

 2\.  Download the AIX agent from the Unitrends Downloads page ([https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en\-gb/articles/4407526882193\-Unitrends\-Downloads](https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4407526882193-Unitrends-Downloads)) into the /tmp folder on the AIX machine. 

 3\.  Execute the following commands to begin the installation:

\# **chmod 755 /tmp/aix5\_cnt**

\# **/tmp/aix5\_cnt**

 4\.  Follow the steps on the screen. You will be asked to specify the directory location where the agent will be installed. If this is a reinstall, you will be asked if you wish to overwrite certain files. Type the interrupt character or press return to continue. The files will be moved to their permanent location.

 5\.  When the configuration process finishes, you will be prompted to reboot the AIX machine to complete the installation.

Once you have installed the agent, you are ready to add your AIX asset to the Unitrends appliance. For details, see [To add an agent\-based asset](Managing_protected_assets.htm#To_add_an_asset).

question: I need to run my own scripts right before and after each backup, for example to quiesce an application. Which products support custom pre- and post-backup scripts?
answer:
Dell (PowerProtect Data Manager): supports user-created pre-scripts and post-scripts that run before and after a centralized backup or snapshot on an agent host, across File System, Microsoft application, Oracle RMAN, SAP HANA, Generic application agents, and PowerMax/PowerStore storage arrays [1][2].
Slide (Slide): the Linux agent runs quiescence scripts placed in /etc/slide/agent/quiescence.d/ immediately before and after the volume snapshot, with each script handling PRE and POST phases to produce application-consistent backups [3].
Veeam (Veeam Backup & Replication): Veeam Agent for Linux supports pre-job/post-job scripts and pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts (Server edition) run before and after snapshot creation, and Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows supports pre-freeze/post-thaw scripts on the agent computer plus pre-job/post-job scripts on the backup server [5][6].
Druva (Druva): administrators can configure File server agents with custom pre-backup and post-backup scripts in the backup policy, and NAS backups support pre/post-backup scripts on Windows and Linux proxies configured in the Phoenix Management Console [7][8].
Microsoft (Azure Backup): Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS) runs pre-backup and post-backup scripts on the protected computer, specified per data source in the ScriptingConfig.xml file, executed with the local system account [9][10].
Red Hat (OADP): OADP lets you create backup hooks in the Backup custom resource to run commands in a pod container before (Pre hooks) and after (Post hooks) the backup, for example to quiesce a database or flush data to disk [11][12].
Commvault (Commvault Cloud): pre-process and post-process scripts run automatically before or after backup operations for file servers (CIFS/NFS/NAS) and databases (DB2, Informix, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SAP HANA, SQL Server), configured at the subclient level, with pre-restore and post-restore scripts for database restores [13][14].
Bacula (Bacula): the Libvirt plugin can execute custom quiesce and unquiesce scripts on guest machines before and after backing up a virtual machine, and Director Job resources support Run Before Job, Run After Job, Client Run Before Job, and Client Run After Job directives [15][16].
Rubrik (Rubrik Security Cloud): RSC allows configuring the Rubrik cluster to run pre-backup, post-snap, and post-backup scripts on a guest OS before a snapshot, after the snapshot, and after the backup process completes, using guest OS credentials [17][18].
Barracuda (Barracuda Backup): the Barracuda Backup Agent runs pre- or post-Agent backup commands by editing the config.ini file with preExecuteScript and postExecuteScript entries, using .bat scripts on Windows and .sh scripts on Linux [21][22].
Velero (Velero): Velero supports executing pre and post hook commands in containers in pods during a backup, specified via pod annotations or in the Backup spec [25][26].
Arcserve (Arcserve UDP): Arcserve UDP lets you create pre/post scripts placed in the prepost folder and select them in the Backup or Restore Wizard, with scripts running at stages such as pre-job-server, post-job-server, pre-snapshot, and post-snapshot [27][28].
N-Able (Cove Data Protection): Backup Manager lets you add scripts in the Scripts tab and apply them as pre-backup or post-backup scripts in the backup schedule settings, with options for username, timeout, and failing the backup on error [29][30].
Trilio (Trilio for Kubernetes): Trilio Vault Hooks inject pre and post commands into pods/containers before and after a backup via Hook CRDs referenced in BackupPlans, enabling application-consistent backups for databases like MySQL, MariaDB, Cassandra, MongoDB, Redis, and PostgreSQL [31][32].
CloudCasa (CloudCasa): App Hooks execute pre-backup, post-backup, and post-restore commands in specified containers on your cluster, selectable from templates or custom definitions and enabled in the cluster backup wizard [33][34].
Portworx (PX-Backup): PX-Backup supports pre-exec and post-exec rules—database-dependent scripts executed on containers before or after the backup operation to freeze or unfreeze application I/O—selected in the backup or scheduled backup definition [35][36].
Arctera (Backup Exec): Backup Exec lets you configure pre-commands and post-commands that run before and after backup and restore jobs, with options to run the job only if the pre-command succeeds, run the post-command even if the job fails, and check exit codes [37][38].
Unitrends (Unitrends Unified Backup): you can specify a Command to run Pre-Backup and a Command to run Post-Backup on the asset for scheduled jobs, using bp_cmd_pre_backup and bp_cmd_post_backup scripts (.bat/.cmd on Windows, .sh on Linux) [39][40].
Datto (BCDR): Datto Linux agents support quiescing scripts (including MongoDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and custom scripts) stored in /etc/datto/dla/pps/ that handle PRE and POST operations, activated per agent in the appliance GUI, and Datto Endpoint Backup with Disaster Recovery supports quiescing scripts for Linux agents enabled per volume in the Partner Portal [41][42].
HYCU (R-Cloud Hybrid Cloud Edition): HYCU lets you specify pre/post-backup and pre/post-snapshot scripts per virtual machine in the Virtual Machines panel, with scripts returning exit codes and environment variables exported during execution [43][44].
Atempo (Tina): Tina supports pre-freeze and post-thaw scripts for VMware backups, looked up in defined Windows and Linux locations and executed with freeze/thaw arguments for consistent snapshots [45].
IBM (Storage Defender): IBM Storage Defender Copy Data Management supports job-level pre-scripts and post-scripts that run before or after a job, selected or uploaded in the job definition with parameters, credentials, and an application server target [47][48].
Synology (Active Backup): Synology Active Backup for Business supports an Enable pre/post script option to execute selected scripts (.bat on Windows, .sh on Linux, under 32 KB) before and after taking snapshots of the device [49][50].
Nakivo (Nakivo Backup & Replication): Nakivo supports running local pre-job and post-job scripts in the Tape Backup Wizard and Backup Copy Job Wizard, with options to wait for the script to finish and to continue or fail the job on script failure [51][52].
Cohesity (DataProtect): Cohesity supports configuring pre-scripts and post-scripts for protection runs, with script paths or names, optional parameters and timeout, and post-scripts running even if the backup fails [53][54].
Storware (Backup and Recovery): Storware Backup & Recovery supports pre/post snapshot command execution via SSH or WinRM before or after taking a snapshot, configured per VM instance in the Settings tab [55][56].
Zerto (Zerto): Zerto lets you run PowerShell Core pre-recovery and post-recovery scripts before and after failover, move, or test failover operations, managed and uploaded on the ZVM Appliance [59][60].
No supporting passage found for: AWS, Acronis, Afi.ai, AvePoint, Axcient, CloudAlly, Eon, Flosum, GRAX, Gearset, Google, Hornetsecurity (Altaro), Keepit, NinjaOne (Dropsuite), Salesforce, Spanning.

citations.title: Enable the use of pre-scripts and post-scripts with backups
citations.text:
Enable the use of pre-scripts and post-scripts with backups
Enable the use of pre-scripts and post-scripts with backups

PowerProtect Data Manager supports the running of user-created scripts before and after a centralized backup on an agent host. You can optionally create a pre-script that runs before a backup or snapshot, or a post-script that runs after a backup or snapshot. These pre-scripts and post-scripts can perform various functions that extend the capabilities of the backup process.

- NOTE: For PowerMax and PowerStore assets, a pre-script or post-script runs only once, regardless of the number of assets on the host. Also, the post-script runs regardless of whether the pre-script runs successfully. This behavior ensures that the application returns to a consistent state, even if the pre-script or backup is unsuccessful.

PowerProtect Data Manager supports the use of pre-scripts and post-scripts with backups or snapshots of the assets or databases of the following agents or sources:

- File System agent on AIX, Linux, or Windows
- Microsoft application agent on Windows
- Oracle RMAN application agent on AIX, Linux, or Windows
- SAP HANA application agent on Linux
- Generic application agent on Linux
- Storage arrays (PowerMax and PowerStore)

E-Lab Navigator provides details on the latest platform support for the agents.

For example, you can create a pre-script that stops a database, stops services, deletes unwanted files, or changes permissions before a backup begins to run. You can also create a post-script that starts a database, starts services, or applies transaction logs after a backup or snapshot completes. For application agents, you can specify that a pre-script runs before a specific backup or a post-script runs after a specific backup, or that both scripts run before and after the same backup.

Each script file name must be unique. The name must end with .sh on Linux or UNIX and .bat on Windows. On Windows, a double extension is not supported, as in the script name myscript.bat.exe . It is recommended that you include the type of script within the script name. For example:

- Pre-script name: ppdm\_pre\_backup.sh or ppdm\_pre\_backup.bat
- Post-script name: ppdm\_post\_backup.sh or ppdm\_post\_backup.bat

For example, with the Oracle RMAN agent on AIX or Linux, you must use an Oracle script name that ends with .sh.

citations.title: Slide Linux Agent
citations.text:
Slide Linux Agent
Slide Linux Agent[¶](#slide-linux-agent "Permanent link") > Application\-Consistent Backups[¶](#application-consistent-backups "Permanent link")

 Quiescence scripts allow applications to participate in the backup process, producing application\-consistent backups. When configured, the agent runs your scripts immediately before and after the volume snapshot is taken, giving applications the opportunity to flush pending writes and reach a consistent state before the snapshot is captured.

Setting up quiescence scripts[¶](#setting-up-quiescence-scripts "Permanent link")
 Place your script in `/etc/slide/agent/quiescence.d/`. For the agent to recognize and run it, the script must meet all of the following conditions:

 * Be a regular file (not a symlink or directory)
* Be owned by `root`
* Have permissions set to exactly `0700`

  Warning

 Scripts that do not meet these conditions are silently skipped. After placing a script in the directory, verify its ownership and permissions:

```
[root@linuxbox] ls -l /etc/slide/agent/quiescence.d/
-rwx------ 1 root ... 10-postgresql.sh
-rwx------ 1 root ... 20-mariadb.sh

```

Script interface[¶](#script-interface "Permanent link")
 The agent calls each script twice per backup and passes the phase as the first argument (`$1`):

 * `PRE` — runs before the snapshot is taken. Quiesce your application here (for example, flush pending writes or pause I/O).
* `POST` — runs after the snapshot completes. Resume your application here.

 Write a single script that handles both phases by branching on the first argument:

```
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

case "$1" in
  PRE)
    # Quiesce your application here (e.g. flush pending writes, pause I/O)
    ;;
  POST)
    # Resume your application here
    ;;
esac

```
 Keep each invocation under 30 seconds. If a script does not finish within this timeout, the agent kills it and all of its child processes.

Execution order[¶](#execution-order "Permanent link")
 Scripts run in lexicographic filename order during the `PRE` phase. Successfully executed scripts run in reverse order during the `POST` phase. Use a numeric prefix to control the order when multiple scripts must run in a specific sequence.

```
/etc/slide/agent/quiescence.d/
├── 01-database
└── 02-application

```
 In this example, `01-database` runs PRE first, followed by `02-application`. On POST, assuming both scripts successfully executed, the order is reversed: `02-application` runs first, then `01-database`.

Error handling[¶](#error-handling "Permanent link")
 If a script's `PRE` invocation fails, the agent immediately calls that script's `POST` phase as a rollback, then continues with any remaining scripts. The backup still proceeds regardless of quiescence script failures.

Console visibility[¶](#console-visibility "Permanent link")
 An agent's quiescence scripts appear in the agent's details page after its next check\-in.

Example scripts[¶](#example-scripts "Permanent link")
 See [Quiescence Script Examples: PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, and SQLite](../guides/quiescence-script-examples/) for ready\-to\-adapt scripts covering these databases.

citations.title: Backup Job Scripts
citations.text:
Backup Job Scripts

You can instruct Veeam Agent for Linux to run custom scripts within the backup job session:

* [Pre\-job and post\-job scripts](#job) — Veeam Agent runs these scripts before the backup job starts and after the backup job completes. You can use pre\-job and post\-job scripts, for example, to configure email notifications about jobs performed by Veeam Agent.
* [Pre\-freeze and post\-thaw scripts](#snapshot) (in the Server edition only) — Veeam Agent runs these scripts before and after creating a snapshot. For example, the pre\-freeze script may quiesce the file system and application data to bring the Linux OS to a consistent state before Veeam Agent creates a snapshot. After the snapshot is created, the post\-thaw script may bring the file system and applications to their initial state.

Consider the following about using backup job scripts:

* Scripts must be created beforehand. You must specify paths to them in the job settings. Veeam Agent supports scripts in the SH file format.
* Scripts must have UNIX line endings (LF).
* Script settings are enabled at the job level. If Veeam Agent operates in the Server edition and you want to configure multiple backup jobs, you can specify individual scripts for each job.

* Scripts are executed under the root user account.
* The script is considered to be executed successfully if a "0" is returned.
* If you use relative paths in your scripts, during script execution such paths will refer to the root directory. For example, the script may have an output that must be saved to a new file. If you specify a relative path to that file or only a file name, the file will be created in the root directory. To specify a different location for a file, use a full absolute path.

Pre\-Job and Post\-Job Scripts

You can instruct Veeam Agent for Linux to run custom pre\-job and post\-job scripts. Veeam Agent executes the pre\-job script directly before the backup job starts. After the backup job completes, Veeam Agent executes the post\-job script.

Veeam Agent starts the backup job regardless of the pre\-job script result. If the pre\-job script fails to execute, Veeam Agent will always start the backup job. Then, after the backup job completes, Veeam Agent will execute the post\-job script. 

The default time period for script execution is 10 minutes. After this period expires, Veeam Agent stops executing the script and displays a warning message in the job session. You can change the script timeouts in the /etc/veeam/veeam.ini configuration file with the timeoutPrePost parameter where the time period is set in seconds.

Pre\-Freeze and Post\-Thaw Scripts

You can instruct Veeam Agent for Linux to run custom pre\-freeze and post\-thaw scripts. Veeam Agent executes the pre\-freeze script before creating a snapshot. After the snapshot is created, Veeam Agent executes the post\-thaw script.

| NOTE |
| --- |
| Veeam Agent does not execute pre\-freeze and post\-freeze scripts if during the backup job a snapshot is not created. |

By default, if the pre\-freeze or post\-thaw script fails to execute, Veeam Agent does not start the backup job. However, you can instruct Veeam Agent to ignore errors that occur during the script execution process. To allow Veeam Agent to start backup jobs regardless of the script execution result, in the /etc/veeam/veeam.ini configuration file, uncomment the ignoreFreezeThawFailures parameter and set its value to true.

If Veeam Agent is set up to ignore script errors, and the pre\-freeze or post\-thaw script fails to execute, Veeam Agent will start the backup job. After the job successfully completes, Veeam Agent will display the Warning status for the job session.

The default time period for script execution is 10 minutes. After this period expires, Veeam Agent stops executing the script. You can change the script timeouts in the /etc/veeam/veeam.ini configuration file with the timeoutFreezeThaw parameter where the time period is set in seconds.

| NOTE |
| --- |
| You can specify pre\-freeze and post\-thaw scripts only if Veeam Agent for Linux operates in the Server edition. If these scripts were enabled for the job while Veeam Agent operated in the Server edition, and then Veeam Agent has switched to another edition (for example, to the Free edition after the license has expired), the backup job will fail. You will need to delete the existing job and create a new backup job without pre\-freeze and post\-thaw scripts enabled. |

citations.title: Backup Job and Snapshot Scripts
citations.text:
Backup Job and Snapshot Scripts

You can instruct Veeam Agent to run custom scripts within the backup job session. Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows supports the following types of scripts:

* [Pre\-freeze and post\-thaw scripts executed on the Veeam Agent computer](#snapshot)
* [Pre\-job and post\-job scripts executed on the Veeam backup server](#job_server) (for backup jobs managed by the backup server)

Considerations and Limitations

* Scripts must be created before you configure the backup job. You must specify paths to them in the backup job settings.

If you use Veeam Backup \& Replication on Linux, you must place the scripts into the /var/lib/veeam/scripts/ directory on the backup server.

If you use Veeam Backup \& Replication on Windows, you can place the script files in any local folder on the backup server.

* Veeam Agent supports scripts in the .EXE, .BAT,.CMD and .PS1 formats.
* Scripts must have Windows line endings (CRLF).
* Script settings are enabled at the backup job level. If you want to configure multiple backup jobs, you can specify individual scripts for each job.
* If you use relative paths in your scripts, during script execution such paths will refer to the root directory. For example, the script may have an output that must be saved to a new file. If you specify a relative path to that file or only a file name, the file will be created in the root directory. To specify a different location for a file, use a full absolute path.

Pre\-Freeze and Post\-Thaw Scripts

Veeam Agent runs these scripts before and after creating a snapshot of the backed\-up volume. For example, the pre\-freeze script may quiesce the file system and application data to bring the OS to a consistent state before Veeam Agent creates a snapshot. After the snapshot is created, the post\-thaw script brings the file system and applications to their initial state.

You can specify pre\-freeze and post\-thaw script settings at the Guest Processing step of a backup job wizard. To learn more, see sections [Pre\-Freeze and Post\-Thaw Script Settings](agent_job_vss_scripts.html) (for backup jobs managed by the backup server) and [Pre\-Freeze and Post\-Thaw Script Settings](agent_policy_win_vss_scripts.html) (for backup policies).

Veeam Backup \& Replication uploads the scripts to each Veeam Agent computer added to the backup job and executes them on these computers. The scripts run in the same way as in the standalone version of Veeam Agent. To learn more, see the [Backup Job Scripts](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/agentforwindows/userguide/pre_post_scripts.html?ver=13) section in the Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows User Guide.

Pre\-Job and Post\-Job Scripts

Veeam Agent runs these scripts before the backup job starts and after the backup job completes. You can use pre\-job and post\-job scripts, for example, to throttle activities of some resource\-consuming services on the backup server during the backup process.

You can specify backup job script settings at the Storage step of the backup job wizard. To learn more, see [Script Settings](agent_job_advanced_scripts.html).

Veeam Backup \& Replication executes the scripts on the backup server under the account under which the Veeam Backup Service runs (the local System account or account that has the local Administrator permissions on the backup server).

Script Execution Order

If you specify both pre\-job and post\-job and pre\-freeze and post\-thaw scripts, the scripts will be executed in the following order:

1. Pre\-job script
2. Pre\-freeze script
3. Post\-thaw script
4. Post\-job script

citations.title: Pre-backup and post-backup scripts for File server
citations.text:
Pre-backup and post-backup scripts for File server
Considerations

Overview
Druva allows administrators to configure File server agents to execute custom pre\-backup scripts and post\-backup scripts. Pre\-backup scripts are executed before backup jobs to perform specific pre\-backup operation. Post\-backup scripts are executed after backup jobs to perform specific post\-backup operation. You can configure backup policy with the settings for pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts to perform customer\-driven processing tasks. For example,

* To backup database dumps as flat files using the Druva File server agent and delete the dump files after the Druva backup job completes.
* To stop an antivirus service before the backup job and restarting the service after backup completes.

Configuring pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts in File server backup policy is optional. Before configuring the pre\-backup script and post\-backup script settings, you should consider the following information:

* The pre\-backup scripts and the post\-backup scripts must be present on the same File server, which is configured with Druva for backup.
* You can configure the pre\-backup scripts and the post\-backup scripts only for Windows and Linux File servers supported by Druva.
* The pre\-backup scripts and post\-backup scripts should be executable files. Ensure that the scripts are created as per the following conventions:

	+ For Linux File server, save the scripts as `pre_script.sh` and `post_script.sh.`
	+ For Windows File server, save the scripts as `pre_script.bat` and `post_script.bat`.
* If the pre\-backup script or post\-backup script execution fails, alert and email will be generated for the respective script failure at the end of the last retried job.
* When the pre\-backup or post\-backup script is killed externally, for example, through Task Manager or command line ( `kill -9 <pid>` ), then the backup cycle gets executed after the context of the script exits.
* If the script execution time limit is not specified, the pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts run until the script execution is complete or 1 year, whichever is less.

Steps to configure pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts
The following diagram depicts the steps to configure pre\-backup scripts and post\-backup scripts.

> **Figure:** This diagram illustrates a three-step workflow for configuring and executing custom pre- and post-backup scripts for a File Server using Druva. The steps include creating the script files on the server, configuring the backup policy in the Druva portal with settings like script location and timeout, and finally executing the backup job.

citations.text:
Pre-backup and post-backup scripts for NAS
Steps to configure pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts

The following diagram depicts the steps to configure pre and post\-backup scripts.

[

![Configure NAS pre post scripts.png](/media/69aba438-00b5-4a38-b95c-5f5ba5435e0c/d9b717b6b451e0dc.png)

> **Figure:** This diagram illustrates a three-step workflow for configuring NAS pre- and post-backup scripts. It shows the process of creating NFS or SMB scripts on a NAS Proxy, defining backup policy settings (enable/disable, location, timeout) in the Phoenix Management Console, and finally running the backup.

](/media/69aba438-00b5-4a38-b95c-5f5ba5435e0c/d9b717b6b451e0dc.png)1. Create pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts on the NAS proxy.

	* Script to backup NFS shares: `pre_script.sh` and `post_script.sh`
	* Script to backup SMB shares: `pre_script.bat` and `post_script.bat`  
	​
2. Create a new backup policy or edit an existing one and perform the following tasks:  
​

[

![Pre-post script settings.png](/media/69aba438-00b5-4a38-b95c-5f5ba5435e0c/bfde1223b42e0c38.png)

> **Figure:** The screenshot shows the 'Pre/Post Script Settings' tab of a 'New Backup Policy' wizard. It allows users to configure script execution for Windows and Linux proxies, including enabling scripts, specifying locations, setting conditions to skip backups, and defining an abort timeout.

](/media/69aba438-00b5-4a38-b95c-5f5ba5435e0c/bfde1223b42e0c38.png)

	* **WINDOWS PROXY**

		+ **Enable Scripts**:Enable pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts execution for SMB share backups. When you enable scripts, the **Scripts location** field gets enabled.
		+ **Scripts Location**:Enter the location of the folder that contains the pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts on the NAS proxy.
	* **LINUX PROXY**

		+ **Enable Scripts**:Enable pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts for NFS share backups.When you enable scripts, the **Scripts location** field gets enabled.
		+ **Scripts Location**:Enter the location of the folder that contains the pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts on the NAS proxy.
	* **SKIP BACKUP IF**

		+ **Pre\-script is not present at the specified location**:Select the option to skip the backup if a pre\-backup script is not available at the specified script location.
		+ **Pre\-script execution fails**:Select the option to skip the backup if a pre\-backup script execution fails.
		+ **Abort pre/post script execution if it does not complete in X Minutes/Hours**:Enter the duration in minutes or hours after which Druva should abort the pre\-backup or post\-backup script execution. You can leave this field blank if you don’t want to enter a timeout value. In that case the pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts run until the script execution is complete or one year, whichever is lesser.  
		​
3. The NAS agent executes the pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts from the path specified in the backup policy. When the pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts are executed, the agent passes a set of arguments to these scripts. These arguments are interpreted in the following sequence:

	1. For pre\_backup script: \[ `script_name`, `job_id` ]
	2. For post\_backup script: \[ `script_name`, `job_id`, `pre_script_status_integer`, `backup_status_integer` ]  
	where,

		* `script_name` represents the absolute path of script.
		* `job_id` represents the job identification number of the current backup job.
		* `pre_script_status_integer` represents the status of the pre\-script execution. To interpret the values of the pre\-script status integers, see [Pre\-script status](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651526-nas-jobs-page).
		* `backup_status_integer` represents the status of the backup job execution. To interpret the values of the backup status integers, see [Backup status](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651526-nas-jobs-page).

Workflow of backup job execution with custom scripts
To run pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts during the backup job execution, you must configure them in the NAS backup policy.The following diagram depicts the life cycle of the backup job when the pre\-backup scripts and post\-backup scripts are disabled and enabled.

citations.title: Using pre-backup and post-backup scripts
citations.text:
Using pre-backup and post-backup scripts
Use pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts

Applies to: Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS)

A *pre\-backup script* is a script that resides on the protected computer, is executed before each MABS backup job, and prepares the protected data source for backup.

A *post\-backup script* is a script that runs after a MABS backup job to do any post\-backup processing, such as bringing a virtual machine back online.

When you install a protection agent on a computer, a ScriptingConfig.xml file is added to the *install path* \\Microsoft Data Protection Manager\\DPM\\Scripting folder on the protected computer. For each protected data source on the computer, you can specify a pre\-backup script and a post\-backup script in ScriptingConfig.xml.

Note

The pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts can’t be VBScripts. Instead, you must use a wrapper command around your script containing **cscript myscript.vbs**.

When MABS runs a protection job, ScriptingConfig.xml on the protected computer is checked. If a pre\-backup script is specified, MABS runs the script and then completes the job. If a post\-backup script is specified, MABS completes the job and then runs the script.

Note

Protection jobs include replica creation, express full backup, synchronization, and consistency check.

MABS runs the pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts by using the local system account. As a best practice, you should ensure that the scripts have Read and Execute permissions for the administrator and local system accounts only. This level of permissions prevents unauthorized users to modify the scripts.

**ScriptingConfig.xml**

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<ScriptConfiguration xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" 
xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" 
xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/2003/dls/ScriptingConfig.xsd">
   <DatasourceScriptConfig DataSourceName="Data source">
     <PreBackupScript>”Path\Script Parameters” </PreBackupScript>
     <PostBackupScript>"Path\Script Parameters” </PostBackupScript>
     <TimeOut>30</TimeOut>
   </DatasourceScriptConfig>
</ScriptConfiguration>

```

citations.title: Using pre-backup and post-backup scripts
citations.text:
Using pre-backup and post-backup scripts
Use pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts > Specify pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts

To specify pre\-backup and post\-backup scripts, follow these steps:

1. On the protected computer, open the ScriptingConfig.xml file with an XML or text editor.

Note

The DataSourceName attribute must be provided as **Drive:** (for example, D: if the data source is on the D drive).
2. For each data source, complete the DatasourceScriptConfig element as follows:

	1. For the DataSourceName attribute, enter the data source volume (for file data sources) or name (for all other data sources). The data source name for application data should be in the form of *Instance\\Database* for SQL, *Storage group name* for Exchange, *Logical Path\\Component Name* for Virtual Server, and *SharePoint Farm\\SQL Server Name\\SQL Instance Name\\SharePoint Config DB* for Windows SharePoint Services.
	2. In the *PreBackupScript* tag, enter the path and script name.
	3. In the *PreBackupCommandLine* tag, enter command\-line parameters to be passed to the scripts, separated by spaces.
	4. In the *PostBackupScript* tag, enter the path and script name.
	5. In the *PostBackupCommandLine* tag, enter command\-line parameters to be passed to the scripts, separated by spaces.
	6. In the `TimeOut` tag, enter the amount of time in minutes that MABS should wait after invoking a script before timing out and marking the script as failed.
3. Save the ScriptingConfig.xml file.

Note

MABS will suffix an additional Boolean (true/false) parameter to the post\-backup script command, indicating the status of the MABS backup job.

citations.title: OADP Application backup and restore
citations.text:
OADP Application backup and restore
Chapter 5\. OADP Application backup and restore > [5\.18\. OADP backing up](#oadp-backing-up) > [5\.18\.7\. Creating backup hooks](#oadp-creating-backup-hooks-doc)

 Create backup hooks to run commands in a container in a pod by editing the `Backup` custom resource (CR). This helps you to run pre\-backup and post\-backup actions such as quiescing a database or flushing data to disk.

 The commands can be configured to performed before any custom action processing (*Pre* hooks), or after all custom actions have been completed and any additional items specified by the custom action have been backed up (*Post* hooks).

**Procedure**

* Add a hook to the `spec.hooks` block of the `Backup` CR, as in the following example:

```
apiVersion: velero.io/v1
kind: Backup
metadata:
  name: <backup>
  namespace: openshift-adp
spec:
  hooks:
    resources:
      - name: <hook_name>
        includedNamespaces:
        - <namespace>
        excludedNamespaces:
        - <namespace>
        includedResources: []
        - pods
        excludedResources: []
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: velero
            component: server
        pre:
          - exec:
              container: <container>
              command:
              - /bin/uname
              - -a
              onError: Fail
              timeout: 30s
        post:
...
```

 where:

`<namespace>`
 Optional: Specifies the namespaces to which the hook applies. If this value is not specified, the hook applies to all namespaces.
 `excludedNamespaces`
 Optional: Specifies the namespaces to which the hook does not apply.
 `pods`
 Currently, pods are the only supported resource that hooks can apply to.
 `excludedResources`
 Optional: Specifies the resources to which the hook does not apply.
 `labelSelector`
 Optional: This hook only applies to objects matching the label. If this value is not specified, the hook applies to all objects.
 `pre`
 Specifies an array of hooks to run before the backup.
 `<container>`
 Optional: Specifies the container in which the command runs. If the container is not specified, the command runs in the first container in the pod.
 `/bin/uname`
 Specifies the entry point for the `init` container being added.
 `onError: Fail`
 Specifies the error handling behavior. Allowed values are `Fail` and `Continue`. The default is `Fail`.
 `timeout: 30s`
 Optional: Specifies how long to wait for the commands to run. The default is `30s`.
 `post`
 Specifies an array of hooks to run after the backup, with the same parameters as the pre\-backup hooks.
