​

**Additional check:**  
​

On the backup proxy, verify the configuration file located at:  
​

`/etc/Druva/EnterpriseWorkloads/openstack/OpenStackConfig.yaml`  
​

Ensure that the `client_id` parameter is correctly configured and not equal to 0\.  
​

If the value is 0, you must rerun the command to refresh the proxy credentials. For more information, see [Activate and set credentials](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/16538883).  
​

OPENSTACK 1004
**Error Message:** Source instance not found.  
​

**Error Description:** This error occurs when the source instance has been deleted in OpenStack.  
​

**Error Resolution:** If a virtual machine configured for backup is deleted from the OpenStack environment, the subsequent backup job will fail. Remove the instance from the backup configuration to prevent further errors.  
​

OPENSTACK 1005
**Error Message:** Snapshot creation failed.  
​

**Error Description:** Occurs when creation of the instance image or Cinder snapshot fails.  
​

**Error Resolution:** Verify that the instance volumes are in a healthy state and that Cinder snapshot quota is available, then retry the backup. Contact Support if the issue persists.  
​

OPENSTACK 1006
**Error Message:** Metadata upload failed.

**Error Description:** Occurs when backup metadata cannot be uploaded.  
​

**Error Resolution:** Retry the backup job. Contact Support if the issue persists.  
​

OPENSTACK 1007
**Error Message:** Volume not found.  
​

**Error Description:** This error occurs when a required Cinder volume has been deleted in OpenStack.  
​

**Error Resolution:** If a volume configured for backup is deleted from the OpenStack environment, the subsequent backup job will fail.  
​

OPENSTACK 1008
**Error Message:** Create instance failed.  
​

**Error Description:** Occurs when restore fails to create the target instance.  
​

**Error Resolution:** Verify the restore flavor, network, port, security group, and quota settings, then retry the restore. Contact Support if the issue persists.  
​

OPENSTACK 1009
**Error Message:** Volume attach failed.  
​

**Error Description:** Occurs when a volume cannot be attached to the backup proxy.  
​

**Error Resolution:** Verify that the backup proxy instance is running and that the volume can be attached in OpenStack. Then, retry the job. Contact Support if the issue persists.  
​

OPENSTACK 1010
**Error Message:** Insufficient Cinder quota.  
​

**Error Description:** Occurs when the OpenStack project does not have enough Cinder quota.  
​

**Error Resolution:** Increase the Cinder quota or free unused volumes and snapshots in the project, then retry the job.  
​

OPENSTACK 1011
**Error Message:** Failed to verify quota.  
​

**Error Description:** Occurs when the backup proxy cannot retrieve Cinder or Nova quota information.

**Error Resolution:** Verify OpenStack credentials and API access and then retry the job. Contact Support if the issue persists.  
​

OPENSTACK 1012
**Error Message:** Backup agent process terminated unexpectedly.  
​

**Error Description:** Occurs when the backup agent process exits unexpectedly during the job.  
​

**Error Resolution:** Retry the job. Contact Support if the issue persists.

question: We are moving our VMs to Proxmox. Which backup products can back up Proxmox VE virtual machines?
answer:
Veeam (Veeam Backup & Replication): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs to backup repositories, including VeeamZIP backups, with restore to Proxmox VE and cross-platform restore options [1][2].
Hornetsecurity (Altaro) (Backup & Recovery): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs to onsite and offsite locations (e.g., Azure, Amazon S3, Backblaze, Wasabi) with deduplication, and restores them via Full VM Restore and Cross Platform Restore [3][4].
Nakivo (Nakivo Backup & Replication): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs with incremental backups, CBT, application awareness, encryption, immutability, backup copies, replication, and full/file/object recovery [5][6].
Barracuda (Barracuda Backup): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs using an auto-deployed agent with change tracking and application-consistent backups, producing image-level backups [7][8].
Commvault (CommCell Console): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs and templates with full, incremental, and synthetic full backups, and restores full VMs and guest files and folders [9][10].
Storware (Backup and Recovery): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs via SSH transfer or export storage repository strategies, supporting full and incremental backups, snapshots, and file-level restore [12][13].
Bacula (Bacula): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs and LXC containers using the Proxmox Plugin, which creates snapshots and executes vzdump, supporting full backups of guests in any power state [14][15].
Druva (Druva): Backs up Proxmox VE VMs via a backup proxy connected to Proxmox nodes and clusters, with manual and scheduled backups [16][17].
Arcserve (Arcserve UDP): Backs up Proxmox-hosted VMs from the UDP Console, with restore to original or alternate locations and file/folder-level recovery [18][19].
Rubrik (Rubrik Security Cloud): Protects Proxmox VE VMs by registering the environment in RSC with RBS and NBD-based backups [20][21].
Acronis (Cyber Protect On-premises, Cyber Protect Cloud): Supports cross-platform recovery of disk-level backups to Proxmox virtual machines [22][23][24].
Axcient (x360Recover, Axcient (General)): Recovers Proxmox systems via Bare Metal Recovery using the Bare Metal Recovery ISO booted in Proxmox [27][28].
No supporting passage found for: AWS, Afi.ai, Arctera, Atempo, AvePoint, CloudAlly, CloudCasa, Cohesity, Datto, Dell, Eon, Flosum, GRAX, Gearset, Google, HYCU, IBM, Keepit, Microsoft, N-Able, NinjaOne (Dropsuite), Portworx, Red Hat, Salesforce, Slide, Spanning, Synology, Trilio, Unitrends, Velero, Zerto.

citations.title: Proxmox Virtual Environment
citations.text:
Proxmox Virtual Environment

Veeam Backup \& Replication offers various data protection and disaster recovery features for Proxmox Virtual Environment (Proxmox VE). Specifically, you can perform the following operations:

* Create backups of Proxmox VE VMs and store them in backup repositories.

* Create VeeamZIP backups of Proxmox VE VMs.

* Create several instances (copies) of the same backup data in different locations.
* Restore VMs from Proxmox VE VM backups to the Proxmox VE environment.

* Restore VMs from VMware ESXi and Microsoft Hyper\-V to the Proxmox VE environment.

* Restore VMs from Nutanix AHV, HPE Morpheus VM Essentials, oVirt KVM, Sangfor aSV, Scale Computing HyperCore, XCP\-ng and Citrix XenServer backups to the Proxmox VE environment.

* Restore VMs from backups produced by Veeam Plug\-in for Universal Hypervisor API to the Proxmox VE environment.

* Restore VMs from Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud backups to the Proxmox VE environment.
* Restore physical machines from backups created by Veeam Agents to the Proxmox VE environment.

* Restore VMs from Proxmox VE backups to Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud environments.

* Restore VMs from Proxmox VE backups to Nutanix AHV, HPE Morpheus VM Essentials, oVirt KVM, Sangfor aSV, Scale Computing HyperCore, XCP\-ng, Citrix XenServer environments and universal hypervisors.

* Perform Instant Recovery\* of VMs and physical machines to VMware vSphere, Microsoft Hyper\-V, Nutanix AHV and Proxmox VE environments.

* Restore application items (such as Microsoft Active Directory, Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft SharePoint, Microsoft DNS, PostgreSQL, Oracle Database and Microsoft SQL Server).
* Restore files and folders of Proxmox VE VM guest OSes.
* Export disks of backed\-up Proxmox VE VMs to VMDK, VHD and VHDX formats.
* Mount disks of backed\-up Proxmox VE VMs to any server and access data in the read\-only mode.

\*Instant Recovery to Proxmox VE has an experimental support status. For more information on Veeam experimental support, see [this Veeam KB article](https://www.veeam.com/kb2976).

citations.title: Considerations and Limitations
citations.text:
Considerations and Limitations

* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support backup of LXC containers.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support backup of VM templates.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support backup of VMs with the same BIOS UUID.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support backup of iSCSI disks attached to VMs — such disks are skipped from backup processing.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support backup of directly attached (passthrough) disks. If such disks are attached to a VM included into a backup job, these disks will be skipped from processing.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support backup of VM permissions granted to users, user groups and API tokens.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support backup of VMs that store their disks in the BTRFS and custom storage. All other [Proxmox VE storage types](https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Storage) are supported.
* The number of concurrent backup operations performed in each storage is limited to 4 to avoid excessive load on the production environment. To change the limit, contact [Veeam Customer Support](pve_export_logs.html).
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE does not support the recovery run logic for periodic backup schedules with a backup window configured — no job session will start immediately after the denied period is over. Only midnight is used as [a reference time](backup_window.html) for periodically run jobs.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE supports backup of VMs that store their disks in LVM\-based storage if the Snapshots as Volume Chain (SAVC) mechanism is enabled.

Guest Processing

When configuring guest processing in backup jobs, consider the following:

* The file exclusion functionality is not supported.

* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE cannot [use Kerberos authentication](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/kerberos_authentication.html?ver=13) while connecting to guest OSes of the processed VMs.

* When restoring a database using Veeam Explorers to the original VM, the VM hostname is used instead of the FQDN name. If Veeam Explorers cannot reach the VM, you can add the FQDN name and the IP address of the VM to the hosts file on the backup server.
* If you import backups created by a job with guest processing enabled, this backup job will truncate transaction logs but it will not store transaction log backups in the repository. To avoid the issue, before running the job, either clone the job and perform active full, or contact Veeam Customer Support.
* Image\-level, application\-aware backups of Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 servers running on Proxmox VE clusters are not Veeam Microsoft 365 restore explorers\-aware. The behavior described in [this article](https://bp.veeam.com/vb365/guide/design/vb365_with_vbr) is currently unsupported for Proxmox VE backups.

* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE will not be able to create an application\-consistent backup of a Microsoft SQL Server running a Windows Server Failover Cluster. If you add such a VM to the backup job scope and enable application\-aware processing for it, Veeam Backup \& Replication will only create an image\-level backup. To work around the limitation, [use Veeam Agent](agents_cluster_support.html) managed by Veeam Backup \& Replication instead.

Replication

When configuring replication of Proxmox VE resources, consider the following:

* Replication operations are supported only on the Veeam Backup \& Replication desktop console.
* Replication within the same cluster does not preserve MAC address of the original VM.
* Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE manages VM BIOS UUIDs in the following way:

* Generates new unique UUIDs while creating VM replicas.
* Preserves UUIDs while failing back to VMs in the original location.
* Generates new unique UUIDs for VMs while performing failover, permanent failover and failback to original VMs restored in a different location.

Making any changes to VM BIOS UUIDs manually may cause technical issues.

* If the original VM is missing disks that exist on the VM replica, Veeam Plug\-in for Proxmox VE will automatically create the missing disks during failback. The missing disks will be placed on the Proxmox VE storage that supports VM disk creation and has the most available free space.

Restore

When restoring Proxmox VE resources, consider the following:

citations.title: Proxmox VE Support Information
citations.text:
Proxmox VE Support Information
**Overview**

With the release of build 9\.16\.9\.0, VM Backup now supports backing up and restoring of VMs hosted on Proxmox VE environments. You can perform the following operations:

* An Internet connection is required to add the host in VM Backup
* Take backups of Proxmox VE VMs to onsite and offsite locations, such as Offsite Backup Server and cloud locations, like Azure, Amazon S3, Backblaze and Wasabi
* Take backups of Proxmox VE VMs irrespective of the storage type
* Backup data will be deduplicated using Hornetsecurity's augmented inline deduplication technology
* Restore Proxmox VE VMs back to a Proxmox VE environment, via Full VM Restore
* No new backup set required if you were running Proxmox VE on the Early Access builds

#### 

**Supported Versions**
* 8\.4
* 9\.0
* 9\.1

### 

**License**
Proxmox VE hosts will require a license. If you were running Proxmox VE on the Early Access builds, please make sure to license any previous hosts.

### 

**Known Issues \& Limitations**
* Replication and CDP will be available later on
* Restore operations —  on the **Proxmox VE host**temporary storage is also required with at least as much free space as the largest disk of the virtual machine (by default "/var/tmp"). Contact the [support team](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us) to override this location
* Concurrency; One Backup and one Restore can run at the same time per host (maximum up to 4 hosts)
* The 'root' user must be used in order to add the Proxmox VE hosts (users part of the root group are not supported)
* When adding more than 1 Proxmox host to the same console, ensure that the hosts do not have the same hostname
* Pass\-through or RDM (Raw Device Mappings) are not backed up
* Excluding Drives is not supported
* Backup of LXC containers is not supported

citations.text:
How to perform a Cross Platform Restore

From build 9\.4 onwards, VM Backup introduced the ability to perform a Cross Platform Restore, allowing you to restore virtual machines across Hyper\-V and VMware. This feature will be available with the **Unlimited**, **Unlimited Plus Edition** and **Subscription**licenses.

Below is a list of the supported Windows operating systems, VMware and Proxmox versions:  

| **Source Hyper\-V Host** | **VMware \& Proxmox Restore target** |
| --- | --- |
| Windows Server 2019 | ESXi 7\.0, 8\.0 \& 9\.0 \| Proxmox VE 8\.4, 9\.0, 9\.1 |
| Windows Server 2022 | ESXi 7\.0, 8\.0 \& 9\.0 \| Proxmox VE 8\.4, 9\.0, 9\.1 |
| Windows Server 2025 | ESXi 7\.0, 8\.0 \& 9\.0 \| Proxmox VE 8\.4, 9\.0, 9\.1 |

| **Source VMware Host** | **Hyper\-V \& Proxmox Restore target** |
| --- | --- |
| ESXi 7\.0 | Windows Server 2019, 2022 \& 2025 \| Proxmox VE 8\.4, 9\.0, 9\.1 |
| ESXi 8\.0 | Windows Server 2019, 2022 \& 2025 \| Proxmox VE 8\.4, 9\.0, 9\.1 |
| ESXi 9\.0 | Windows Server 2019, 2022 \& 2025 \| Proxmox VE 8\.4, 9\.0, 9\.1 |

| **Source Proxmox VE Host** | **Hyper\-V \& VMware Restore target** |
| --- | --- |
| Proxmox 8\.4 | Windows Server 2019, 2022 \& 2025 \| ESXi 7\.0, 8\.0 \& 9\.0 |
| Proxmox 9\.0 | Windows Server 2019, 2022 \& 2025 \| ESXi 7\.0, 8\.0 \& 9\.0 |
| Proxmox 9\.1 | Windows Server 2019, 2022 \& 2025 \| ESXi 7\.0, 8\.0 \& 9\.0 |

To perform a Cross Platform restore, follow the steps below:

1. Navigate to **\[Restore]** \> **\[Cross Platform Restore]**
2. Select one or more backup locations that contain the backups of the VMs you wish to restore. Then click **\[Next]** to proceed  

![](/media/80b4b90e-e96a-4bf9-b891-d98c73d02e95/3ab86c304d2c.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Cross Platform Restore' wizard in HornetSecurity VM Backup, showing Step 1: 'Choose locations to restore from'. The network backup location '\10.2.185.60\Backups\Don\CrossPlatform_Testing' is selected, while other locations like local backups, Backblaze, and offsite backups are listed but not selected.
3. Select the VM(s) you wish to restore and click **\[Next]**  

![](/media/80b4b90e-e96a-4bf9-b891-d98c73d02e95/432ec4de96f4.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Cross Platform Restore' wizard, showing Step 2: 'Choose which Virtual Machines to Restore'. Two virtual machines, 'DC' and 'Mail-Server', are selected for restoration, each with their host IP or name listed.
4. Select which backup version you would like to restore. You can also give the restored VM a new name.  

Then select to which host you will be restoring to, you can refer to the table above for the full list of supported versions.  

You can also select to restore to an **\[Unconfigured Host]**, which will not require a license. [See here for more information.](https://support.hornetsecurity.com/hc/en-us/articles/19688306365585)  

Finally, select the **\[Restore to Location]**, which for **Hyper\-V**will be any locally connected disk (iSCSI included) and for **VMWare** you will be able to select a datastore **\[Restore to Datastore]**  

![](/media/80b4b90e-e96a-4bf9-b891-d98c73d02e95/b29eb2574112.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of Step 3 in the Cross Platform Restore wizard, showing configuration options for restoring two virtual machines (DC and Mail-Server) to different hosts and locations, including restore version, name, decryption key, target host, and restore path.

When you're happy with your selection, click **\[Restore]**
5. The restore operation will begin in the background and progress can be monitored from the Dashboard  

![](/media/80b4b90e-e96a-4bf9-b891-d98c73d02e95/18f8ecf038f4.png)

> **Figure:** Dashboard screen of HornetSecurity VM Backup showing Backup Drive Status with a pie chart of free space, backup, and other data; Deduplication & Compression status with 0% savings; Active & Upcoming Operations with two restores in progress; and Recent Operations listing completed backups for VM-003, Proxmox, Ubuntu, and VM-001.

**Notes:**

• The VM will be restored with the basic configuration, so once restored, make sure to check the settings

• The NIC will be automatically disabled and will need to be added manually

• For certain Linux VMs, if they fail to boot, try a fresh VM configuration and attach the restored virtual disks

Once the restore jobs are complete, you will see the completed restore operations in the Dashboard, and your VMs will show up on the specified Host and/or Datastore.  

![](/media/80b4b90e-e96a-4bf9-b891-d98c73d02e95/6a5987bf17fe.png)

Feature Requirements
Proxmox VE Support

Proxmox Virtual Environments (VE) are supported on all [supported browsers](https://helpcenter.nakivo.com/User-Guide/Content/Deployment/System-Requirements/Deployment-Requirements.htm#Web) for NAKIVO Backup \& Replication and all [supported operating systems](https://helpcenter.nakivo.com/User-Guide/Content/Deployment/System-Requirements/Supported-Platforms.htm).

To successfully discover Proxmox VE items (clusters and standalone hosts (nodes)), add them to the **Inventory**, back up Proxmox VE VMs, create backup copies, and perform full and file level recovery, make sure you meet the following requirements:

* **Proxmox VE** are supported for the following Proxmox VE versions:

	+ **Proxmox VE 8\.x**. For more details, refer to Proxmox VE [versions table](https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/FAQ#faq-support-table).
> **Notes**
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 	+ The Proxmox VE (host/cluster) of the version lower than the oldest supported version cannot be discovered.
> 	+ The Proxmox VE (host/cluster) of the version higher than the newest supported version can be discovered, but confirmation of the operation is required to proceed.
> 	+ The product can discover all Proxmox VE storage types (See [Proxmox VE Storage Types](https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Storage#_storage_types)), except the following:
> 	
> 	
> 		- PBS
> 		- ESXi

> **Notes**
> 
> 
> 
> 
> 	+ For the Proxmox VE cluster, the transporter is injected into each cluster host.
> 	+ Transporters injected into Proxmox VE hosts are supported for auto\-update.

**Supported Functionality**

	+ Change Block Tracking (CBT)

	> 
	> 
	>

	>

	> 	
	> 	> qm agent \<vmid\> ping
	> 	- Virtio\-serial driver must be installed on the Windows based VM. For Linux based VMs, you only need to run the install command.
	> 	
	> 	
	> 		* For Debian/Ubuntu: *apt\-get install qemu\-guest\-agent*
	> 
	> 	- For FreeBSD\-based VMs, create the script files in the source VM usr/sbin/ folder:
	> 	
	> 	
	> 		* "pre\-freeze\-script"
	> 		* "post\-thaw\-script"Make sure they have sufficient permissions.
	+ Backup encryption

* Backup copy of Proxmox VE VM can be saved to the following types of storage:

	+ Repositories/stream repositories with creating immutable copies for Proxmox VE VM backups
	+ Data storage types:

		- Forever Incremental

Native Change Tracking

citations.title: Proxmox VE Backup
citations.text:
Proxmox VE Backup

Proxmox VE (Virtual Environment) is an open\-source virtualization platform for enterprises. Proxmox VE is Debian GNU/Linux based and allows deployment and management of [Virtual machines (QEMU/KVM hypervisor)](https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Qemu/KVM_Virtual_Machines) and Containers (LXC).

This feature allows you to backup Proxmox VE infrastructures, allowing you to:

* Add supported Proxmox VE clusters and standalone hosts (nodes) to the Inventory.
* Back up Proxmox VE VMs and templates.
* Copy Proxmox VE VM backups.
* Create Proxmox VE VM replicas.
* Instantly recover full Proxmox VE VMs from backups using Flash VM Boot.
* Recover full Proxmox VE VMs from backups.
* Perform File Recovery from Proxmox VE VM backups to source or a custom VM.
* Perform Object Recovery from Proxmox VE VM backups to a custom destination.
* Perform Universal Object recovery from Proxmox VE VM backups for a VM disk.

The feature supports **Full** and **Incremental** backups and offers two methods for **Change Block Tracking** (CBT): the native Proxmox VE change tracking and the proprietary method developed by NAKIVO.

The feature supports **Backup encryption** to ensure data is securely encrypted and transferred, preventing unauthorized access and maintaining data confidentiality.

Immutability is supported for backups stored in supported repositories.

A transporter injected inside a Proxmox VE host or a Proxmox VE node can be edited when locked within a job run.

For a full list of supported functionality, see the corresponding section in Feature Requirements.

For more details on how to discover Proxmox VE clusters and standalone hosts (nodes), add them to the Inventory, back up Proxmox VMs, create backup copies, and perform full and file\-level recovery refer to the following articles:

* [Adding Proxmox VE Items to Inventory](../Settings/Inventory/Adding-Proxmox-VE-Items-to-Inventory.htm)
* [Creating Proxmox VE Backup Jobs](../Backup/Creating-Proxmox-VE-Backup-Jobs/Creating-Proxmox-VE-Backup-Jobs.htm)
* [Creating Backup Copy Jobs of Proxmox VE Backups](../Backup/Creating-Backup-Copy-Jobs/Creating-Backup-Copy-Jobs.htm)
* [Full Recovery Job Wizard for Proxmox VE](../Recovery/Full-Recovery/Proxmox-VE-VM-Recovery/Proxmox-VE-VM-Recovery.htm)
* [File Recovery from VM Backups](../Recovery/Granular-Recovery/File-Recovery/File-Recovery.htm)
* [Object Recovery for Microsoft Exchange](../Recovery/Granular-Recovery/Object-Recovery-for-Microsoft-Exchange/Object-Recovery-for-Microsoft-Exchange.htm)
* [Object Recovery for Microsoft Active Directory](../Recovery/Granular-Recovery/Object-Recovery-for-Microsoft-Active-Directory/Object-Recovery-for-Microsoft-Active-Directory.htm)

citations.title: Protecting Proxmox VE
citations.text:
Protecting Proxmox VE
Configure the Proxmox VE data source

Barracuda Backup follows the lifecycle policy of each supported vendor and does not support versions that are end of life or end of support as indicated by the product vendor.

Barracuda Backup uses an auto\-deployed agent to perform backups of Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE) virtual machines (VMs). Once configured, the agent handles information gathering and backup processing on the Proxmox VE cluster node where it is deployed.

**Currently not supported**

* Backup of the Proxmox host machine
* Cloud or Local LiveBoot
**Tip:** Configure the data source using the IP address or FQDN of the Proxmox host. This ensures reliable connectivity between the Barracuda Backup appliance and the Proxmox VE environment.

Use the following steps to configure a Proxmox VE data source:

1. Log in to Barracuda Backup and select the associated Barracuda Backup device in the left pane or in the devices table for customers with multiple Barracuda Backup devices.
2. Go to **Backup \> Sources**, and click **Add a Computer**.
3. Complete the following information on the **Add a Computer** page:

	* **Computer description**
	* **Computer name**
4. In the **Computer type** drop\-down menu, select **Proxmox VE**.
5. In the **Proxmox VE Computer Information** section, enter the credentials of the account that Barracuda Backup is to use to connect to the primary node in the Proxmox VE cluster.

**Note** 

In the initial release, it is required to temporarily allow password\-based authentication for the root user by editing the SSH configuration on the first node where the agent is deploying. You can disable this after the cluster is configured on the Barracuda Backup.

As a best practice, use a unique account for this integration point and grant it the least level of privileges required, coordinating with the system administrator. This account requires administrative privileges to the Proxmox VE cluster. For additional information, see [Security for Integrating with Other Systems \- Best Practices](https://documentation.campus.barracuda.com/wiki/spaces/CP/pages/8198763 "https://documentation.campus.barracuda.com/wiki/spaces/CP/pages/8198763").

6. Click **Test Credentials** to verify that Barracuda Backup can successfully communicate with the Proxmox VE cluster. If the connection is unsuccessful, verify that the credentials are correct.
7. Once the Proxmox data source is configured, click **Save**.
8. The **Add Data Source** page displays. Ensure that **Enable Backups** is checked. This allows Barracuda Backup to perform backups of the VMs.
9. In the Proxmox VE Agent deployment section, click on **Deploy Proxmox VE Agent.** This will deploy the agent responsible for information gathering and backup processing to the node in the cluster it is configured on.

By default, if a snapshot fails when trying to quiesce a VM, Barracuda Backup retries the snapshot without quiescing. Quiescing pauses disk activity to ensure a clean, consistent snapshot. To require quiescing on every snapshot, select **Quiesce Only**.

10. Finish configuring the offsite replication destination, and click **Save**.
11. Once the data source is configured, the **Schedules** page displays. For more information, see [Backup Scheduling](https://documentation.campus.barracuda.com/wiki/spaces/BBSv42/pages/7111136 "https://documentation.campus.barracuda.com/wiki/spaces/BBSv42/pages/7111136").

Change tracking configuration
Change Block Tracking (CBT) speeds up incremental backups by tracking only the data blocks that changed since the last backup, rather than re\-reading the entire disk.

1. Navigate to the Proxmox data source configuration.
2. Locate the **Enable Change Tracking** checkbox.
3. Enable the option for optimal incremental backup performance.
4. Click **Save**.

**Default behavior**  
Change tracking is enabled by default for new Proxmox data sources, with a maximum of six incremental backups after each full backup.

Application\-consistent backups
For VMs that require application\-level consistency, such as database or email server workloads, install and enable the QEMU Guest Agent and then require application\-consistent backups in the backup configuration.

citations.title: Backup
citations.text:
Backup

Barracuda Backup produces file\-level backups for any data source protected with the Barracuda Backup Agent for Windows, macOS, and Linux, as well as data sources protected using network file system protocols. This includes both physical servers, guest virtual machine (VM) systems, and network\-attached storage devices. File\-level backups provide a greater level of granularity and control over the data that is protected and recovered than image\-level or volume\-level backups. With file\-level backups you can recover entire systems (bare metal recovery), volumes, folders, and individual files.

Barracuda Backup is also capable of producing image\-level backups for VMware vSphere, Microsoft Hyper\-V, and Proxmox VE virtual machines. When you back up VMs, Barracuda Backup copies a VM image as a whole, at a block level. Image\-level VM backups do not require a backup agent to be installed in each guest VM, thus reducing the amount of time required to configure and manage the protection of these virtual environments. With image\-level VM backups you can recover entire VMs and perform both file\-level and instant VM recovery. **Note:** Instant VM recovery (LiveBoot) is not currently supported for Proxmox VE VMs.

citations.title: Proxmox VE
citations.text:
Proxmox VE
Backup Process[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/proxmox-ve#backup-process)

SSH Transfer[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/proxmox-ve#ssh-transfer)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

SSH Transfer strategy:

*   supports only QCOW2 disk images and Ceph RBD volumes

*   supports incremental backups

*   supports over iSCSI

![](/media/a1c188a8-1d6c-4ebb-95c6-1edb2d9e7e3a/afe37d5a5897f656.png)

> **Figure:** Diagram illustrating Storware Backup and Recovery architecture, showing management via Proxmox VE API with SDH data export from hypervisor nodes to a backup destination (file/NFS/object/enterprise systems), with green arrows indicating transfer and blue arrows indicating management.

Backup is done by transferring QCOW2 disk images over SSH directly from the hypervisor (optionally using Netcat for transfer). Metadata is backed up only in the full backup. This method supports incremental backups where the last snapshot is required for the next incremental backups. The resulting backup has separate files for each disk + metadata, so you have the option to exclude specific drives as well.

*   QCOW2 - file-based storage only

*   crash-consistent snapshots created using hypervisor CLI over SSH

*   optionally FS freeze can be executed before snapshot can be executed (FS thaw once the snapshot is completed) if enabled and guest tools installed inside

*   QCOW2 snapshots mounted locally on the hypervisor and exported via SSH (optionally with netcat)

*   for incremental backups, both last and currently created snapshots are mounted and block-difference is sent via SSH

*   metadata exported via SSH • restore imports metadata and overwrites empty disks with data from a merged backup over SSH

Export storage repository[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/proxmox-ve#export-storage-repository)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Proxmox virtual environment requires you to create storage used for VM export. Export storage should also be accessible to Storware Backup & Recovery Node in its staging directory. This implies that storage space doesn't have to be exported by Storware Backup & Recovery Node - it can be mounted from an external source. The only requirement is to have it visible from both Proxmox VE hosts and the Node itself. Keep in mind that ownership of the files on the share should allow both Storware Backup & Recovery and Proxmox VE to read and write files.

![](/media/a1c188a8-1d6c-4ebb-95c6-1edb2d9e7e3a/882a7fa4c29e2bac.png)

> **Figure:** The image is a diagram illustrating the architecture of Storware Backup and Recovery for Proxmox environments. It shows the data flow from VMs on a Proxmox host through export storage (staging) via NFS to a staging space, then to various backup destinations including local storage, file systems, deduplication appliances, object storage, and enterprise backup providers.

Backup Process[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/proxmox-ve#backup-process-1)
*   native VM export is done to the prepared NFS storage (staging space on Storware Backup & Recovery) using SSH access to the hypervisor

*   crash-consistency - FS freeze used for VMs, LVM snapshot for containers

*   optional application consistency using pre/post export command execution for VMs (pre/post snapshot) for containers

*   data and metadata are in a single VMA image

*   only full backups are supported

*   restore imports VMA image to the hypervisor

citations.title: Proxmox VE
citations.text:
Proxmox VE
How to set up export storage repository backup[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/proxmox-ve#how-to-set-up-export-storage-repository-backup)

Proxmox virtual environments require backup storage to be defined on each server. This storage must be a location accessible from Storware Backup & Recovery Node (the simplest setup, when you use only 1 node, is to create NFS share for the staging path on Storware Backup & Recovery Node)

1.  Create storage from NFS share (Content-type: **only VZDump**)

citations.title: Features
citations.text:
Features
Proxmox and QEMU Plugins Comparison

The Proxmox and QEMU Plugins both provide backup capabilities for containers and virtual
machines running on the Proxmox VE hypervisor. While they share this common purpose, each
plugin offers different features. The information below will help you choose the most suitable
option for backing up VMs or containers on Proxmox.

If you need to back up a genuine QEMU hypervisor, the Proxmox Plugin cannot be used;
in this case, only the QEMU Plugin is supported.

| Features | Proxmox Plugin | QEMU Plugin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supported hypervisor | Proxmox hypervisors | QEMU hypervisors: Proxmox (PVE mode) and Genuine QEMU (QEMU mode) |
| Virtualization technology | Backup/restore QEMU VMs and LXC guests | Backup/restore only QEMU VMs |
| API technology used | Proxmox API (Proxmox VE Rest\-like API) | QMP (QEMU Machine Protocol) API |
| Backup level support | Full only | Full/Incremental backups using Block Dirty Bitmap. Differential backups are not supported. |
| Backup capability | VMs in any state (stopped, running, etc.) | Only running VMs |
| Disk image format | Backed up disk image is a raw disk | Backed up disk image is a qcow2 disk |
| Hypervisor storage usage | Does not require space to store the backup before sending it to the Storage Daemon | Requires space to store the backup before sending it to the Storage Daemon |

For a complete understanding of each plugin’s capabilities and constraints, it is strongly
recommended to review the [QEMU](../../qemu/index.html#qemuplugin) and [Proxmox](../index.html#proxmoxplugin) Plugins
documentation separately, with particular attention to their limitations;
see [Limitations for Proxmox](../Limitations/index.html#proxmoxlimitations) and [Limitations for QEMU](../../qemu/index.html#qemulimitations).

See also

citations.title: Backup
citations.text:
Backup

[Enterprise](https://docs.baculasystems.com/BCBEComparison/index.html)
Bacula Enterprise Only

This solution is **only** available for Bacula Enterprise. For subscription inquiries, please reach out to <sales@baculasystems.com>.

The backup of a single guest VM consists of the following steps:

1. Save guest VM configuration (for [LXC](../../../../../../glossary.html#term-LXC) guest VMs).
2. Create a new backup snapshot (default), suspending or stopping the
guest VM as requested.
3. Execute `vzdump` and save data.

Backups can be performed for guest VMs in any power state (running or
stopped). The Proxmox hypervisor will automatically create the required
backup snapshot and remove it after the backup. Any other guest VMs
snapshots will be unaffected.

The Proxmox Plugin will inform you about every guest VM backup start and
finish:

```
 JobId 68: Start Backup JobId 68, Job=proxmox.2018-01-25_11.25.05_21
 JobId 68: Using Device "FileChgr1-Dev2" to write.
 JobId 68: Volume "Vol-0002" previously written, moving to end of data.
 JobId 68: proxmox: Start Backup vm: ubuntu-container (101)
 JobId 68: proxmox: Backup of vm: ubuntu-container (101) OK.
...

```

The backup will create a single (`.vma`) file for any [QEMU](../../../../../../glossary.html#term-QEMU) guest VM
and two files (`.conf` and `.tar`) for any [LXC](../../../../../../glossary.html#term-LXC) guest VM which is
saved. Inside Bacula, those are represented as follows.

* `/@proxmox/qm/<name-label>/VM<vmid>.vma` for [QEMU](../../../../../../glossary.html#term-QEMU) guest VMs
* `/@proxmox/lxc/<name-label>/VM<vmid>.conf` and
* `/@proxmox/lxc/<name-label>/VM<vmid>.tar` for [LXC](../../../../../../glossary.html#term-LXC) guest VMs

Multiple files will be created during a backup if multiple guest VMs are
backed up with one job. However, note that backing up multiple VMs goes against
[hypervisor best practices](../../../general/index.html#hypervisorbestpractices). The distinct file names as shown above allow to
locate the proper guest VM archive for restore.

Tip

You can exclude machine disks from [Proxmox](../../../../../../glossary.html#term-Proxmox) image backup in
the Proxmox Console VM Disk Settings screen.

See also

Next articles:

Plan and set up your Proxmox environment

citations.title: How to manually backup a Proxmox virtual machine
citations.text:
How to manually backup a Proxmox virtual machine
To manually back up a virtual machine

If you want to backup virtual machines at a given point in time, you can trigger a manual backup on a virtual machine. After the manual backup is complete, the next backup happens as per the schedule defined in the backup policy.

Considerations
* A manual backup is not restricted by the backup window that you defined in the backup policy; it continues till all the data is backed up.
* If you restart or reboot your virtual machines during backups, the backup operation is aborted. Hybrid Workloads agents or backup proxy start a fresh backup following the backup schedule. Alternatively, you can start a manual backup at any time.
* A manual backup is not restricted by bandwidth, it uses the maximum bandwidth available.
* The Automatic Retry feature does not work with manual backups.
* When the Proxmox VE UI disk size differs from the internal **vg** or **zpool** allocation, backup and restore processes utilize the actual storage size defined by the Volume Group or ZFS Pool rather than the UI\-reported size.

1. Log in to the **Management Console**.
2. From the top menu bar, select your organization if organizations are enabled.
3. Click **Protect \> Proxmox**.  
The **All Nodes** page appears that lists all the registered nodes/clusters.
4. Select the registered node/cluster from the **Node** list in the left navigation pane.
5. In the left navigation pane, click **Configured VMs**.
6. Select the virtual machine(s) you want to backup.  
​

[

![](/media/bf8efc52-586a-4dc9-aa54-8a29012c3200/fb66fd0844c4e1fb.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Configured VMs' screen in Enterprise Workloads, showing a list of virtual machines with columns for Virtual Machine, Administrative Group, Backup Policy, Backup Enabled, and Last Backup Status. The 'Backup Now' button is highlighted, and one VM (AKS-VM-4) is selected.

](/media/bf8efc52-586a-4dc9-aa54-8a29012c3200/fb66fd0844c4e1fb.png)
7. Click **Backup Now** and confirm your action.
Backup of the selected virtual machines start. You can track the progress and details about the backup job in progress on the [Proxmox jobs page](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/13740918-monitoring-proxmox-jobs).

citations.title: New Features and Enhancements
citations.text:
New Features and Enhancements

The following new features and enhancements are available for Arcserve UDP 11\.0:

**New Features**

* **Proxmox:** This release introduces support for Proxmox Virtual Environment (PVE) in the UDP Console. Proxmox is an open\-source enterprise virtualization platform that combines the KVM hypervisor, Linux Containers (LXC), software\-defined storage, and advanced networking in a single solution. With this integration, you can protect Proxmox virtual machines directly from the UDP Console. The web\-based interface provides centralized visibility and control to simplify backup management and strengthen disaster recovery operations.
* This release includes the following capabilities:
+ Backup of Proxmox\-hosted virtual machines that run UDP\-supported Windows operating systems and Linux distributions.
+ Restore virtual machines to the original location or an alternate location for migration, and disaster recovery scenarios.
+ Restore files and folders by mounting a recovery point, enabling granular recovery without restoring the entire virtual machine.

**Enhancements**

* **Support for Preserving Custom Trusted Certificates During UDP Agent Upgrade:** UDP Agent upgrades now automatically preserve customer\-added SSL/TLS trusted certificates. If your environment uses custom certificates for secure communication, the certificates remain available after the upgrade completes, eliminating the need to manually reconfigure them after each agent upgrade.
* **Note:** This enhancement applies to UDP Agent upgrades on supported Windows and Linux nodes.
* **NTFS Volume Support:** Enhanced support for backing up NTFS volumes formatted with allocation unit sizes up to 2 MB. Previously, Arcserve UDP supported backup operations only for volumes formatted with allocation unit sizes up to 64 KB.
* **Assured Security Enhancements**
+ **Incremental Scan Support:** UDP 11\.0 now performs Assured Security Incremental Scans. Instead of rescanning the entire recovery point, it scans only new or changed files since the last scan. Activity log clearly shows whether each scan job ran a Full or an Incremental Scan.
+ **ReFS Support:** Assured Security now scans ReFS file systems in addition to NTFS. It supports ReFS versions 3\.1, 3\.4, and 3\.7 for both Full and Incremental Scans.

* **Notes:**
+ Current scans cannot detect renamed or moved files because their creation or modification timestamps do not change. This enhancement is planned for the future.
+ Each scan job generates an antivirus scan result in the activity log.

Onboarding a Proxmox environment
Procedure

Onboard a Proxmox Virtual Environment in RSC to protect Proxmox

Before you begin
See the general prerequisites in [Prerequisites for Proxmox VE
 protection](prerequisites_proxmox_ve_protection.html "Proxmox VE protection on RSC requires specific platform configurations, software installations, and account permissions to enable successful backup and recovery operations through RSC.").

About this task
To protect Proxmox hosts in RSC, you must register your Proxmox
 VE instance with RSC.

1. Log in to RSC.
2. Click ![Applications](https://docs.rubrik.com/en-us/saas/images/ui-icons/AppTray.svg) and select
 Data Protection.
The Data Protection dashboard appears.
3. On the navigation bar, click Inventory.
The Inventory page appears.
4. Click the Proxmox VE inventory card.
The Proxmox VMs page appears.
5. On the Proxmox VE card, click Set up to configure your
 Proxmox VE instance.
The Proxmox VM page appears.
6. Click Add Source.
The Add Proxmox VE wizard appears and displays the Enter Proxmox
 Environment Details page.
7. Enter the Proxmox VE details:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Proxmox VE Hostname | Enter the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) or IP  address of the API endpoint of the Proxmox  environment.Note: For clustered environments, any one  Proxmox node is sufficient. |
| API token | Enter the API token of the Proxmox environment. |
| Certificate (optional) | Enter the certificate at the root certificate path:  /etc/pve/pve\-root\-ca.pem. |

8. Click Next.
The Select Rubrik Cluster page appears.
9. On the Select Rubrik Cluster page, select the Rubrik
 cluster that will protect the Proxmox environment.
10. Click Next.
The Confirmation page appears.

RSC adds the Proxmox environment.
12. Click Finish.

Results
RSC establishes a secure connection to Proxmox VE and begins
 discovering virtual machines and related resources to start protecting Proxmox virtual
 machines.The new Proxmox environment appears on the Inventory page.

citations.title: Prerequisites for Proxmox VE protection
citations.text:
Prerequisites for Proxmox VE protection

Proxmox VE protection on RSC requires specific platform
 configurations, software installations, and account permissions to enable successful backup
 and recovery operations through RSC.

The following prerequisites apply for Proxmox VE protection.

**The following table lists software agent and network connectivity requirements
 for data ingestion.**

| Component | Configuration details |
| --- | --- |
| Rubrik cluster | You must set up a Rubrik cluster that is connected to RSC. |
| Rubrik Backup Service | You must install Rubrik Backup Service (RBS) on each required  Proxmox node and register it with RSC prior to  backup.Before installing RBS, however, you must install the  `uuid-runtime` package on each Proxmox node.  This package provides the `uuidgen` utility,  which RBS requires to generate a UUID during installation. You  install the package by running the following command:`apt  install uuid-runtime` |
| NBD client | You must install the Network Block Device (NBD) client on the  Proxmox node for backups to work with the `apt install  nbd-client` command.Proxmox backup requires the NBD  kernel module to be loaded in one of the following ways:* Run the `sudo modprobe nbd nbds_max=256`  command to load the module immediately. * Alternatively, you can apply persistent load  (recommended): To ensure the module loads automatically  with the correct settings after a reboot, you must run  the following commands as  root: ``` # Set the number of allowed NBD devices echo "options nbd nbds_max=256" > /etc/modprobe.d/nbd.conf # Ensure the module loads on boot echo "nbd" > /etc/modules-load.d/nbd.conf ``` |
| Fleecing storage | RSC allocates a fleecing disk for each virtual  machine disk and stores the fleecing disk in the same location as  the backed up disks. The required disk capacity is proportional to  the amount of changes written to the disk during the backup. |
| QEMU guest agent | The Rubrik cluster needs the virtual machine IP address to  communicate with RBS inside the virtual machine, and the QEMU guest  agent reports it. You must install and run the QEMU guest agent in  the destination virtual machine to recover folders or  files. |
| Rubrik Backup Service (in\-guest) | You must install and run RBS in the destination virtual machine.  The Rubrik cluster must be able to connect to RBS at the IP address  that the QEMU guest agent reports. |

**The following table shows required credentials and RBAC privileges for
 environment management.**

| Access type | Permission level |
| --- | --- |
| Required roles | RSC requires the Data Source Management  privilege to add Proxmox VE environment resources to the  root. |
| API token | RSC requires a valid API token generated in  Proxmox VE for REST API interactions. You need the proper  permissions to view resources and create disks and virtual machines.  When creating tokens, you must de\-select the Privilege separation  option in Proxmox VE. |
| RSC privileges | RSC requires the AddProxmoxEnvironment  privilege to register new environments. |
| Organization access | RSC requires global organization access to add  Proxmox VE environment resources to the root. |
| Proxmox VE certificate | The Proxmox VE certificate must match either the IP address or the  hostname of the Proxmox VE host. |

Cross-platform recovery
Cross\-platform recovery

You can recover a disk\-level backup to a physical machine or to a virtual machine. For example, a disk\-level backup is an Entire machine backup or a Disk/volumes backup that contains the system disk and the boot disk. 

Cross\-platform recovery (machine migration) is performed in the following cases:

* When you recover a backup of a physical machine to a virtual machine.
* When you recover a backup of a virtual machine to a physical machine.
* When you recover a backup of a virtual machine to a virtual machine on a different type of hypervisor.

Cross-platform recovery
Cross\-platform recovery

You can recover a disk\-level backup to a physical machine or to a virtual machine. For example, a disk\-level backup is an Entire machine backup or a Disk/volumes backup that contains the system disk and the boot disk. 

Cross\-platform recovery (machine migration) is performed in the following cases:

* When you recover a backup of a physical machine to a virtual machine.
* When you recover a backup of a virtual machine to a physical machine.
* When you recover a backup of a virtual machine to a virtual machine on a different type of hypervisor. 

If a virtual machine is backed up by a protection agent installed inside the guest operating system, the backup is treated as a physical machine backup.

citations.title: Perform a Proxmox Recovery - x360Recover
citations.text:
Perform a Proxmox Recovery - x360Recover
Proxmox Environment Setup

Overview
Unlike Hyper\-V or VMware, Proxmox doesn’t have an easy way to import virtual disks. This is mainly because of the flexible storage model used by KVM systems. Often, storage does not use virtual disk image files but instead leverages ZFS volumes directly, for example. Because of this, the simplest and most universal recovery method for these platforms is Bare Metal recovery.

Despite the name, Bare Metal Recovery refers to the direct recovery of a system from backup to the recovery machine. Whether this machine is truly bare\-metal hardware or a virtual machine does not matter. Boot the virtual machine from the Bare Metal Recovery ISO to perform the recovery.

To set up a Proxmox environment, upload the Bare Metal Recovery ISO to the Proxmox ISO store.

1. Download the Bare Metal Recovery ISO from the Appliance or Vault downloads page, or directly from the [x360Recover downloads](/x360Recover/x360Recover_Software_Downloads "x360Recover Software Downloads") page. After you download the ISO, upload it to Proxmox so it's available to virtual machines.  

![baremetalrestore.png](/media/37ed6681-333d-41dc-b6b0-6ce4caeca392/080e221e7f29d2a5.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Downloads section in the x360Recover appliance interface, showing two download options: 'Installation ISO' and 'Bare Metal Restore', with the latter highlighted by a red box.
2. In Proxmox, select your ISO storage bin and click **Upload**. If you have not created an ISO storage bin yet, refer to the [Proxmox documentation](https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Storage:_Directory) for instructions on configuring storage.  

![isoupload.png](/media/37ed6681-333d-41dc-b6b0-6ce4caeca392/f1471126a3a9bb03.png)

> **Figure:** This screenshot displays the Proxmox Virtual Environment 8.1.3 interface, specifically showing the Storage ISOs view on node 'pve'. The Upload button is highlighted in red, indicating the action to upload an ISO file, with a list of available ISO images visible below.
3. Select the file and click **Upload**.  

![isoupload2.png](/media/37ed6681-333d-41dc-b6b0-6ce4caeca392/e64da62bb8e45d96.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of an upload dialog showing a file named 'x360Recover-bmr-rc1.iso' with a size of 3.83 GB, currently 14.18% uploaded (555.42 MiB), with 'Abort' and 'Upload' buttons at the bottom.

question: Which backup products can write backups to a physical LTO tape library or autoloader?
answer:
Nakivo (Nakivo Backup & Replication): Native tape support writes backups to physical tape libraries (LTO3 or later) and standalone drives, with backups stored in a repository then copied to tape [1].
Storware (Backup and Recovery): Provides native, fully integrated support for LTO tape libraries via a Tape Manager service and Tape Pool backup destinations [3][4].
Veeam (Veeam Backup & Replication): Backup to tape jobs copy backups from a primary repository to LTO or IBM 3592 tape libraries, standalone drives, and VTLs [5][6].
Unitrends (Unitrends Unified Backup): Recovery Series and Recovery MAX appliances with the ADX license copy backups to SCSI, SAS, or Fibre Channel tape devices [7].
Atempo (Miria): Media Manager supports a wide range of LTO tape libraries and drives, writing in TAR (PAX) or LTFS formats [9].
Atempo (Tina): Supports automated library management with LTO and other tape drives connected via SAS, FC, or SCSI [10].
Acronis (Cyber Protect On-premises): Backs up to stand-alone tapes and tape libraries attached to a storage node, using tape pools selected in a protection plan [12].
Cohesity (NetBackup): Backs up NDMP hosts to tape devices and advanced tape libraries, including three-way and remote NDMP backups to tape [16].
Arctera (Backup Exec): Uses Advanced Device and Media Management to back up to robotic libraries, automatically allocating and recycling media [18].
Bacula (Bacula): Bacula Enterprise backup and restore software acts as a client application driving tape libraries managed by ACSLS [23].
Dell (NetWorker): Supports backing up to WORM and DLTWORM tape drives and media, applying WORM attributes to pools [25][26].
Arcserve (Arcserve Backup): Automatically detects and configures tape libraries via the Tape Engine, with the Tape Library Option license, for backup to tape [27][28].
No supporting passage found for: AWS, Afi.ai, AvePoint, Axcient, Barracuda, CloudAlly, CloudCasa, Commvault, Datto, Druva, Eon, Flosum, GRAX, Gearset, Google, HYCU, Hornetsecurity (Altaro), IBM, Keepit, Microsoft, N-Able, NinjaOne (Dropsuite), Portworx, Red Hat, Rubrik, Salesforce, Slide, Spanning, Synology, Trilio, Velero, Zerto.

citations.title: Backup to Tape
citations.text:
Backup to Tape

NAKIVO Backup \& Replication provides native tape support for automated tape libraries, including virtual tape libraries (VTLs), as well as for standalone tape drives.

Backup to Tape is the process of backing up critical data to a tape cartridge. In practice, backing up to tape involves creating a backup, storing it in a Backup Repository, and then transferring it to a tape cartridge for long\-term retention. NAKIVO Backup \& Replication supports backups of VMware, Hyper\-V, Nutanix AHV, Amazon EC2, and physical machine workloads. These backups can be sent to physical tape libraries or VTLs for storage.

NAKIVO Backup \& Replication also supports the Disk Staging (D2D2T) backup strategy, in which disk storage is used as an intermediate stage in the backup process before the backup is ultimately written to tape. This approach improves performance and reliability while retaining the benefits of tape\-based storage.  
In NAKIVO Backup \& Replication, the process of storing backups to tape consists of two stages:

**Stage 1** – creating backups and storing them in the Backup Repository:

[

![](/media/bb009ac8-7822-4516-8846-372c8d5f5009/4715112b045d.png)

> **Figure:** A diagram showing a backup architecture with a SOURCE HOST containing three VMs, connected to a TRANSPORTER, which is linked to a BACKUP REPOSITORY. The DIRECTOR manages the TRANSPORTER, indicated by a bidirectional arrow.

](../Resources/Images/Tape+Backup/Tape Backup.png)

**Stage 2** – copying backups from the repository to the tape library:

[

![](/media/bb009ac8-7822-4516-8846-372c8d5f5009/433fd5334a46.png)

> **Figure:** A diagram showing the architecture of a backup system with four components: DIRECTOR (a gear icon), TRANSPORTER (a chip icon), BACKUP REPOSITORY (a database icon), and TAPE LIBRARY (a tape icon). The DIRECTOR communicates bidirectionally with the TRANSPORTER, which connects unidirectionally to both the BACKUP REPOSITORY and the TAPE LIBRARY.

](../Resources/Images/Tape+Backup/Tape Backup_1.png)

[Recovering from tape](Recovery-From-Tape.htm) is the reverse of backing up: the backups stored on the tape cartridges are first recovered to the Backup Repository and then recovered using NAKIVO Backup \& Replication's tools.

Before you back up/recover to/from tape (physical or VTL), you need to [configure](../Settings/Tape/Tape.htm) NAKIVO Backup \& Replication by adding tape libraries, discovering cartridges, etc.  

The Native Tape support is fully integrated into NAKIVO Backup \& Replication solution and allows you to administer all backup and restore operations on tapes directly from the application's user interface. Saving data on tapes presents you with the same data managing options as disk repositories: you can store full and incremental backups, apply user\-defined retention settings to the archived data, select restore points and so on.

NAKIVO Backup \& Replication supports Linear Tape\-Open tape libraries and standalone tape drives starting from generation 3 (LTO3\) or later as well as VTL. Using the solution, you can discover not only tape libraries and standalone devices, but also the tape cartridges in those devices.

> **Note**
>   
> For best performance, ensure all tape cartridges in robotic libraries have barcodes. Barcodes are optional for standalone devices.

Also, any changes to the tape infrastructure (moving or removing cartridges, changing their order, etc.) made by any other means (i.e. manually or via command line) rather than with NAKIVO Backup \& Replication is the user's responsibility, since the system is unaware of such changes.

NAKIVO Backup \& Replication supports writing/reading backups to/from discovered tape cartridges, as well as other operations, like moving cartridges between slots, erasing, scanning, etc.

The table below provides a description of some of the tape\-related terms:

Create a Tape Manager[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#create-a-tape-manager)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Prerequisites[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#prerequisites)
Before creating Tape Manager in Storware Backup & Recovery you need to install Tape Manager service on machine with tape library. You can download Tape Manager RPM file from [Storware Repository](https://repo.storware.eu/storware/current/)
.

Example:

Copy

    rpm -ivh sbr-tape-manager-x.x.x-x.el8.x86_64.rpm 

Tape Manager service by default runs on ports 8686 (HTTP) and 8787 (HTTPS).

Udev configuration[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#udev-configuration)
For correct discover tape library and drives, is required to configure udev rule. Tape drives order in udev should be the same as drives order in the tape library.

citations.title: Tape Pools
citations.text:
Tape Pools
Create Tape Manager[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#create-tape-manager)

To create Tape Manager, log in to Storware Backup & Recovery and go to `Backup Destinations` -> `Tape Pools` -> `Tape Managers` tab and click `Create` button. You need to specify:

*   Name of Tape Manager instance

*   URL of Tape Manager service

    Copy

        http://IP_of_tape_manager:8686
        or
        https://IP_of_tape_manager:8787

*   Node Config for scanning Inventory of Tape Manager service

*   Secret Key generated by Tape Manager service

Secret Key is generated during first startup of Tape Manager service. It’s located in service directory `/opt/vprotect/tapemanager/config/secretKey.jwk`. In Storware Backup & Recovery you need to provide the value from “k” property without quotation marks.

Example of secretKey.jwk:

Copy

    {
        "kty": "oct",
        "k": "ZtOPeOvdJq0M62ka2I8BJmUi7GJbCVEpJyxAsOs4JO0=",
        "alg": "HS256"
    }

If you remove this file, new secret api key will be generated at startup of Tape Manager service.

Inventory Synchronization[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#inventory-synchronization)
After creating Tape Manager you need to run Inventory Synchronization to fetch all Tape Libraries, Tape Drives and Tapes from Tape Manager.

Managing Tape Manager[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#managing-tape-manager)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In Tape Manager details you have access to all Tape Libraries, Tape Drives and Tapes associated with this Tape Manager.

Tape Libraries[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#tape-libraries)
In Tape Libraries View you have access to all Tape Libraries synced from Tape Manager service. Currently you can only browse or delete Libraries from this view.

Tape Drives[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#tape-drives)
In Tape Drives View you have access to all Tape Drives synced from Tape Manager service. Currently you can only browse or delete Drives from this view.

Tapes[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#tapes)
In Tapes View you have access to all Tapes synced from Tape Manager service. In this view, you can:

*   Browse Tapes.

*   Delete them (this operation will result in loosing all data stored on them).

*   If they are not present you can change their name (barcode).

*   If they are not present you can assign them to location where they are physically stored.

Locations[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#locations)
Locations are physical places where you store Tapes when they are outside of Tape Library.

To create Location you need to specify name with an optional description.

You can only assign **not present** tapes to Location. During Tape Manager Inventory Sync Task if a Tape that is in Location will be present again it will be automatically removed from Location.

Notes and limitations[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#notes-and-limitations)
Only environments with a single Tape Library per Tape Manager are supported. Drives visible by the operating system need to be in the same order as drives in Tape Library.

Create a Tape Pool[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#create-a-tape-pool)

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Prerequisites[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#prerequisites-1)
Before creating a Tape Pool Backup destination you need to:

*   Have working Tape Manager.

*   Do a Tape Inventory Synchronization.

Setup[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#setup)
To create Tape Pool you need to specify:

*   Name of Backup Destination.

*   Tape Manager.

*   Tape Library from previously selected Tape Manager.

*   Tape Drive from selected Library.

*   One or more Tapes from selected Library.

Initialization[](https://docs.storware.eu/backup-destinations/tape-pools#initialization)
After creating or updating a Tape Pool Backup Destination, wait for the Backup Destination Initialization Task to complete. This Task will initialize all Tapes associated with this Tape Pool. After that, your Backup Destination is ready to use.

citations.title: Backup to Tape
citations.text:
Backup to Tape

If you want to store your Veeam Plug\-In backups on tape, you can copy backups from a primary backup repository to a tape library by means of backup to tape jobs. From tape, you can later restore the backups to a backup repository for further database recovery operations.

Getting Started

Before you copy Veeam Plug\-In backups to tape, you must complete the following preparation steps:

1. Add a tape server to your backup infrastructure. For details, see [Tape Servers](tape_servers.html).
2. Add media pools for full and incremental backups to your backup infrastructure. For details, see [Creating Media Pools](creating_custom_media_pools.html).
3. Create a Veeam Plug\-In backup. Make sure that your Veeam Plug\-In backups meet the requirements listed in section [Considerations and Limitations](#limitations).

After that, you can create a backup to tape job to make a copy of your database data in the tape library. For details, see [Creating Backup to Tape Jobs](creating_backup_to_tape_jobs.html).

Considerations and Limitations

Before you copy Veeam Plug\-In backups to tape, consider the following:

* Backups that you plan to copy to tape must be created with Veeam Plug\-In version 12 or later.
* Veeam Backup \& Replication supports the following tape libraries for Veeam Plug\-In backups: Linear Tape\-Open (LTO) and IBM 3592 (Jaguar). You can use physical libraries, standalone drives, virtual tape libraries, and partitions of physical or virtual tape libraries added to the Veeam backup infrastructure.
* Veeam Backup \& Replication supports the following tape connections: direct connection over Fibre Channel (FC), Serial Attached SCSI (SAS) or SCSI, and remote connection over iSCSI or switched FC fabric.
* Backup to tape for Veeam Plug\-Ins does not support GFS retention.

How Backup to Tape Works

The backup to tape job consists of the following steps:

1. Veeam Backup \& Replication will scan the source backup repository searching for Veeam Plug\-In backups.

As a source for the backup to tape job, Veeam Backup \& Replication can use any Veeam Plug\-In backups created in standalone or managed mode, including backups produced by backup copy jobs.

1. Veeam Backup \& Replication will generate the backup job metadata file (.VACM) and copy it to the tape library. This approach ensures that backup files stored on tape are not left without the central metadata even if the backup session fails.
2. After that, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy the backup data files (.VAB) and their backup metadata files (.VASM).

Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy all closed backup files stored in the repository and skip backup files that are not yet closed. For details on when Veeam Plug\-In for Oracle RMAN closes backup files, see [Reuse of Backup Files](rman_bfiles.html#bfiles_reuse).

Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy backup files to tape at the database server level: one tape drive will write backup files of one server at a time. If your tape library has multiple tape drives and you set parallel processing in the media pool and application backup policy configurations, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy backup files of multiple servers in parallel — one server per tape drive. Backup files of the same server are never copied in parallel. This approach ensures that a single backup job metadata file is always created on tape.

Depending on the backup type, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy the Veeam Plug\-In backup files to tape in the following way:

* In case of a full backup, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy all closed Veeam Plug\-In backup files detected in the source repository and store them on tape.

* In case of an incremental backup, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy only those Veeam Plug\-In backup files that were closed since the previous backup to tape job run and store them on tape.

With full and incremental backups on tape, you can create virtual full backups. In case of Veeam Plug\-In backups, there are no synthetic operations during the virtual full creation: Veeam Backup \& Replication copies all closed Veeam Plug\-In backup files stored in the source backup repository and writes them to tape as a new full backup. If you want to create such backups, make sure that the export of virtual full backups is enabled even for backup chains with periodic fulls in the settings of the backup to tape job. To learn more, see [Choose Media Pool for Full Backups](backup_to_tape_pools.html).

How Restore from Tape Works

To restore a Veeam Plug\-In backup from tape, you must perform 2 operations:

1. Restore the backup from tape to a disk\-based backup repository.

If your tape library has multiple tape drives and you set parallel processing in the media pool and application backup policy configurations, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy backup files of multiple servers in parallel — one server per tape drive. Backup files of the same server are never copied in parallel. This approach ensures that a single backup job metadata file is always created on tape.

Depending on the backup type, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy the Veeam Plug\-In backup files to tape in the following way:

* In case of a full backup, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy all closed Veeam Plug\-In backup files detected in the source repository and store them on tape.

* In case of an incremental backup, Veeam Backup \& Replication will copy only those Veeam Plug\-In backup files that were closed since the previous backup to tape job run and store them on tape.

With full and incremental backups on tape, you can create virtual full backups. In case of Veeam Plug\-In backups, there are no synthetic operations during the virtual full creation: Veeam Backup \& Replication copies all closed Veeam Plug\-In backup files stored in the source backup repository and writes them to tape as a new full backup. If you want to create such backups, make sure that the export of virtual full backups is enabled even for backup chains with periodic fulls in the settings of the backup to tape job. To learn more, see [Choose Media Pool for Full Backups](backup_to_tape_pools.html).

How Restore from Tape Works

To restore a Veeam Plug\-In backup from tape, you must perform 2 operations:

1. Restore the backup from tape to a disk\-based backup repository.

citations.title: Backup copy targets
citations.text:
Backup copy targets

Before adding the tape backup copy target, review these requirements and considerations.

Unitrends supports copying to tape from Recovery MAX appliances and from select Recovery Series appliance models. Tape is not supported with ION/ION\+ and Unitrends Backup virtual appliances.

The following requirements must be met before setting up a tape target on a Recovery Series or Recovery MAX appliance:

| System | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Recovery Series or Recovery MAX appliance | The appliance must be licensed with the advanced archiving (ADX) feature. Check for ADX in the Feature String under Configure \> Appliances \> Edit \> License. |
| Tape device | ●   The tape device must be either SCSI, SAS, or Fibre Channel. ●   The tape device must be configured as described in [Configuring the tape device on the Unitrends appliance](#Configuring_the_tape_device_on_the_Unitrends_appliance). ●   The tape or set of tapes must have adequate space to store the data being copied. If the copy does not fit, the job fails. ●   If using tape barcodes, your tape device must have a barcode reader and tapes must have valid barcode labels. |

Before copying to tape, note these additional considerations:

| Tape feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Multi\-tape devices | The following considerations apply to devices with multiple tapes: ●   All tapes configured for the backup copy job must be rotated as a set as the job writes across all tapes.  ●   All tapes must be available to recover data from the backup copy. ●   To recover data from tapes that do NOT have barcode labels, the tapes must be loaded into the same slot position as when the backup copy was written. ●   For tapes that do NOT have barcode labels, it is strongly recommended that you develop a labeling system to help you manage the tapes. Prior to pulling a tape without a barcode, note its slot number. When you pull a set of tapes, be sure to physically label each tape with the slot number and other identifying information for speedy recovery. ●   If your tapes have barcodes, there are no special procedures when recovering from a backup copy. The appliance automatically uses the barcode during the recovery process. If you have moved tapes with barcodes to different slots, the appliance reads the barcodes to determine the location of the tapes. |
| Multiple tape drives | The following considerations apply to devices with multiple tape drives: ●   Even though you can connect multiple tape drives, the appliance only uses one tape drive for backup copies.  ●   You can connect an autochanger that has multiple tape drives; however, only one drive can be enabled for use by the appliance. |
| Tape devices with barcodes | On tape devices that support barcodes, the appliance recognizes the barcode as soon as you insert the tape into the library. |

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)](#)[To connect the tape device](#)

 1\.  Connect the tape drive or autochanger to the Unitrends appliance using a SAS or LVD SCSI cable. If using a LVD SCSI cable, ensure that a SCSI bus terminator is installed on the tape device according to the vendor’s documentation.

 2\.  Once connected, power on the tape device. 

 3\.  Once the tape device initializes, log in to the Unitrends appliance and reboot by selecting Configure \> Appliance \> Edit \> Shutdown/Restart (on the General tab). This enables the appliance to discover the tape device.

[

![Connect Tape 1](/media/e5b642ef-1c0c-4870-b5e0-36bf342bd06c/c0bf6d9e6782c048.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Unitrends appliance management interface showing the 'Configure' section with the 'Appliances' tab selected. The 'Edit Appliance' dialog is open, and a 'Shutdown appliance' modal is displayed, prompting for the root password with options to Shutdown, Restart, or Cancel.

](../Resources/Images/Config_copy_targets/connect-tape-1.png)

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)](#)[Configuring the tape device on the Unitrends appliance](#)

This section discusses how to configure your tape device after it has been connected to the appliance. Tape drives and autochangers must be configured before you can begin copying backups. After configuring the tape drive and autochanger, you must prepare the tape media. The media can be prepared manually or automatically by the Unitrends appliance. 

Tape configuration procedures are given below. Use the procedure that applies to your tape device. (Use only one procedure. The autochanger procedure configures both the changer and the tape drive.)
