Overview
[\#](#about-cloud-backup-for-google-workspace)About Cloud Backup for Google Workspace

Cloud Backup for Google Workspace can protect your Google Workspace data (including Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Contacts, Chat, and shared drives), Google Vault data (including Gmail, Drive, and shared drives), Google Directory (users and groups), and Google Classroom data, by offering automatic backups and flexible restores/exports that enable fast recovery from errors, attacks, and failures.

[\#](#subscription-and-licensing-information)Subscription and Licensing Information
To find out how AvePoint charges for Cloud Backup for Google Workspace, refer to [Subscription and Licensing Information](/licensing/google-workspace-subscriptions.html).

NOTESuspended users and Archived users are not in the scope of counting licenses for charge.

[\#](#google-workspace-google-directory-and-google-classroom)Google Workspace, Google Directory, and Google Classroom
Google Workspace, Google Directory, and Google Classroom are individual modules. To use each module, ensure that your organization has purchased the module in the subscription of Cloud Backup for Google Workspace. Suppose your organization has Google Workspace, Google Directory, and Google Classroom modules. In that case, the following pages distinguish these modules via the **Google Workspace**, **Google Directory**, and **Google Classroom** tabs: **Dashboard**, **Protection**, **Restore**, and **Subscription**.

NOTEThe following functions are only available for organizations with the Google Workspace module in the subscription of Cloud Backup for Google Workspace: **Data** **management**, **End\-user restore** (for ReCenter), and **Unusual** **activities analysis**.

For more information on the data types that are supported or unsupported, refer to the [Support Lists](/google-backup/support-lists/index.html).

[\#](#google-vault-protection)Google Vault Protection
Protection for the Google Vault data is an addon in the Google Workspace module. If your organization needs the protection for Vault, contact the AvePoint representative to enable this feature in your tenant’s subscription to Cloud Backup for Google Workspace. Once the Vault protection has been enabled, the following pages will display the **Google Workspace** and **Vault** tabs to distinguish the two protections: **Dashboard**, **Protection**, and **Restore**. For additional details, see [Vault Data Protection](/google-backup/about-cloud-backup-for-google-workspace/vault-data-protection.html).

[\#](#integration-with-ava)Integration with Ava
Cloud Backup for Google Workspace offers integration with Ava, an AvePoint virtual assistant that offers instructions and answers to your questions. Note that administrators can control who can access Ava in a tenant’s environment. For more information, refer to the [Control Ava Access](/configuration-and-deployment/administration/control-ava-access.html) section in the AvePoint Online Services User Guide.

[\#](#helpful-notes)Helpful Notes
Note the following:

* ReCenter is a portal where invited Google users can restore or export their data that is protected by Cloud Backup for Google Workspace, as well as view and download job reports. You can click **Go to** **ReCenter** **portal** to access the portal. For additional details, refer to the [ReCenter User Guide](/recenter/about-recenter.html). Recovering Google Classroom data hasn’t been supported in ReCenter.
* When a backup job needs to back up a large number of objects, to not affect the next backups, AvePoint Cloud Backup for Google Workspace can split the backup into sub jobs to shorten the time of the backup job.
* For files and folders in drives or shared drives, if a file/folder was backed up before it has been moved to a new location, without any changes to its content, the file/folder couldn’t be backed up again in the new location.

[\#](#language-support)Language Support
Cloud Backup for Google Workspace supports the following languages: English, French, German, Japanese, and Korean.

citations.title: Preparing the environment for successful Google Workspace backups and restore
citations.text:
Preparing the environment for successful Google Workspace backups and restore
1\. What is Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) in your environment?

Google Workspace plans provide a custom email for your business and include collaboration tools like Gmail, Calendar, Meet, Chat, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Sites and more.

2\. Why is it essential to perform regular backups of Google Workspace?
Performing regular backups of Google workspace workloads is crucial to ensure data protection and disaster recovery. Backups help safeguard against accidental deletions, data corruption, cyberattacks, and other potential issues resulting in data loss.

3\. What data and components does Druva backup from Google Workspace?
Druva backups Gmail, Google Drive and Shared Drives

Please find more information below :

1. [Protect Google Workspace Apps \- Druva Documentation](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8367746-protect-google-workspace-apps)
2. [Protect Google Shared Drives data using Druva inSync \- Druva Documentation](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8367757-protect-google-shared-drives-data-using-druva-insync)

4\. Can you explain the backup workflow for Google Workspace?
The backup workflow for Google Drive/Gmail in Druva inSync involves the following steps:

1\. Create a SaaSApps profile and enable Google Drive/Gmail for backup

2\. Identification and selection of Google Drive/Gmail or entities for backup.

3\. Map users to the profile

4\. Schedule or manually run the backup

5\. Availability of backup data for restore operations as per retention policies.

5\. What are the prerequisites before configuring Druva for Google workspace backups?
Before configuring Druva for Google workspace backups, ensure the following prerequisites:

1. A valid subscription to Druva inSync and appropriate licensing for Google Workspace
2. Support Article : [Protect Google Shared Drives data using Druva inSync \- Druva Documentation](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8367757-protect-google-shared-drives-data-using-druva-insync)
3. An account with Licensed Google Super Admin privileges for initial configuration.
4. Configure Cloud Key Management to store the encryption Key.
5. Configure a profile to protect GDrive/Gmail data
6. Associate and add users to GDrive/Gmail\-enabled Profile
7. To configure the Shared Drive backups: [Protect Google Shared Drives data using Druva inSync \- Druva Documentation](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8367757-protect-google-shared-drives-data-using-druva-insync)

citations.text:
Architecture

[Enterprise](https://docs.baculasystems.com/BCBEComparison/index.html)
Bacula Enterprise Only

This solution is **only** available for Bacula Enterprise. For subscription inquiries, please reach out to <sales@baculasystems.com>.

**Bacula Enterprise** Google Workspace Plugin is using several Google Workspace APIs
to perform almost all of its operations. Therefore, the plugin is working at the
maximum granularity that the service provides.

![Google Workspace APIs](/media/b9ac1f1c-27e2-4114-94e6-1e84328c9499/feb13923fff7.png)

> **Figure:** A list of Google Workspace developer products, including Admin Console, Classroom, Cloud Identity, Cloud Search, Contacts & profiles, Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Chat, Google Docs, Google Drive, Google Forms, Google Keep, Google Sheets, Google Sites (Classic), Google Slides, Google Tasks, Google Vault, and Google Workspace, each with its corresponding icon.

Google Workspace APIs

All the information is gotten using HTTP requests to Google Cloud from the
FD where the plugin is installed.

The plugin will contact a **Google Cloud Platform application** that needs to be **manually created and configured**
before using the plugin. It will serve as a bridge to download the required
data or objects during backup time and send them to the Storage Daemon.
Conversely, the plugin will receive them from an SD and perform uploads as needed
during a restore operation.

citations.title: Protecting Google Workspace data
citations.text:
Protecting Google Workspace data

This feature is not available for tenants in Compliance mode. For more information, see [Compliance mode](compliance-mode.html).

What does Google Workspace protection mean?
* Cloud\-to\-cloud backup and recovery of Google Workspace user data (Gmail mailboxes, Calendars, Contacts, Google Drives) and Google Workspace Shared drives.
* Granular recovery of emails, files, contacts, and other items.
* Support for several Google Workspace organizations and cross\-organization recovery.
* Optional notarization of the backed\-up files by means of the Ethereum blockchain database. When enabled, you can prove that a file is authentic and unchanged since it was backed up.
* Optional full\-text search. When enabled, you can search emails by their content.
* Up to 5,000 items (mailboxes, Google Drives, and Shared drives) per company can be protected without performance degradation.
* Backed\-up data is automatically compressed and it uses less space on the backup location than on its original location. The compression level for cloud\-to\-cloud backups is fixed and corresponds to the Normal level of non\-cloud\-to\-cloud backups. For more information about these levels, see [Compression level](compression-level.html).

citations.title: Adding Individual or All Shared Drives
citations.text:
Adding Individual or All Shared Drives
Adding Individual or All Shared Drives to Google Drive Backup Content

You can add the individual or all shared drives to the Google Drive backup content. The shared drives that you add are included in backups of the app.

Add all shared drives so that all shared drives, including new shared drives that are automatically discovered, are included in backups of the app.

Start the Configuration Wizard
1. From the Command Center navigation pane, go to **Protect \> Google Workspace**.

The Google Workspace **Overview** page appears.
2. On the **Apps** tab, click the Google Drive app.

The **Overview** page of the app appears.

Configure Content
1. On the **Content** tab, at the upper\-right area of the page, click **Add**.

The **Configure Content** page appears.
2. Select **Add content to backup**, and then click **NEXT**.

The **Type** page of **Add Content** configuration wizard appears.

2. Click **NEXT**.

The **Content** page of the configuration wizard appears.

Select the Users

2. Click **NEXT**.

The **Google Workspace plan** page of the configuration wizard appears.

Select the Google Workspace Plan

Summary
1. Review the selected shared drives details.
2. Click **SUBMIT**.

citations.title: Google Workspace
citations.text:
Google Workspace
Google Workspace

Google Workspace is a cloud-based productivity suite that provides email services, file storage, and collaboration capabilities as SaaS applications. Google Workspace includes Gmail, Google Drive, and other services commonly used in enterprise environments. Cohesity Cloud Services provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective data protection solution for the following Google Workspace applications:

- l Gmail
- l Google Drive

Cohesity Cloud Services securely connects to your Google Workspace domain using a service account with domain-wide delegation. The service account is authorized through OAuth 2.0 scopes granted by a Google Workspace administrator. Cohesity Cloud Services protects the selected data across your Google Workspace domain, including Gmail and Google Drive. The backed-up Google Workspace data is stored in the Google Cloud region that you select during registration.

In case of data loss or corruption, recovery can be performed to the original location or to an alternate location (new location). The alternate location can be within the same Google Workspace domain or a different one, but it must already be registered as a source with Cohesity Cloud Services.

For Gmail recovery, you can perform a full recovery of Gmail mailboxes, or you can perform granular recovery of individual items within Gmail mailboxes. For Google Drive, you can perform a full recovery of individual drives, or you can perform granular recovery of individual items within the drives.

Protecting Google Workspace data using Cohesity Cloud Services involves the following steps:

- l Prerequisites: Complete all prerequisites and review all considerations before you begin.
- l Source Registration: Register your Google Workspace instance as a source with Cohesity Cloud Services.
- l Backup: Configure backup protection by either applying an existing backup policy that defines the backup schedule, retention settings, and other details, or creating a new policy based on your backup requirements. Then run the backups.
- l Recovery: Recover data in case of accidental deletion or corruption to the original or an alternate location (new location).

citations.title: Google Workspace Requirements
citations.text:
Google Workspace Requirements
Scopes

Note: The Scopes related to Contacts, Calendars, and Tasks are applicable only after the protection of Contacts, Calendars, and Tasks is supported in the next release.

The scopes required for Google Workspace authentication are described as follows:

- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly Read-only access to Gmail for backup.

- l users.getProfile: Read mailbox history ID and email address for Gmail backup planning.
- l users.labels.list: Enumerate labels so Gmail backup captures label metadata.
- l users.messages.list/users.messages.get: List and download messages (and attachments) during Gmail backup.
- l Batch users.messages.get: Efficiently fetch many message bodies during Gmail backup.
- l users.history.list: Drive incremental Gmail backup from the last history checkpoint.
- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify
- Read/write Gmail access for recovery (insert, label, trash; not permanent delete).
- l users.messages.insert: Recover emails into the target mailbox without sending them.
- l users.messages.modify: Apply recovered label IDs to inserted messages.
- l users.messages.trash: Move conflicting or replaced messages to trash during recovery.
- l users.labels.create/users.labels.update: Recreate or update labels on the recovery target.
- l users.labels.list/users.messages.get: Map existing labels and dedupe messages before recovery writes.
- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly

Read-only Drive access for backup and entity hierarchy.

- l about.get (Drive v3/v2): Read user Drive root and quota/usage for backup and entity hierarchy.
- l drives.list/drives.get: Discover and describe shared drives during backup and hierarchy.
- l files.list/files.get: Enumerate and read file metadata during Drive backup.
- l files.export/media download: Download native Google docs and binary file content for backup.
- l revisions.list/revisions.get: Capture latest revision metadata and content where required.
- l permissions.list: Back up shared-drive ACLs and pick impersonation users for access.
- l changes.getStartPageToken/changes.list: Run incremental Drive backup from the change feed.
- l files.list (size fields): Estimate shared-drive size for entity hierarchy reporting.

- l files.get (script recovery setup): Resolve Apps Script Drive files when creating the Script client.
- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive
- Full Drive access for recovery writes.
- l files.create/files.update: Create and overwrite files/folders (including media upload) on recovery.
- l permissions.create: Recover sharing permissions on My Drive and shared drives.
- l files.get/files.list: Locate existing targets and verify recovered items after write.
- l drives.get/permissions.list: Access shared-drive metadata while recovering into shared drives.
- l about.get: Confirm recovery target Drive identity and capacity before writes.
- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.scripts

Modify Google Apps Script file behavior via Drive.

- l Drive Apps Script file create/update paths: Allow Drive recovery to manage Google Apps Script files on the target.
- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/script.projects
- Apps Script API access to project content.
- l projects.updateContent: Overwrite Apps Script project source when Drive conversion recovery is required.
- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly
- Read-only Calendar access for backup.
- l calendarList.list: List calendars to back up for the user.
- l events.list (including syncToken): Full and incremental Calendar event backup.
- l https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar

Full Calendar access for recovery.

- l calendars.insert/calendars.patch: Recreate and update secondary calendars on recovery.
- l calendarList.patch: Recover calendar list properties (color, selected, etc.).
- l events.insert/events.import: Create or import recovered events into the target calendar.
- l events.patch: Update existing events during recovery overwrite/merge.
- l events.get/events.list: Deduplicate and verify events (iCalUID/extended

properties) before write.

citations.title: Google Workspace
citations.text:
Google Workspace

Rubrik Security Cloud protects your Google Workspace workloads, such as Google
 Drive and Gmail data, for your organization.

As organizations expand their use of collaboration suites such as Google Workspace, they
 face new challenges in protecting important data in applications such as Google Drive
 and Gmail.

Complex deployments can increase the risk of data integrity issues, potentially leading
 to data loss and revenue loss due to cyber incidents or accidental deletions. The native
 tools provided by Google, such as Google Vault, have limitations. These include a strict
 30\-day retention period, no point\-in\-time recovery through snapshots, and limited
 options for restoring individual files, folders, and emails. While Google offers a
 secure platform, your organization is responsible for protecting its applications and
 data.

Rubrik Security Cloud (RSC) offers a solution to these challenges with
 a simplified, SaaS\-based platform that secures and automates data protection for Google
 Workspace workloads. By utilizing a global policy model known as an SLA Domain, RSC automates backup and recovery schedules, ensuring your data is
 protected with secure, immutable backups. This method reduces management complexity and
 aligns data protection with your business needs. 

Protecting Google Workspace workloads with RSC involves a structured
 approach that ensures comprehensive and consistent data protection policies across your
 cloud infrastructure. This approach breaks down the tasks into three main categories:
 authorization, configuration, and protection.

**The following table provides an overview of these task categories and the
 associated activities.**

| Task category | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Authorization | You grant RSC secure access to your Google Workspace  organization using Domain\-Wide Delegation (DWD) and OAuth\-integrated  workflows that follow Google security best practices. |
| Configuration | You set up SLA Domains to automatically protect Google Drive and  Gmail data according to your business goals. SLA Domains enable you to  define and manage data protection policies consistently across your  Google Workspace hierarchy, including at the Organization,  Organizational Unit (OU), and individual user levels. |
| Protection | You enforce data security by assigning SLA Domains to Google  Workspace workloads. RSC provides quick recovery options  for your workloads, including Google Drive files, Shared Drives, and  Gmail messages. |

citations.title: Key features for Google Workspace protection
citations.text:
Key features for Google Workspace protection
Recovery options

| Recovery option | Description | Detailed workflow options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entire Drive restore | Restores the full contents of a My Drive or a Shared Drive from a  point\-in\-time snapshot. The destination can be the original location  or the drive of an alternate user. | * Restore location: Restoring to the Google Drive of the  original user or to the Google Drive of a different  user. * Restore method: In\-place overwrite, in\-place skip, or  restore to a new folder. |
| File and folder restore | Searches for and restores specific files or folders from a  selected snapshot. You can restore to the original location or a new  folder within the original drive or the drive of an alternate  user. | * Restore location: Restoring to the Google Drive of the  original user or to the Google Drive of a different  user. * Restore method: Restore to the same path or restore to a new  folder. |
| Gmail recovery | Restores individual emails, conversation threads, or all Gmail,  Calendar, and Contacts data from a point\-in\-time snapshot. RSC uses an indexed search to help you locate  specific communications quickly. | * Restore location: Restoring to the inbox of the original  user or to the inbox of a different user. * Restore method: Assigning a new label to group recovered  items. If an item already exists, RSC  updates the labels and skips the content transfer. |
| Google Calendar recovery | Restores individual events or entire calendars from a  point\-in\-time snapshot. RSC protects calendar data  together with Gmail and manages recovery from the Gmail inventory  through the same restore wizard. RSC supports  calendar and event browsing with search and advanced  filters. | * Restore location: Restoring to the calendar of the original  user or to the calendar of a different user. * Restore method: Restoring specific calendars and events or  the full calendar. You can optionally restore a calendar  with a new name. |
| Google Contacts recovery | Restores connection contacts, contact groups, and other contacts.  RSC protects contacts data together with Gmail  and manages recovery from the Gmail inventory using the same restore  wizard. RSC supports contact browsing and search  across contacts and contact groups. | * Restore location: Restoring to the contact list of the  original user or to the contact list of a different  user. * Restore method: Selectively restoring individual contacts  and contact groups. You can restore other contacts as a  complete set in a single operation. |
| Mass recovery | Restores Google Drive and Gmail, Calendar, and Contacts data for  multiple users, multiple shared drives, organizational units,  Google  groups, or the entire application from a  point\-in\-time snapshot. Mass recovery requires a separate license.  For more information, see [Google Workspace mass recovery](gws_mass_recovery.html "Mass recovery restores Google Drive data along with Gmail, Calendar, and Contacts data from a point-in-time snapshot. Depending on the workload, mass recovery restores data for multiple users, multiple shared drives, specific organizational units, Google groups, or the entire Google Workspace application."). | * Restore location: Restoring to the original user accounts or  locations only. |
| Prioritized recovery | Restores the most recently modified data first during a recovery  at the Organizational Unit (OU),  Google  groups, or application level, before recovering  the remaining data.Note: Prioritized recovery requires a separate  license. For more information, see [Google Workspace prioritized recovery](gws_prioritized_recovery.html "Prioritized recovery enables you to first restore high-priority data during a recovery at the Organizational Unit (OU), Google groups, or application level, before recovering the remaining data."). | * Restore scope: Restores at the Organizational Unit (OU),  Google  groups, or application level for Google  Drive and Gmail, Calendar, and Contacts data. * Recovery priority: Recover data from the most recent days  first, then continue incrementally, and optionally perform a  full recovery of all remaining data. |

citations.title: Create Google Workspace Backup Policies
citations.text:
Create Google Workspace Backup Policies

This page is for Data Protection.##### Who can use this feature

 Anyone with these permissions: Manage backup policies

A Google Workspace backup policy protects each user’s Gmail mailbox and Drive in a workspace you’ve connected to Eon.
You can also back up Google Groups and shared drives from the same workspace.

This article explains how to create a backup policy for a Google Workspace.

Create a backup policy for Google Workspace
You can create a backup policy from the [Backup Policies page](https://console.eon.io/settings/backup-policies) in the Eon console.
To get started, click **Create Backup Policy**.

citations.title: Create Google Workspace Backup Policies
citations.text:
Create Google Workspace Backup Policies
Create a backup policy for Google Workspace > Before you start

Before you create a Google Workspace backup policy, make sure you’ve connected the workspace you want to back up.
See [Google Workspace: Connect Source Workspaces](/data-protection/saas-workloads/google-workspace/connections/connect-source-workspaces) for instructions.

[1](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/google-workspace/create-google-workspace-backup-policies#choose-the-backup-policy-type)### Choose the backup policy type

For **Backup source**, choose **SaaS application**.

In **Apply policy to**, choose **Google Workspace**.
For more information on backup policy types, see [Backup policy types](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/backup-policy-overview#backup-policy-types).

These settings can’t be changed after you continue.

Click **Continue**.

[2](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/google-workspace/create-google-workspace-backup-policies#choose-the-workspace)### Choose the workspace

In the **Google Workspace** step, select the workspace you want to back up.
The list shows only workspaces connected as a Google Workspace source workspace, and marks a workspace already covered by another policy as **Already in a policy**.

The footer of this step shows the policy name and labels.
Optionally, add labels to the policy to allow filtering.
You add and remove labels next to **Backup policy name**.

Click  (Add label), type a label, and then press **Enter** or click  .
To remove a label, click the x icon on it.

Click **Next**.

[3](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/google-workspace/create-google-workspace-backup-policies#choose-what-to-back-up)### Choose what to back up

In the **Backup Settings** step, provide a **Backup policy name**, then choose what to back up in the workspace.

Under **Users**, **Back up all organizational units and groups** is on, which backs up every user’s Gmail mailbox and Drive.
To narrow the scope, turn **Back up all organizational units and groups** off and choose what to leave out:

* In **Excluded organization units**, search for and select the organizational units you don’t want to back up.
* In **Excluded groups**, search for and select the groups you don’t want to back up.

A user in an excluded organizational unit or group isn’t backed up, even when they also belong to one you’re backing up.
See [Group and organizational unit exclusions](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/google-workspace/about-google-workspace-backup-policies#group-and-organizational-unit-exclusions) for details.

Then choose whether to back up the other data in the workspace:

* Turn **Back up groups** on to back up your Google Groups, including each group’s settings and membership.
* Turn **Back up shared drives** on to back up the shared drives in the workspace.

Click **Next**.

[4](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/google-workspace/create-google-workspace-backup-policies#set-the-backup-schedule)### Set the backup schedule

Google Workspace backup policies use a single, fixed daily schedule.

In the **Schedules** step, set the start time, the retention period, and the vault to store snapshots in.

Click **Next**.

[5](/data-protection/backup-and-protection/backup-configuration/backup-policies/google-workspace/create-google-workspace-backup-policies#save)### Save

When you’re done, click **Create**.
Your policy begins backing up the workspace according to the configuration you set.

Google Drive Backup, Restore, and Download
Description

Topic
This article explains how to back up your Google Drive (GDrive) and restore or download those backups.

Environment
NinjaOne SaaS Backup

NinjaOne SaaS Backup allows you to perform the following actions with Google Drive data:

* Restore the entire user's Google Drive, a single folder, or a single file.
* Perform a point\-in\-time restore, retrieving data from any date since the backup began.
* Restore data to the same user's Google Drive or another user's Google Drive within the same tenant.

NinjaOne SaaS Backup can only access items stored in the users “My Drive”. NinjaOne SaaS Backup cannot access shared items and so cannot back them up. Shared items, however, will back up from the owner’s user account. Similarly, any other items not specifically within “My Drive” in Google Drive will not be backed up.Select a topic to continue:

Active Backup for Google Workspace Admin Console > Manage Notification Services > Note:

*   Active Backup for Google Workspace Portal needs to be enabled in the Active Backup for Google Workspace admin console for users to restore data by themselves. To allow specific users access to **Active Backup for Google Workspace Portal**, go to **Control Panel** > **Application Privileges**, select **Active Backup for Google Workspace Portal**, and click **Edit** to give permissions.
*   Only users with admin privileges can cancel other users' restoration tasks from Active Backup for Google Workspace admin console.
*   If you wish to copy the backup data to a remote server, use **Snapshot Replication** to create a replication task for the folder that stores the backup data. Do not use **Hyper Backup** to create a backup task or manually move the data. Otherwise, data such as extended attributes may be lost.
*   Block-level deduplication is only supported on shared folders in Btrfs volumes, with the exception of encrypted shared folders. Likewise, single instancing for mail and calendar attachments is only supported on shared folders in Btrfs volumes. For detailed information on the support of the two features, please refer to the table below:

    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Drive | O   | O   |

    | Contacts | X   | X   |
    | Calendar | Attachment only | X   |

*   Files or folders will not be backed up or will be skipped by Active Backup for Google Workspace under the following circumstances:

citations.title: How Datto SaaS Protection works
citations.text:
How Datto SaaS Protection works
Backup process

The following describes and illustrates the steps SaaS Protection performs to backup data. 

1. In a SaaS environment, Microsoft and Google Workspace user data is stored in the cloud, meaning in Microsoft and Google Workspace servers, instead of in the organization's own storage servers.
2. SaaS Protection is granted access to specific API scopes within the organization's M365 or Google Workspace APIs.
3. With the approved API scopes, SaaS Protection is allowed to retrieve the organization's M365 or Google Workspace data.
4. A backup of each end user's service data is stored in Kaseya's own private independent cloud. The cloud consists of multiple data storage centers located in the US, Australia, Canada, Germany, Singapore, and the UK.

The backup process is performed up to *three times a day*. Each backup provides a snapshot of the current state of the data at the time the backup is created. Not only is the content backed up, but the folder structure is backed up and maintained as well.  
[

![](/media/cb4c5f3e-5751-4984-b088-048763d20eb2/a7a93795a8e152ef.png)

> **Figure:** A diagram illustrating the data flow for Datto SaaS Protection. User data from a desktop is sent to Microsoft or Google Workspace Cloud (1), which requests access via API Scopes. Access is granted (2), data is retrieved (3), and then stored in the Datto SaaS Protection Cloud (4).

](../Resources/Images/DSP Backup Process.png)

IMPORTANT  The backed up data is immutable, meaning the data cannot be modified or destroyed in any way. However, backups are pruned (deleted) per the applicable retention period (see the article [Understanding the pricing model](../Administrator_requirements/02_Understanding_the_pricing_model.htm)).

citations.title: What is Datto SaaS Protection?
citations.text:
What is Datto SaaS Protection?
Services that are backed up

Datto SaaS Protection provides data backup capabilities for the following M365 services: OneDrive, Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams. Key points for each service are described in the following table. Other services, such as Microsoft Planner, are not supported.

| Service | Key points |
| --- | --- |
| OneDrive | * All documents in each individual's OneDrive account are backed up. * Regular images files (.jpg) are backed up. * A snapshot is saved for each of the daily backups.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* Image libraries (e.g., smart albums, face/location albums, and UI groups) are not captured. * Shared and group documents are not backed up as this is not allowed by the M365 API. |
| Exchange | Mail:* Shared mailboxes can be backed up. * Group emails can be backed up. * [Microsoft 365 Exchange In\-place archives](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/enable-archive-mailboxes) (Online Archives) can be backed up (see [Protecting Exchange online archives](../Managing_your_organization_environment/protect-online-archives.html)). * Notes in Exchange can be backed up but can only be restored as messages. The messages can be converted back into notes.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example, public folders are not backed up. Contacts:* A user's contacts are backed up.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* Shared and group contacts are not backed up as this is not allowed by the M365 API. * Contact profile pictures are not backed up. * Attachments that are references to OneDrive objects through the API cannot be accessed and backed up.  Calendar:* Team calendar events can be backed up through attendee Exchange backups (each attendee has a copy of the event in their calendar).  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* Shared and group calendars are not backed up as this is not allowed by the M365 API. * Attachments that are references to OneDrive objects through the API cannot be accessed and backed up. |
| SharePoint | The following SharePoint site data is backed up:* Documents * Templates * Assets * Pages * Collections: Microsoft sites that administrators have created that do not fall into the SharePoint Root Site collections. * Lists: Custom lists, document libraries, Wiki page libraries, task lists. To identify a list type, right\-click the three\-dot menu and click **Details**.  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* SharePoint metadata is not backed up. * SharePoint archive data is not backed up because it cannot be accessed from the cold storage tier within SharePoint. * The following are not backed up due to M365 API limitations: contacts, calendars, forms, image libraries, and event lists.  NOTE  Datto SaaS Protection only supports the cloud version known as "M365 SharePoint". Local installations of M365, such as SharePoint 2010 and 2013, are not supported. |
| Teams | Public channels:

  * Content (Team sites, files, and documents) is backed up * Calendar meetings are backed up * Public channel conversation messages are backed up  Private channels (found under SharePoint sites): * Content (Team sites, files, and documents) is backed up * Conversations are backed up  Shared channels: * Content (Team sites, files, and documents) is backed up * Conversations are backed up  Other items may not be backed up due to technical limitations. For example:* 1\-1 chats (e.g., personal direct messages) are not backed up. * Per single Teams message/conversation, 1000 is the maximum number of replies that can be backed up. |

Exchange backup exceptions
If you are using Datto SaaS Protection for M365 and your mail service is disabled or not provisioned, Datto will not be able to back up contacts and calendars.

The Exchange service encompasses mail, contacts, calendars, and tasks but will fail backups if the mail service isn't present because Exchange in 2\.0 is linked directly to Exchange in 1\.0\. 

Exchange backups include online archives only if the online archive backup feature has been enabled for the organization. For details, see [Protecting Exchange online archives](../Managing_your_organization_environment/protect-online-archives.html).

Datto does not back up the rules for M365 Exchange services.

OneNote backup exception
Due to a Microsoft limitation, backup of OneNote sections larger than 2 GB may fail. If you experience this issue, you can opt to split the section into smaller ones that are less than 2 GB.

citations.title: Product overview
citations.text:
Product overview
What is Backup and DR Service?

This page describes Google Cloud Backup and DR Service
capabilities, key benefits, what you can back up, and how it works.

**Note:** Enable [30\-day introductory trial for Backup and DR Service](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/30-day-introductory-trial/intro-trial) to explore a unified, centralized backup solution featuring
immutable backup vaults.

Backup and DR Service is a managed service that provides backup and recovery of
workloads running in Google Cloud. Backup and DR Service provides centralized
management, monitoring, and reporting of day to day backup operations all from
one place. The service supports seamless integration with existing automation
using Terraform and APIs.

Backup and DR Service provides the following capabilities:

* Centralized backup management
* Policy\-based backup management
* Comprehensive monitoring and reporting
* Incremental backups for faster recovery point objective (RPO) and lower total
cost of ownership (TCO)
* Backup storage: the service supports two types of storage for backups:

	+ A backup vault is a Google\-managed secured and isolated storage
	resource, managed by Backup and DR Service. Backup vault provides the
	following features:

		- **Immutability**: your data cannot be changed
		- **Indelibility**: your data cannot be deletedBackup vault storage is supported for Compute Engine instances,
	Cloud SQL, Google Cloud VMware Engine VMs, and self\-managed Oracle and 
	Microsoft SQL Server databases running inside VMs or Bare Metal Solution.
	+ Self\-managed storage refers to storage resources, excluding
	backup vaults, that you can directly access and manage yourself.
	Because you manage the storage, it can be deleted prematurely by any user
	who has sufficient storage permissions.

| Capability | Backup vault storage | Self\-managed storage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Immutable and indelible backups | Yes | No |
| Multi\-region backups | Yes | Yes |
| CMEK\-encrypted backups | Yes\* | Yes |

**Note:** CMEK\-encrypted backups (Backup vault storage) are only supported
for Persistent Disk, Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, and Compute Engine.
Whether using backup vaults or self\-managed storage, you create
backup plans for your data resources that you have to
protect. A backup plan defines when to back up a resource, where to store the
backup, and how long to retain the backups.

Backup vaults
A backup vault is secured and isolated storage, managed by
Backup and DR Service.
A backup vault can store backups in a region or in a multi\-region,
as long as the selected location is
[compatible with the workload location](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/concepts/backup-vault#workload-location-compatibility).

Backup vaults can be created in these
[supported locations](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/concepts/backup-vault#locations).

The minimum enforced retention period, a property of backup vault,
ensures that backups are strongly secured against modification and deletion for
the timeframe you define. You can specify the minimum enforced retention period
up to 99 years.

You create, access, and manage backup vaults using Backup and DR Service in
the Google Cloud console.

For full details on backup vaults, see
[Backup and DR Service backup vault storage](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/concepts/backup-vault).

Self\-managed storage
Self\-managed storage includes Persistent Disk snapshots and backups in
Cloud Storage buckets that are created to store backup data in your
Google Cloud projects.

The Backup and DR appliance management console is an interface for
managing backup to self\-managed storage.

**Note:** To store backups on immutable, indelible storage managed by
Backup and DR Service, see
[backup vault](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/concepts/backup-dr#backup-vaults).

Backup plans
There are some important differences between backup plans created in the
Google Cloud console and backup plans created in the appliance management console,
as described in the following table.

| Supported workload | Backup plan in Google Cloud console | Backup plan in appliance management console |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compute Engine VMs | Yes | Yes |
| Compute Engine disks | Yes | Yes |
| Cloud SQL instances | Yes | No |
| AlloyDB clusters | Yes | No |
| Google Cloud VMware Engine VMs | No | Yes |
| File systems and self\-managed databases, such as Oracle, SQL Server,  SAP HANA, IBM Db2, PostgreSQL, SAP ASE, SAP IQ, and SAP MaxDB, can run  on virtual machines (VMs) or on Bare Metal Solution. | No | Yes |
| Minimum RPO | 4 hours | 15 mins |

Backup plans created in the Google Cloud console use backup vault storage.

citations.title: Product overview
citations.text:
Product overview
Back up Compute Engine instances using the appliance management console

Compute Engine instances can be backed up using the appliance management console
into self\-managed storage, and using the Google Cloud console into backup vaults.

**Note:** You can also back up Compute Engine instances and disks into
backup vaults directly from the Google Cloud console, which is better in
most cases. See
[Back up Compute Engine instances](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/cloud-console/compute/compute-instance-backup).

Back up Google Cloud VMware Engine VMs
Google Cloud VMware Engine VMs are fully supported in the
appliance management console for both backup vault and self\-managed
storage.

Back up self\-managed Oracle and SQL Server databases
Self\-managed Oracle and SQL Server databases are the following databases running
inside a VM or Bare Metal Solution in your project:

* Oracle databases running on Bare Metal Solution, Compute Engine VMs, or
Google Cloud VMware Engine VMs
* SQL Server databases running on Compute Engine or Google Cloud VMware Engine VMs

These self\-managed databases can be backed up from the appliance management console
into backup vaults or into self\-managed storage.

Restore your data
After you have backed up your data, you can restore it to its original location
or to a different location. You can restore entire virtual machines, specific
disks, or individual files. To learn more about how to restore your data, see
the [Restore data overview](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/restore-data/restore-overview).

Pricing
Refer to [Backup and DR Service pricing](https://cloud.google.com/backup-disaster-recovery/pricing)
for pricing details.

What's next
The following quickstart guides can help you begin a backup and recovery
workflow for your application:

* [Protect and recover Compute Engine instances](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/quickstarts/gce-instances-backup-vault).
* [Protect and recover VMware VMs](/backup-disaster-recovery/docs/quickstarts/vmware-backup-recovery).

Spanning (User Guide): Restores specific metadata types (ApprovalProcesses, Classes, Flows, Layouts, Profiles, Reports, etc.) directly in Spanning Backup, with metadata comparison between backups to select and restore items [3][4].
AvePoint (Cloud Backup for Salesforce): Restores metadata types such as AssignmentRules, ApexClass, Flow, CustomObject, PermissionSet, Profile, and more via in-place restore to the original org or out-of-place restore to another organization [7][8].
Veeam (Veeam Data Cloud, Veeam Backup for Salesforce): Restores metadata of deleted objects (Apex classes, reports, dashboards, etc.) via a Restore Metadata wizard to the same or another Salesforce tenant, with dependency ordering requirements [9][10].
GRAX (GRAX): Performs incremental metadata backups of all possible Salesforce metadata objects, stores them in customer-owned storage, and provides a Metadata viewer with version history, comparison, and download of metadata file versions [12][13].
Rubrik (Rubrik Security Cloud): Backs up and recovers Salesforce metadata such as custom objects, layouts, email templates, workflows, and validation rules via a Restore Metadata wizard, with snapshot comparison against the live environment [14][15].
Commvault (Commvault Cloud, CommCell Console): Restores Salesforce metadata to the Salesforce cloud or a file system, with all metadata supported by the Salesforce API supported for restore, including validation before restore [16][17][18].
Druva (Druva): Provides a Metadata tab for comparing metadata between snapshots and restoring or downloading individual metadata files, including metadata restore during full org restore [19][20].
Cohesity (Cloud Protection Service): Backs up and recovers Salesforce data and metadata using permissions such as Modify Metadata through Metadata API Functions for metadata recovery [21][22].
Flosum (Backup and Archive (B&A)): Creates backup metadata restore jobs where you select a backup and choose the Salesforce metadata types to restore [23].
Gearset (Gearset): Restores metadata from data backup jobs via snapshot or Metadata History, with a default comparison metadata filter covering types like Apex classes, flows, custom objects, and more [25][26].
No supporting passage found for: AWS, Acronis, Afi.ai, Arcserve, Arctera, Atempo, Axcient, Bacula, Barracuda, CloudAlly, CloudCasa, Datto, Dell, Eon, Google, HYCU, Hornetsecurity (Altaro), IBM, Keepit, Microsoft, N-Able, Nakivo, NinjaOne (Dropsuite), Portworx, Red Hat, Salesforce, Slide, Storware, Synology, Trilio, Unitrends, Velero, Zerto.

citations.text:
Restoring metadata

Spanning offers restore of specific metadata types, making it easy to 
restore metadata directly in Spanning Backup. The following metadata types are restorable in Spanning Backup for Salesforce: ApprovalProcesses, AssignmentRules, Classes, Dashboards, Emails, FlowDefinitions, Flows, Layouts, Objects, Pages, Permissionsets, Profiles, Reports, ReportTypes, Roles, Triggers, and Workflows.

NOTE  
To restore other metadata types, you'll need to export them out of Spanning Backup, then use a tool like Force.com IDE, ANT Migration Tool, or Workbench to import them into Salesforce. To export metadata, see [Exporting data](SF-export-data.htm).

Use these procedures to restore metadata:

[![Closed](https://help.spanning.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)To restore](#) [metadata to the same organization](#)

1. Log in to Spanning Backup for Salesforce as the System Administrator.
2. Click **Restore**.
3. In the Select Type step:

> * Select **Metadata** as the type of data you want to restore.
> * Select **This Org** for the restore destination.
> * Click **Next**.  
> [

![](/media/3f19ea0d-3d92-4028-aa1c-be35f5b5819e/f244512c2165.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Restore' screen in Spanning Salesforce, showing the 'Select Type And Destination' step. The 'Metadata' type and 'This org' destination are selected, with a progress bar indicating the current step as 'SELECT TYPE'. The 'Next' button is highlighted for proceeding to the next step.

](../Resources/Images/Span-SF/restore-meta.png)

1. In the Select Metadata step:

> * Select the backup to restore from.
> * Choose the items to restore by expanding the metadata types and selecting individual items. To preview an item, hover over the item and click **Preview**.
> * Once you've selected all the items you want to restore, click **Next**.  
> [

![](/media/3f19ea0d-3d92-4028-aa1c-be35f5b5819e/04df5f07f489.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Restore' screen in Spanning Salesforce, showing the 'Select Items To Restore' step. The user has selected metadata types including AssignmentRules and specific Email templates, with a date selector set to 'Fri, Aug 8, 2025 2:00 AM'. The interface includes a progress bar with steps: SELECT TYPE, SELECT METADATA, RESTORE SETTINGS, CONFIRM RESTORE, and a 'Next' button to proceed.

](../Resources/Images/Span-SF/restore-meta-2.png)

1. In the Restore Settings step:

> * (Optional) Check the box to ignore warnings from Salesforce during this metadata restore only.
> 
> 
> * Click **Next**.  
> [![](/media/3f19ea0d-3d92-4028-aa1c-be35f5b5819e/bb050defdbc1.png)](../Resources/Images/Span-SF/restore-meta-3.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Restore Settings' step in the Spanning Salesforce restore workflow. It shows an optional checkbox to 'Ignore Warnings' during metadata restore and a 'Next' button to proceed to the 'Confirm Restore' step. The navigation bar includes options like Dashboard, Restore, Export, and Settings.

1. In the Confirm Restore step, review the items that will be restored. Click **Restore**. Click **Confirm**.  
[

![](/media/3f19ea0d-3d92-4028-aa1c-be35f5b5819e/19d42f695e4a.png)

The dialog warns that the process cannot be undone and prompts the user to click 'Confirm' to proceed. The background lists 4 metadata items to be restored, including AssignmentRules and Email templates.

](../Resources/Images/Span-SF/restore-meta-4.png)
2. When the restore is complete, you are notified via email and Chatter (if enabled). View the restore results on the Dashboard by clicking the **Metadata Restore** row in the Recent Activity.  
[

![](/media/3f19ea0d-3d92-4028-aa1c-be35f5b5819e/dd78d72d6358.png)

> **Figure:** Dashboard screen showing a successful backup with 100% completion, 0 errors and 0 warnings, scheduled for Friday August 8, 2025 at 2:00 AM. Recent activity includes successful Metadata Restore, Multi-Record Export, and Multi-Record Restore actions. Subscription status indicates 'Not Enough Licenses' with 8 licenses purchased for 12 users.

](../Resources/Images/Span-SF/restore-meta-5.png)
[

![](/media/3f19ea0d-3d92-4028-aa1c-be35f5b5819e/e6b66012de31.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'View Metadata Restore' screen in Spanning Salesforce, showing a completed metadata restore task initiated by a user on August 8, 2025. The restore is 100% complete, restoring 4 items including assignmentRules and email templates.

> * Review the items to restore. Click **Restore**. Click **Confirm**. Selected items are restored.

NOTE  You can only restore specific metadata types directly from Spanning. For non\-restorable metadata types, you can export the items from Spanning and use tools like Force.com IDE or the ANT migration tool to restore them back into Salesforce.

[![Closed](https://help.spanning.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)Comparing](#) [metadata in different organizations](#)

Use this procedure to select a backup and compare its metadata to the live (current) metadata in a different Salesforce org.

The comparison shows any files that were added, deleted, or updated, along with a side\-by\-side view of the changes in any updated files. While viewing the comparison results, you can opt to export files or perform a metadata restore.

NOTE  Spanning Backup for Salesforce does not need to be installed in the target org to perform the metadata comparison.

citations.title: Restore Metadata
citations.text:
Restore Metadata
[\#](#restore-metadata)Restore Metadata > [\#](#in-place-restore)In Place Restore

[\#](#restore-metadata)Restore Metadata
You can restore **AssignmentRules**, **ApexClass**, **ApexTrigger**, **ApprovalProcess**, **CustomLabels**, **CustomObject**, **Dashboard**, **EmailTemplate**, **FlexiPage**, **Flow**, **GlobalValueSet**, **Layout**, **PermissionSet**, **Profile**, **QuickAction**, **Report**, **ReportType**, **SharingRules**, **Workflow**, **DuplicateRules**, **PermissionGroups**, **Queues**, and **Tabs** metadata by designating the metadata through recovery point, metadata type, and metadata name. The metadata restore is only available to user groups that have the **Restore** **metadata** permission.

NOTEIn the restore job, the conflicting metadata will be overwritten by the backup metadata.

You can choose one of the following ways to restore all metadata in an organization:

* [In Place Restore](#in-place-restore) – Restore specific metadata to the original organization.
* [Out of Place Restore](#out-of-place-restore) – Restore specific metadata to another organization.

To restore the metadata to the original organization, complete the following steps.

1. Click **Restore** in the left navigation.
2. On the **Restore** page, click the **Restore** button next to an organization that you want to restore.
3. Select the **Restore** **metadata** tile, and then click **Next** to configure the data scope.
4. In the **Recovery** **point** field, select the time from which you want to restore the metadata and click **Apply**.
5. Click **Search**. All metadata in the backup will be displayed.
6. In the **Metadata type** pane, select the metadata types you want to restore. You can also search for desired metadata by entering the keyword of the metadata type in the search box.
7. In the **Metadata** pane, select the metadata you want to restore in different metadata types. You can also search for specific metadata by metadata display name or API name in the search box.

NOTEDue to SOAP API limitations, metadata display names are supported only for the following metadata types: **ApexClass**, **ApexTrigger**, **EmailTemplate**, **Profile**, **Report**, **ApprovalProcess**, **PermissionSet**, and **Dashboard**.

To ensure data completeness and accuracy, you can click **View parent metadata of the selected metadata** to view the parent metadata related to your selection. Please review the listed parent metadata and verify them in Salesforce. To successfully restore the selected metadata, ensure that the corresponding parent metadata exists in your destination organization.
8. Click **Next** to configure the restore settings.
9. In the **Configure** **restore settings** step, configure the following settings:

	* Where do you want to restore the data? – Select the Restore the data to the original organization option.

	In the **Select a default user for restoring records that belong to deactivated users** text box, enter a keyword of usernames to load valid users and select a default user.

	NOTEThe default user must have the **Modify All Data** permission for the objects where the specific metadata resides.
	* If any metadata fails to be restored, do you want to continue to restore other successful metadata? – Select Roll back all metadata changes to keep the records consistent if you would like to revert the successfully restored metadata of the object; select Keep any successful metadata for a partial restore if you would like to keep the successfully restored metadata of the object.
	* **Revert metadata to the backup version** – Turn on/off the toggle to define if you want to revert metadata to the backup version. By enabling the toggle, AvePoint Cloud Backup for Salesforce® will restore the metadata to your destination organization and remove any newly added fields (which were not included in the backup metadata file) from the destination.
10. Click **Next** to go to the **Overview** page to view the settings of the restore job.
11. Click **Restore** to restore the metadata as your configurations. After the job has started, you can go to the job monitor to view more job details. For details, refer to [Job Monitor](/salesforce/job-monitor.html).

citations.title: Restoring Metadata
citations.text:
Restoring Metadata

You can restore metadata of objects deleted from Salesforce, including Apex classes, connected app configurations, reports, dashboards and so on. You can recover metadata to the same Salesforce tenant or to another tenant so that the object metadata in one Salesforce tenant matches the metadata in another one.

Before you restore a Salesforce metadata component, make sure that all components the metadata file depends on already exist on the target Salesforce tenant. To restore the components, create a separate metadata restore job. For example:

* If you want to restore flow definitions (FlowDefinition metadata file), restore the Flow metadata file first. For details on the FlowDefinition dependencies, see [Salesforce Documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_flowdefinition.htm).
* If you want to restore session settings (ProfileSessionSetting metadata file), restore the Profile metadata file first. For details on the ProfileSessionSetting dependencies, see [Salesforce Documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_profilesessionsetting.htm).
* If you want to restore password policies (ProfilePasswordPolicy metadata file), restore the Profile metadata file first. For details on the ProfilePasswordPolicy dependencies, see [Salesforce Documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_profilepasswordpolicy.htm).

| Note |
| --- |
| * Before you restore records, field values, or files of a deleted Salesforce object, you must restore the object metadata and then back up this object to make it available in the restore wizard. * If you want to restore metadata of a [custom object](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.dev_objectedit.htm&type=5) that was deleted from Salesforce permanently, you must restore the following types of metadata first: CustomObject, CustomTab, Layout and Profile. Note that when restoring metadata of the Profile type, you must choose all profiles that have access to the custom object. * If you delete a metadata field from Salesforce and then create a new field using the same API name, Veeam Data Cloud will treat this field as the same item when restoring metadata and will populate it with the values of the deleted field. |

To restore Salesforce metadata, perform the following steps:

1. [Launch the Restore Metadata wizard](sf_restore_metadata_launch.html).
2. [Specify a name and description for the restore job](sf_restore_metadata_name.html).
3. [Select a target Salesforce tenant](sf_restore_metadata_organization.html).
4. [Select objects whose metadata will be restored](sf_restore_metadata_data.html).
5. [Review the restore list](sf_restore_metadata_restore_list.html).
6. [Finish working with the wizard](sf_restore_metadata_summary.html).

citations.title: Salesforce Metadata Backup
citations.text:
Salesforce Metadata Backup

As of April 2025, GRAX only performs incremental metadata backups. GRAX will take a snapshot of any new files or ones that have changed since the previous backup. For example, if a file was added on Monday, modified on Wednesday, and rolled back to the original version on Friday, GRAX will only save the three versions from Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

GRAX supports periodic backup of all possible metadata objects from Salesforce. GRAX stores your metadata in the customer-owned storage solution (S3, Azure, etc), and the version history is available in the GRAX Diagnostics and Tools page.

Configuration / Setup[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#configuration-setup)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By default, GRAX checks for any new or changed metadata once per day. To change the metadata backup frequency, simply select a backup interval in the `General Settings` tab.

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/2028d509b11d4e49.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the General Settings screen showing the Metadata Backup Interval setting, highlighted with a red box. The interval is set to 'Daily' with an option to 'Take full metadata backup'.

Metadata Backup Interval Setting

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/de09eabcf9f9a31e.png)

> **Figure:** The 'Edit Setting' dialog displays the expanded dropdown menu for selecting the 'Metadata Backup Interval'. The options include Disabled, Hourly, Twice/Day, Daily, Twice/Week (currently selected), and Weekly, with specific times shown in UTC.

Metadata Backup Interval Selection Window

Working with Metadata Backups[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#working-with-metadata-backups)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The metadata backups are stored in the customer-owned storage solution (S3, Azure etc) and can be accessed with the Salesforce Metadata viewer in the GRAX Diagnostics and Tools page.

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/295b4d804c590355.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the GRAX Application Settings page showing a sidebar with options like Auto Backup, Archive, Restore, and Sandbox Seeding. The main area displays connection statuses for Salesforce (Connected) and Object Storage (Not connected), with a pink arrow pointing to the 'Diagnostics and Tools' button.

Getting to GRAX Tools List

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/4a7ac76446ae831e.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the GRAX Tools page showing a list of tools including Field Level Security, Missing Field Permissions, Reset Auto Backup objects, Salesforce Automations, and Salesforce Metadata. A pink arrow points to the 'Salesforce Metadata' tool, which is highlighted with a pink play button, indicating it is selected or actionable.

Metadata Explorer in GRAX Tools List

Metadata files are grouped by Salesforce Object Type

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/f105d15e9875b08e.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the GRAX Tools Salesforce Metadata explorer, showing an expanded list of AnimationRule files (e.g., Lead.animationRule, Sales.animationRule) alongside other collapsed metadata categories.

Metadata Object Selection

Viewing Metadata File contents[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#viewing-metadata-file-contents)
To view the contents of a metadata file version, click the Visibility / Eye icon for the desired version, the file will be displayed above the version list.

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/d3d22e97e12c97d0.png)

> **Figure:** This screenshot shows the Salesforce metadata version history view for a CurrencySettings backup file, displaying XML content and a list of versions with download actions.

View Metadata Object Version
