Salesforce Metadata Backup
Comparing Metadata Versions[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#comparing-metadata-versions)

To see the differences between 2 versions of a metadata file:

1.  Click the "Compare" icons to select the 2 versions you want to diff.

2.  Once 2 versions have been selected the "Compare" button above the version list will be enabled. Click it to open a list of the changes between the 2 selected versions.

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/db6abeefcaf8dd48.png)

> **Figure:** This screenshot shows a version comparison view for the settings/Currency.settings file, highlighting differences between two backups taken on Mar 24 and Jun 3, 2025. It includes a Versions table with 'Compare' actions (marked as step 1) leading to the diff display (marked as step 2).

Metadata Object Version Diff View

Downloading Metadata Versions[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#downloading-metadata-versions)
To download the contents of a metadata file version, click the "Download" icon for the desired version.

![](/media/f875d337-e5b0-4a89-bd07-df51d1c4e36f/c174d4ae50cb58c7.png)

> **Figure:** A 'Versions' dialog listing file backups with their timestamps and hashes. A red arrow points to the download icon in the action column of a specific version row.

Metadata Object Version Download

Frequently Asked Questions[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#frequently-asked-questions)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Which Salesforce API is used to determine what metadata is backed up?[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#which-salesforce-api-is-used-to-determine-what-metadata-is-backed-up)
We utilize the [describeMetadata()](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_describe.htm)
 API.

Additional documentation on Salesforce's metadata API can be found [here](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_intro.htm)
.

Why does the Salesforce Metadata Tool in GRAX not show metadata for all of my objects?[](https://documentation.grax.com/protect-data/backup/salesforce-metadata-backup#why-does-the-salesforce-metadata-tool-in-grax-not-show-metadata-for-all-of-my-objects)
This [describeMetadata()](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_describe.htm)
 API call retrieves the metadata that describes your organization. This information includes Apex classes and triggers, custom objects, custom fields on standard objects, tab sets that define an app, and many other metadata types. **Standard objects without custom fields are not included in this data.**

citations.title: Salesforce backup and recovery
citations.text:
Salesforce backup and recovery

RSC securely backs up your Salesforce organization with snapshots and
 recovers your data from those snapshots.

You can back up your Salesforce data automatically or on demand to recover data when data
 is compromised by malicious activity. For backups, RSC takes snapshots
 of the data in your Salesforce organization, and you can recover your data from these
 snapshots.

You can:

* Back up and recover Salesforce fields, records, objects, profiles, and
 metadata.Data backup and recovery also keeps relationships between objects
 intact.
* Automatically back up data at either 12\-hour or 24\-hour intervals so that you have
 daily restore points.
* Compare snapshots to see the differences between snapshot data and metadata to
 determine which snapshot to recover.
* Take on\-demand snapshots to back up data as needed.

Salesforce fields, records, and objects backup and recovery
You can recover Salesforce records or certain fields in such records from a snapshot
 to a Salesforce production or sandbox environment. You can also recover Salesforce
 objects, including all the files, fields, and records in the objects.

Before recovery, you can compare the records in a snapshot with those in your live
 Salesforce environment. Record and object recovery involves keeping relationships
 between dependent or related objects intact. Because records or objects you want to
 recover might have dependent or related records, you can analyze your records or
 objects to find the ones with dependencies.

During analysis, RSC provides a list of dependent and related records
 or objects, and you can select the parent and child records to recover. You can also
 recover records or objects that were deleted before the last snapshot was taken.

Salesforce metadata backup and recovery
You can recover Salesforce organizational metadata, such as from custom objects,
 layouts, email templates, workflows, and validation rules to a production or sandbox
 environment. You can recover all metadata or specific metadata for objects, and you
 can recover specific metadata components for general metadata types, such as user
 permission configurations.

citations.title: Recovering Salesforce object metadata
citations.text:
Recovering Salesforce object metadata
Procedure

Recover Salesforce custom object metadata associated with individual Salesforce
 objects from a snapshot to a Salesforce production or sandbox environment. You can recover
 all metadata related to individual objects, or you can recover specific metadata. Object
 metadata that you can restore includes fields, validation rules, record types, and page
 layouts.

About this task
You can recover Salesforce custom object metadata from a snapshot to a Salesforce
 production or sandbox environment.

1. Log in to RSC.
2. Click ![Applications](https://docs.rubrik.com/en-us/saas/images/ui-icons/AppTray.svg) and select
 SaaS App Protection.
The SaaS Apps Dashboard appears.
3. Click the Salesforce inventory card.
The details page for the Salesforce instance appears.
4. Click Restore.
5. Click Get Started in the Restore Metadata section.
Selecting Don't show again skips this page the next time you restore metadata. 
The Restore Metadata wizard appears.
6. Select Object metadata and click
 Next.
7. Select the objects with the metadata to restore.
8. Click Select metadata and select the type of metadata to
 recover.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Restore all metadata | Restores all metadata associated with the Salesforce  object. |
| Restore specific metadata | Restores specific metadata, for example, a custom field of a  Salesforce object.Select the metadata to recover. |

9. Click Close and then click
 Next.
10. Specify the Salesforce environment to which to restore the object
 metadata.

| Action | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Use an existing destination | To use an existing Salesforce environment, select the environment  from Destination Environment and then click Next. |
| Add a new destination | To add a new destination, perform the following steps: 	* Click . 	* Enter details about the Salesforce organization to use as the 	 recovery destination. 	* Log in to Salesforce to grant RSC access to 	 manage your Salesforce data. 	* Click Done. |

When recovering metadata to an existing destination, by default, RSC takes the source destination as the recovery destination.
 This list contains the source organization and the associated sandbox
 organizations. RSC does not list the sandbox organizations
 associated with any other production organization.When you add a new
 destination, the user account you use to connect to the Salesforce
 organization must have write permission. RSC does not back
 up the Salesforce organization added from this window. When adding a backup
 environment, the Salesforce organization must be associated with the source.
 It should also have the same schema, to ensure data integrity and avoid
 backup issues.
11. Click Next.
12. Select the snapshot to use to restore object metadata.
13. **Optional:** 
To compare snapshot data with the live environment data, hover over the
 snapshot, and then click Compare.
The Compare with Live Environment dialog box appears, displaying the
 modified, added, and deleted records. The following table explains the different
 types of records:

| Record type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Added | The data is available in the snapshot, but not available  in the live environment. When you restore the record, the  snapshot data is added to the recovery destination. |
| Modified | The data available in the live environment and in the  snapshot is different. You can hover over a modified cell to  see the difference. When you restore the record, the  snapshot data overrides the data in the recovery  destination. |
| Deleted | The data is available in the live environment, but not  available in the snapshot. When you restore the record, the  live environment data is deleted from the recovery  destination. |

14. After comparing the metadata, click Close.
15. Click Next.
16. Verify the recovery options and metadata, and then click
 Restore.

Results
RSC starts restoring the metadata to the selected Salesforce
 environment. You can view the progress of the recover job on the Events page.

citations.title: Restoring Metadata to Salesforce
citations.text:
Restoring Metadata to Salesforce
Restoring Salesforce Metadata to Salesforce > Procedure

Restoring Salesforce Metadata to Salesforce
You can restore Salesforce metadata to the Salesforce cloud. Data is restored from media. When data is restored from media, the data is restored to a staging location, and then the data is upload to Salesforce. You can also [validate the metadata restore operation](./validating_restore_of_salesforce_metadata_to_salesforce.html) before you perform the actual restore operation.

Metadata [supported by the Salesforce API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/metadata-coverage/62) is supported for restore operations.

Note

* You cannot restore managed package components to Salesforce.
* To restore metadata, you must select individual components, instead of selecting the entire metadata.

Before You Begin
Verify that the Salesforce user who performs the restores [has the required permissions](./salesforce_account_and_user_permissions.html).

1. From the Command Center navigation pane, go to **Protect \> Salesforce**.

The Salesforce **Overview** page appears.
2. Go to the **Organizations** tab.
3. For the organization that contains the data that you want to restore, click the action button ![action_button](/media/c10888e9-bebb-45c8-be42-ed609d18f43f/7cd7e025ac1d969d.png), and then click **Restore**.

The **Select restore type** page appears.
4. Select **Metadata restore**.

The **Backup content** page appears.

Here you can download up to 1 GB of metadata and use tools like Workbench to later import into a Salesforce environment. Select one or more metadata components, and then click **Download**.
5. Optional: To select a backup, do the following:

	* To show the latest backup, select **Show latest backup**.
	* To show a backup at a specific time, select **Show backup as of a specific date**, and then select the date and time.
	* To show backups for a date range, select **Show backup for a date range**, and then specify **From time** and **To time**.
6. Go to **Metadata** \> **unpackaged**, and then select the metadata object(s) that you want to restore.

Note

For each metadata file that you want to restore, check if the metadata file (**\-meta.xml**) exists, and then select it. For example, suppose that you have **AccountBeforeUpdate.cls** file that is accompanied by the **AccountBeforeUpdate.cls\-meta.xml** file and you want to restore metadata. In this case, you will need to select both files in the restore operation.
7. Click **Restore**.

The **Restore options** dialog box appears.
8. Next to **Restore target**, select **Salesforce**.
9. In the **Destination details** section, from the **Destination organization** list, select the Salesforce destination.
10. Click **Run**.
11. Click **Confirm**.

What to Do Next
* Monitor the **restore** job. If the job is not successful, go to the job details page to review the errors.
* In Salesforce, check the metadata deploy status, results, and errors. If errors occur, go to the **Deployment Details** page to troubleshoot, or contact your Salesforce administrator or Salesforce support. For more information, go to [Monitor Deployments](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.deploy_monitoring.htm&type=5) on the Salesforce support website.

citations.title: Restoring Salesforce Metadata to Salesforce
citations.text:
Restoring Salesforce Metadata to Salesforce

You can restore the Salesforce metadata to the Salesforce cloud. Data is restored from media. When data is restored from media, the data is restored to a staging location, and then the data is upload to Salesforce. You can also [validate the metadata restore operation](./validating_restore_of_salesforce_metadata_to_salesforce.html) before you perform the actual restore operation.

Metadata [supported by the Salesforce API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/metadata-coverage/62) is supported for restore operations.

If you need to modify or customize the metadata that you backed up, perform the following operations:

1. Restore the metadata to a file system.
2. Modify the corresponding xml files.
3. Use the Force.com Migration Tool tool to deploy the metadata to the Salesforce organization. For more information, go to the [Salesforce help](https://developer.salesforce.com/page/Force.com_Migration_Tool) website, *Force.com Migration Tool*.

Before You Begin
* Verify that the Salesforce user who performs the restore operation has a System Administrator profile or an equivalent profile.
* You must have a subclient that includes metadata. For more information, see [Backing Up Salesforce Metadata](./backing_up_salesforce_metadata.html).

citations.title: Restores
citations.text:
Restores
Salesforce Restores

As part of your overall data protection planning, plan your Salesforce restore operations according to your requirements.

After the restore is complete, you can view all the associated details of the restore job. For more information, see [Viewing Restore Operation Details](./viewing_restore_operation_details.html).

Record\-level Restores
You can restore Salesforce records to a file system (Commvault software only) or to the Salesforce cloud.

When you perform a record\-level restore, you can view all versions of a Salesforce object record.

If you have triggers or workflows that are associated with the unmanaged package and the restore destination is a Salesforce instance, then you can have the Commvault software disable the workflows or triggers before the restore, and then activate them after the restore completes (**Disable triggers and rules** check box). Use this option to improve load performance and minimize errors.

Note

You can use the **Metadata** tab in the object configuration to define granular exclusions for this setting. For example, you can exclude broad categories from the restore or use **Granular overrides** to specify rules or triggers that must be enabled or disabled during the restore operation. For more information, see [Configure Salesforce Object and Metadata Settings for Restores](./configure_salesforce_object_and_metadata_settings_for_restores.html).

Object\-level Restores
You can restore Salesforce data to the following destinations:

* A file system path that you specify when you perform the restore (Commvault software only)
* A relational database management system that you specify when you perform the restore
* The Salesforce cloud

Salesforce Metadata
You can restore Salesforce metadata to a file system (Commvault software only) or to the Salesforce cloud. All metadata [supported by the Salesforce API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/metadata-coverage/62) is supported for restore operations.

Seeding a Salesforce Sandbox
You can perform a restore to seed a Salesforce sandbox.

Perform granular or bulk seeding by configuring rules or templates that specify the objects that you want to seed and the object records to use for the seeding. If you want to seed multiple objects that are not related, these objects need to be included in the seeding template. The seeding templates will be saved for immediate or future use, consistent reseeding of development or training sandboxes, or to be edited to create new templates.

You can specify any of the following records:

* All records
* Records that are returned from a user\-defined SQL query
* Records that have been backed up in the last N number of days
* The most recently backed up N records

How to Restore / Seed a Full Org using Druva App

**Overview**
In Salesforce environments, disaster recovery or data restoration may require rebuilding the organization from scratch, including restoring all data from backups. These situations can arise due to data loss, accidental deletion of records, custom objects, or even custom metadata.

The Druva App provides a robust solution to address these challenges effectively. 

This document outlines the recommended steps to perform a Full Org Restore operation, enabling administrators to recover and restore their Salesforce organization easily and precisely.

Metadata components such as Custom Objects, Picklists, User Profiles, and others are essential for successful data restoration. Any required metadata missing in the target organization could result in errors or failures during the restoration process.

If you notice any missing metadata components in your target org, follow the steps below to address them. Otherwise, proceed to the next step.

citations.title: Configuring Salesforce Backups
citations.text:
Configuring Salesforce Backups
View **Backups and Snapshots** > View Snapshot Details

Click a snapshot row to open the snapshot detail page. The detail page contains two sub\-tabs: **Objects** and **Metadata**.

**Objects sub\-tab**

The Objects sub\-tab lists all Salesforce objects included in the snapshot with their record change counts. 

| Column | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Object Name** | The name of the Salesforce object. |
| **Total Records Affected** | The total number of records created, updated, or deleted in this object. |
| **Created** | Records created in this snapshot. |
| **Updated** | Records updated in this snapshot. |
| **Deleted** | Records deleted in this snapshot. |

Click an object name to view its individual records. You can:

* Filter records by **Record Change Type** (Created/Updated or other types).
* Search records using a **Where Clause** (SOQL\-style search).
* Select records and click **Download ▾** to download the data.
* Select records and click **Restore** to restore the selected records. The restore wizard opens directly at **Step 3 — Preview**; record selection is already determined from your selection. For more information, see [Restore Data](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8367885-restore-data).
* Click the **▾** on a record row to view the backup history for that record. For more information, see [View Backup History of a Record](#view-backup-history-of-a-record).

**Metadata sub\-tab**
The Metadata sub\-tab enables you to compare metadata between two snapshots and restore or download individual metadata files.

**Procedure**

1. In the **Select Snapshot to Compare** field, select a second snapshot using the calendar date picker.
2. Click **Compare**. The left panel displays a list of metadata types with their change counts. The right panel shows the individual files for the selected metadata type.
3. Select a metadata type in the left panel to populate the file list in the right panel.
4. Select files in the right panel and click **Show Comparison** to open the Metadata Comparison view.
5. Click **Download** or **Restore** to download or restore the selected files.
6. Click **Clear** to reset the snapshot comparison.

**Metadata Comparison**
The Metadata Comparison modal displays a side\-by\-side XML diff of the selected file between the two snapshots.

* **Show only items with difference** — filters the view to show only changed fields.
* **Updated Metadata** and **Deleted Metadata** checkboxes — filter by change type.
* **Download** — download the metadata file.
* **Restore** — restore the metadata file to the Salesforce organization.
For more information about restoring data, see [Compare and Restore Records](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8367885-restore-data#h_4b8378b023) and [Compare and Restore Metadata](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8367885-restore-data#h_687c7f3ed4).

citations.title: Plan and Prepare for Salesforce Data Protection
citations.text:
Plan and Prepare for Salesforce Data Protection
Create User Profile and Connected App

As a prerequisite for backing up and recovering Salesforce data and metadata, you must first create a user profile and a connected app in your Salesforce environment to establish a connection.

To create user profile and connected app using Lightning Experience:

1. Log into your Salesforce org using System Administrator profile user.
2. Click **Setup** .
3. Locate the profile setup by typing **profile** in the search box on the left.
4. Click **New Profile** .
5. Select **System Administrator** from the list to create a clone of the profile.
6. Provide a name to the profile (for example, Cohesity Backup Admin Profile).
7. Click **Save** .
8. Click **Edit** .
9. Ensure that **Modify All Data** and **API enabled** permissions are granted to the new profile.
10. Grant **View Encrypted Data** permission to profile, if encrypted fields are used for standard/custom objects.
11. Grant **Query all files** permission to profile, to back up private library files for all users.
12. Grant **View and Edit Converted Leads** permission if the lead is converted and needs to be restored.
13. Click **Save** .
14. Click **View Users > New User** for creating a new user.
15. Provide user details like **First Name** , **Last Name** , **Username** , **Email** and select the profile created earlier.
16. Click **Save** .
17. **Logoff** and **Logon** to the Salesforce portal, using newly created user.

To configure Connected App:

1. Log in to Salesforce org using newly created user.
2. Click **Setup** .
3. Locate the **App Manager** setup by typing it in the search box on the left.
4. Click **New Connected App** at the top right.
5. Click **Create a Connected App** option and then click **Continue** to process further.
6. Provide the basic information for the new app, such as the name.
7. Select the **Enable OAuth settings** checkbox. Set the callback URL to http://localhost:1717/OauthRedirect.
8. Select the **Full Access** and **Perform requests at any time (refresh\_token, offline\_access)** from the list of the **Available OAuth scopes** . This is required by the app for permissions to back up and restore various objects and records.
9. Click **Save** .
10. Go to the app created and look for consumer key. Copy the consumer key to a text file for use later. This is required to register your Salesforce domain with Cohesity Cloud Services.
11. Click **Setup** . Type **My Domain** . Click **My Domain** . Copy the URL displayed in the **Current My Domain URL** field, this is required to register your Salesforce domain with Cohesity Cloud Services.
12. Click **Generate certificate** and download the certificate.
13. Go back to the Connected App created earlier and click **Edit** , to associate the certificate.
14. Select the **Use Digital Signature** checkbox and upload the certificate created by using **Choose File** .
15. Click **Save** .
16. From the **App Manager** , locate the app and click **Manage** .
17. Click **Edit Policies** .
18. Under **OAuth Policies** , set permitted users to **Admin approved users are pre-authorized** and set **IP Relaxation** to **Relax IP restrictions** . Choose default for all other settings.
19. Click **Save** .
20. Scroll down and click **Manage Profiles** .
21. Select the profile associated with the user who can use this Connected App for backup and restore.
22. Click **Save** .

This completes the setup of Connected App in Salesforce using the Lightning experience.

Salesforce Considerations
Review the following considerations before registering, protecting, or restoring Salesforce data and metadata.

Objects Skipped by Default During Backup
By default, Salesforce backs up all objects except Feed, History, and Share objects. These objects are not typically critical for business continuity. You can enable backups for these objects if required.

- l History objects . History objects cannot be recovered. Select these objects for backup only if you need to retain historical record level or field level changes for auditing purposes.
- l Share objects . Only manual Share objects can be recovered. Other Share object types cannot be recovered due to Salesforce API limitations. During recovery, Share tables are automatically created unless they contain manual Share rules.
- l Feed objects . Feed objects are views into the FeedItem object. To avoid duplication, Cohesity Cloud Services backs up only the FeedItem object. Due to Salesforce API limitations, only specific FeedItem record types can be recovered.

Note: Skipping Feed, History, and Share objects improves backup performance and reduces storage consumption for recovery points.

citations.text:
Restoring metadata from a data backup job
Restoring metadata via Metadata History

* * *

Related Articles

*   [Creating your first data backup job](https://docs.gearset.com/en/articles/3277396-creating-your-first-data-backup-job)

question: Which backup products support Nutanix AHV virtual machines natively, without installing agents in each VM?
answer:
Commvault (CommCell Console, Commvault Cloud): Uses the Virtual Server Agent installed on a proxy machine to manage agentless backup and restore of guest VMs, with Changed Block Tracking for incremental backups [1][2].
Druva (Druva): Performs agent-less backup using a backup proxy appliance deployed in Prism Element or Prism Central, with incremental backups using Nutanix Change Region Tracking [4].
Veeam (Veeam Backup & Replication): Backs up Nutanix AHV VMs to backup repositories via the Veeam Plug-In for Nutanix AHV, without agents in each VM [6][7].
Cohesity (NetBackup): Uses an agentless architecture where NetBackup communicates with the AHV cluster through Nutanix AHV APIs, with a backup host acting as access host [8].
Unitrends (Unitrends Unified Backup): Performs host-level backups leveraging Nutanix REST APIs for application- and OS-consistent backup without installing an agent on each VM [11][12].
Storware (Backup and Recovery): Uses Nutanix APIs to create snapshots and attach their disks to a proxy VM running the Storware node, which reads data from attached disks [13][14].
Dell (PowerProtect Data Manager): Enables a protection engine for Nutanix clusters with Prism Central as the asset source, providing image-level backup of Nutanix VMs [15].
Bacula (Bacula): The Nutanix-AHV Plugin performs image backup by querying guest VMs through the hypervisor API to read and save VM disks using snapshots and NDFS, handled by a proxy VM [18][19].
Acronis (Cyber Protect Cloud, Cyber Protect On-premises): Protects Nutanix virtual machines using the Agent for Nutanix AHV deployed as a virtual appliance on the Nutanix AHV host, backing up VMs agentlessly from a dedicated machine [23][24].
Arcserve (Arcserve Backup, Arcserve UDP): Supports agentless VM backup policies for Nutanix AHV [27].
Rubrik (Rubrik Security Cloud): Takes application-consistent or crash-consistent snapshots of AHV virtual machines natively at the cluster/VM level [36][37].
Nakivo (Nakivo Backup & Replication): Performs Nutanix AHV VM backups with optional app-aware mode using Nutanix Guest Tools for guest OS quiescing [38].
IBM (Storage Defender, Storage Protect): Supports block-based backup for Acropolis (AHV) virtual machines [40].
Atempo (Tina): Provides a Nutanix AHV agent that performs full and incremental backups of VMs via the Nutanix APIs without in-guest agents [47].
No supporting passage found for: AWS, Afi.ai, Arctera, AvePoint, Axcient, Barracuda, CloudAlly, CloudCasa, Datto, Eon, Flosum, GRAX, Gearset, Google, HYCU, Hornetsecurity (Altaro), Keepit, Microsoft, N-Able, NinjaOne (Dropsuite), Portworx, Red Hat, Salesforce, Slide, Spanning, Synology, Trilio, Velero, Zerto.

citations.text:
Nutanix Acropolis Hypervisor (AHV)
Key Features

| Feature | Description | Additional information |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agentless backups and restores | Install the Virtual Server Agent on a machine to act as a VSA proxy. A VSA proxy manages backup and restore operations for guest VMs in your environment, eliminating the need to install agents on guest VMs. | [Deployment](./deployment_for_nutanix_ahv.html) [System Requirements](./system_requirements_for_virtual_server_agent_with_nutanix_ahv_03.html) |
| "Incremental forever" data protection | After an initial full backup, you can perform ongoing incremental backups to capture changes for the source VM. | [Backups](./backups_09.html) |
| Changed Block Tracking | Commvault uses Changed Block Tracking (CBT) to identify changes for each incremental backup. | [Changed Block Tracking](./changed_block_tracking_for_nutanix_ahv_01.html) |
| Restores | You can restore full VMs or guest files and folders. | [Restores](./restores_10.html) |
| Simplified operational interface | The web\-based Command Center interface uses smart defaults to simplify configuration and support streamlined operations. | [Command Center](../software/protect_hypervisors_virtual_machines_and_instances_with_commvault.html) |
| Single point of administration | The CommCell Console provides advanced options for Commvault operations. Using the CommCell Console, you can configure a virtualization client that serves as a single point of administration for a Nutanix cluster. You can perform backups and restores from the virtualization client, and perform other administrative tasks such as creating schedules and generating reports. | [Creating a Virtualization Client for Nutanix AHV](./creating_virtualization_client_for_nutanix_ahv_01.html) |
| Automatic protection for all virtual machines | By default, all virtual machines are automatically selected for backup, to ensure that all virtual machines are backed up. | [Default Subclient Coverage](./default_subclient_coverage_for_unprotected_virtual_machines_02.html) |
| Application\-aware backups | Perform application\-consistent backups without installing application agents on virtual machines. From the Command Center, you can use the Auto discover applications option to automatically find applications on servers and install the agents that can back up the applications. (For more information, see [Automatic Discovery of Applications in the Command Center](../software/automatic_discovery_of_applications.html).) | [Application\-Aware Backups](./application_aware_backups_for_virtual_server_agent.html) |
| Automatic discovery | To back up categories of virtual machines, you can create rules to automatically select virtual machines based on specific criteria. Automatic discovery is useful in environments where virtual machines are frequently added or removed. | [Virtual Machine Discovery and Filtering](./virtual_machine_discovery_and_filtering_02.html) |
| Customized filters | To exclude virtual machines from backups, create rules to filter virtual machines. | [Defining Filters for Content](./defining_filters_for_content_09.html) |
| VM conversion | When restoring a VM, you can choose to restore to a different hypervisor. This capability can be used to migrate VMs to a different virtualization platform. | [Cross\-Hypervisor Restores](../software/cross_hypervisor_restores_virtual_machine_conversion.html) |
| Reports | You can view detailed information about each backed up virtual machine, including information such as size of the data, status of integration services, guest operating system, and the host on which the virtual machine is running. | [Reports for Virtual Server Agents](./reports_for_virtual_server_agents.html) |
| Snapshot support | Use snapshots to capture virtual machine data quickly, with minimal impact on the source VM, and use the snapshot as a source for backup copies. | [IntelliSnap for Nutanix Acropolis Hypervisor](./overview_intellisnap_for_nutanix_acropolis_hypervisor_ahv.html) |

citations.text:
Nutanix AHV Clusters on AWS

You can deploy Commvault to protect workloads running in Nutanix AHV Clusters on AWS.

Commvault Supported Features
With Nutanix AHV Clusters on AWS, you can use the following configurations for backups and restores using Commvault:

* **Regular Backups and IntelliSnap Backups**

	+ Supports Nutanix AHV Clusters on AWS for both regular and IntelliSnap backups.
	+ Enables backup copies for Windows and Linux VMs.
* **Multiple Proxies and MediaAgents**

	+ Supports multiple Windows and Linux proxies.
	+ Utilizes Windows and Linux MediaAgents for enhanced backup and restore operations.
* **File\-Level Restore**

	+ Provides both agentless and agent\-based file\-level restores for granular recovery.
* **Secondary Copy Level Browse and Restore**

	+ Enables browsing and restoring from secondary copy levels.
* **Changed Block Tracking (CBT)**

	+ Changed Block Tracking (CBT) to optimize backup performance by backing up only changed data.
* **Full VM Restores** 

	+ Supports full VM restores, including in\-place and out\-of\-place options.

Nutanix Clusters Deployment and Pre\-requisites
For the latest and most accurate information on deployment and prerequisites for Nutanix clusters, refer to the [Nutanix documentation](https://portal.nutanix.com/page/documents/list?type=software).

citations.title: User Guide - Preparing your environment for successful Druva Nutanix AHV Backup
citations.text:
User Guide - Preparing your environment for successful Druva Nutanix AHV Backup
Purpose > 1\. What is Nutanix?

* Nutanix converges server compute, storage, storage networking, and virtualization and lets you manage the entire infrastructure through **Prism Elements** and **Prism Central**.

---

**💡 Tip** 

*(If Compared with VMWARE, Prism Element is similar to ESXi and Prism Central is similar to vCenter)* 

---

2\.What is Nutanix AHV?
* Nutanix AHV is a virtualization platform that powers VMs and containers for applications and cloud\-native workloads on\-premises and in public clouds.
* Nutanix AHV ( **N** utanix **A** cropolis **H** ypervisor) is a Nutanix own developed native bare metal Type\-1 hypervisor

3\.Why perform a Nutanix AHV VM backup?
* To protect crucial data which helps us in case of hardware failure, natural disasters, cyber\-attacks, or accidental deletion.
* In case of disaster, you can perform restorations in three ways: 

	+ Full VM restore
	+ Disk Restore
	+ Folder level restore

4\. What does Druva back up from Nutanix AHV?
* Druva performs agent\-less backup with the help of a backup appliance known as [backup proxy](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651326-about-backup-proxy-for-nutanix).
* Druva helps to protect virtual machines in **Prism Element** s or **Prism Centrals**.
* Decide what you want to protect. 

	+ **\[A]** VMs in a Prism Element. 

		- If you deploy a Backup proxy in a Prism Element and register it, Druva will only backup VMs managed by the Prism Element.
	+ **\[B]** VMs in a Prism Central. 

		- If you deploy a Backup proxy in a Prism Central environment and register it, Druva backs up VMs in all clusters managed by Prism Central.
* Backup scope 

	+ Full backup
	+ Application consistent Backup (NGT Tool required).
	+ Incremental Backup (using Nutanix Change Region Tracking(CRT))

---

**📝 Note**  
​*\- Nutanix Guest tools for virtual machine quiescing and application\-consistent backups. However, Druva can take a snapshot even without Nutanix Guest Tools resulting in crash\-consistent backups.* 

---

5\. What is Nutanix AHV backup proxy in Druva?
* Backup proxy is the key component that sits between your data center and Druva Cloud and is responsible for performing backup and restore of virtual machines. [Click Here to know more:](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651326-about-backup-proxy-for-nutanix)
* [Prerequisites](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651331-prerequisites-for-backup-proxy-deployment) to install the backup proxy.
* A Backup Proxy is responsible for VM Discovery and VM Backup/Restore using Prism Central or Prism Element.
* Deploy first backup proxy and register the Prism. [Link](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8832088-deploy-the-first-backup-proxy-and-register-prism)

6\. What is the Druva backup workflow for Nutanix AHV?
To learn more about the backup workflow for Nutanix AHV, ( [Click Here](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651327-nutanix-ahv-backup-workflow) )

7\. What are the requirements before you run an installation for Druva Backup Proxy?
* Druva performs agent\-less backup with the help of a backup appliance called Backup Proxy.
* To backup a Nutanix VM using Prism you have to assign the **iSCSI Data Services IP** address in the Prism ( [Click Here](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651332-configure-data-services-ip) )
* Druva uses port **9440** and **443** to perform backup and restore ( [Click Here](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651330-ports-and-communication-protocols) )
* Druva seeds data to Amazon s3 and in order to facilitate this operation, certain **firewall rules** need to be added. please refer to the following link:( [Click Here](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651333-firewall-rules-for-nutanix-ahv) )

---

**📝 Note**  
​*\- It is not a requirement but a best practice, to have the Proxy server deployed on same container as the VMs(Virtual Machines) that are getting backed up*

---

8\. How do I register a Nutanix setup in Druva?
* To register your Nutanix setup with Druva, you need to deploy a backup proxy that performs backup and restore operations.
* You can deploy / install backup proxy using 2 methods: 

	+ Recommended way 

		- Hybrid Workloads Common Installer (Windows) ( [Step\-by\-step user interface template](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8832088-deploy-the-first-backup-proxy-and-register-prism) )
	+ Workaround 

		- [OVA](https://help.druva.com/en/articles/8651341-manually-deploy-the-backup-proxy-using-prism-console) (Manual way)

citations.title: Nutanix AHV
citations.text:
Nutanix AHV

Veeam Backup \& Replication offers various data protection and disaster recovery features for Nutanix AHV environments. Specifically, you can perform the following operations:

* Create backups of Nutanix AHV VMs and store them in backup repositories.
* Create VeeamZIP backups of Nutanix AHV VMs.
* Create several instances (copies) of the same backed\-up data in different locations.
* Restore VMs from Nutanix AHV backups and snapshots to the original Nutanix AHV environment.
* Restore VMs from VMware ESXi and Microsoft Hyper\-V to the Nutanix AHV environment.

* Restore VMs from HPE Morpheus VM Essentials, oVirt KVM, Proxmox VE, Sangfor aSV, Scale Computing HyperCore, XCP\-ng and Citrix XenServer backups to the Nutanix AHV environment.

* Restore VMs from backups produced by Veeam Plug\-in for Universal Hypervisor API to the Veeam Plug\-in for Nutanix AHV environment.

* Restore VMs from Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud backups to the Nutanix AHV environment.
* Restore physical machines from backups created by Veeam Agents to the Nutanix AHV environment.
* Restore VMs from Nutanix AHV backups to Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud environments.
* Restore VMs from Nutanix AHV backups to VMware vSphere and Microsoft Hyper\-V environments.

* Restore VMs from Nutanix AHV backups to HPE Morpheus VM Essentials, oVirt KVM, Proxmox VE, Sangfor aSV, Scale Computing HyperCore, XCP\-ng, Citrix XenServer environments and universal hypervisors.

* Perform Instant Recovery of VMs and physical machines to VMware vSphere, Microsoft Hyper\-V, Nutanix AHV and Proxmox VE environments.
* Perform Instant Recovery of Nutanix AHV VM disks from backups and attach them to VMs running in Nutanix AHV clusters.
* Restore files and folders of Nutanix AHV VM guest OSes.
* Restore application items (such as Microsoft Active Directory, Microsoft Exchange, Microsoft SharePoint, PostgreSQL, Oracle Database and Microsoft SQL Server).
* Restore Nutanix AHV VM disks and attach them to VMs running in Nutanix AHV clusters.
* Export disks of backed\-up Nutanix AHV VMs to VMDK, VHD and VHDX formats.

* Mount disks of backed\-up Nutanix AHV VMs to any server and access data in the read\-only mode.

citations.title: Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV
citations.text:
Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV

With Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV, you can immediately recover different workloads as Nutanix AHV VMs. You can use Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV to migrate the entire infrastructure or individual VMs to a Nutanix AHV cluster.

| Important |
| --- |
| To restore to Nutanix AHV, you must install Veeam Plug\-In for Nutanix AHV on the backup server. To learn more, see the [Installation](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbahv/userguide/install_ahv_services.html?ver=9) section in the Veeam Plug\-In for Nutanix AHV User Guide. |

Supported Backup Types

To recover machines to a Nutanix AHV cluster, you can use the following backups:

* Backups of VMware vSphere virtual machines created by Veeam Backup \& Replication.
* Backups of VMware Cloud Director virtual machines created by Veeam Backup \& Replication.
* Backups of Microsoft Hyper\-V virtual machines created by Veeam Backup \& Replication.

* Backups of virtual and physical machines created by [Veeam Agent for Microsoft Windows or Veeam Agent for Linux](agents_introduction.html).

* Backups of Nutanix AHV virtual machines created by [Veeam Plug\-In for Nutanix AHV](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbahv/userguide/overview.html?ver=9).
* Backups of Amazon EC2 instances created by [Veeam Backup for AWS](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbaws/guide/overview.html?ver=10).
* Backups of Microsoft Azure virtual machines created by [Veeam Backup for Microsoft Azure](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbazure/guide/overview.html?ver=8.1).
* Backups of Google Compute Engine VM instances created by [Veeam Backup for Google Cloud](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbgc/guide/welcome.html?ver=7).

* Backups of oVirt VMs created by [Veeam Plug\-In for oVirt KVM](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbrhv/userguide/overview.html?ver=7).
* Backups of Proxmox VE VMs created by [Veeam Plug\-In for Proxmox VE](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbproxmoxve/userguide/overview.html?ver=3).

* Backups of Scale Computing HyperCore VMs created by [Veeam Plug\-in for Scale Computing HyperCore](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vpsch/userguide/overview.html?ver=2).

* Backups of HPE Morpheus VM Essentials VMs created by [Veeam Plug\-in for HPE Morpheus VM Essentials](hpe_morpheus_vme.html).
* Backups of Xen VMs created by [Veeam Plug\-in for Xen](xen.html).

* Backups of Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization VMs created by [Veeam Plug\-in for KubeVirt](vkp.html).

Performing Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV

The procedure of restore to Nutanix AHV practically does not differ from the procedure described in the [Performing Instant Recovery of Workloads to Nutanix AHV](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbahv/userguide/instant_recovery_ahv.html?ver=9) section in the Veeam Plug\-In for Nutanix AHV User Guide.

[

![Launch Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV](/media/2d0d2d1a-296f-450e-b7f7-f4c97278e98d/bc164756ce8f0c18.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Veeam Backup and Replication interface showing the 'Backup' tab with a context menu open for 'Instant recovery'. The menu highlights the 'Nutanix AHV...' option, indicating the action to launch Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV for a selected backup job.

](images/instant_recovery_to_nutanix.png "Launch Instant Recovery to Nutanix AHV")

Quick configuration checklist to protect AHV virtual machines
Quick configuration checklist to protect AHV virtual machines

| Step overview | Description and reference |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy NetBackup to protect AHV VMs | On a very high level to protect AHV VMs you need:* NetBackup primary server * NetBackup media server (Recommended) * NetBackup client that can act as a backup host The operating system of the backup host must be a Linux RHEL, SUSE, or Windows. The backup host can be a NetBackup media server or a client, or an NetBackup Appliance.NetBackup appliance including Flex appliance and Flex scale appliance is also supported as a NetBackup media server that can act as a backup host. NetBackup uses an agentless architecture to protect the AHV VMs. The communication between NetBackup and AHV cluster happens through Nutanix AHV APIs. |
| Configure an AHV access host for backup and recovery | An AHV access host acts as a backup host and a recovery host during backup and recovery respectively. The access host is involved in the data movement during the backup and restore operations.If you plan to use a backup host that is not a NetBackup media server or an appliance, add the backup host to the NetBackup AHV Access Hosts list.Note: A backup host which is not a media server or an appliance needs to have the NetBackup client installed on it.See [Add an AHV access host](v147709570-173785610 "Add an AHV access host"). |
| Enable secure communication between NetBackup and AHV | The following sections contain more information about setting up a secure communication between NetBackup and AHV:* Secure communicationSee [Configure secure communication between the AHV cluster and NetBackup host and Nutanix Prism Central and NetBackup host](v147708883-173785610 "Configure secure communication between the AHV cluster and NetBackup host and Nutanix Prism Central and NetBackup host"). * Communication portsSee [About the ports that NetBackup uses to communicate with AHV](v147709114-173785610 "About the ports that NetBackup uses to communicate with AHV"). |
| Manage AHV clusters, Prism Central server, and intelligent VM groups | * Managing AHV clustersSee [Add or browse an AHV cluster](v147709147-173785610 "Add or browse an AHV cluster"). * Managing Prism Central serverSee [Add a new Nutanix Prism Central](v158257181-173785610 "Add a new Nutanix Prism Central"). * Managing intelligent VM groupsSee [Create an intelligent VM group](v147709148-173785610 "Create an intelligent VM group").See [Remove the intelligent VM group](v147709417-173785610 "Remove the intelligent VM group"). |
| Protect the AHV VMs | * Prerequisite:Adding an AHV cluster requires the Default AHV Administrator role. * Best practicesSee [Things to know before you protect AHV virtual machines](v147709766-173785610 "Things to know before you protect AHV virtual machines"). * Protecting virtual machinesSee [Protect AHV VMs or intelligent VM groups using Protection plan](v147709971-173785610 "Protect AHV VMs or intelligent VM groups using Protection plan"). |
| iSCSI Transport for Windows backup hosts | Prerequisite For Windows 2012 or later, iSCSI client initiator is present on Windows. By default, the iSCSI initiator service is stopped or disabled on Windows.See [Enable the iSCSI initiator service on windows backup host](v148946256-173785610 "Enable the iSCSI initiator service on windows backup host").Note: If a backup or a recovery host that is selected is on Windows, ensure that iSCSI service is running on windows computer to avoid failure of backup or restore jobs. |
| iSCSI Transport for Linux backup hosts | PrerequisiteTo use iSCSI, `scsi-initiator-utils` package must be installed. By default, it is installed on the RHEL/SUSE.See [Install the iSCSI initiator package on Linux backup host](v148946257-173785610 "Install the iSCSI initiator package on Linux backup host").Note: To use the NFS protocol on the Linux backup or recovery host,  NFS allowed listing of the host on the Nutanix AHV Prism Console is required. For details, refer [https://www.veritas.com/content/support/en\_US/doc/127664414\-132725336\-0/v127698742\-132725336](https://docs.cohesity.com/docs/netbackup/8.1.2/127664414-132725336-0/v127698742-132725336). If the `iscsi-initiator-utils` package is already installed on the backup or the recovery host,  ensure that the iSCSI daemon is running.* To check the status of the daemon use the command **systemctl status iscsid**. * If the daemon is disabled then run the command **systemctl enable iscsid** and then run the command to start the iSCSI daemon **systemctl start iscsid**. |

citations.title: Protecting AHV virtual machines with file-level backups
citations.text:
Protecting AHV virtual machines with file-level backups
Protecting AHV virtual machines with file\-level backups

In most cases, Unitrends recommends that you use host\-level backups to protect your AHV virtual machines. However, in some instances, you might wish to protect your VMs at the guest level in the same way you would protect physical machines, by using agent\-based file\-level or Windows image\-level backups. Host\-level and agent\-based backups provide you with different options. 

Use the following topics to determine whether to run host\-level or agent\-based backups of AHV virtual machines:

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)](#)[General features of AHV host\-level and agent\-based protection](#)

General features of AHV host\-level and agent\-based protection are given here:

NOTE  To protect a VM with both host\-level and agent\-based backups, ensure that the VM's host\-level and agent\-based jobs do not overlap. Running both simultaneously may lead to undesirable results.

| AHV protection strategy | Considerations |
| --- | --- |
| Host\-level backups | The following apply to host\-level backups: ●   Quickest setup, do not need to add VMs individually or install a Unitrends agent on each VM. ●   Automatically include new VMs in backup schedules. (Not supported for SLA policy schedules.) ●   Leverages Nutanix REST APIs to perform application and operating system consistent backup and recovery. Application consistent protection requires that Nutanix Guest Tools (NGT) are installed and running on the virtual machine. ●   Supports excluding disks from a backup. If you have a requirement to exclude data at the directory\- or file\-level, or if you don’t have space in your containers for snapshots of your VMs, consider using file\-level backups. ●   Supports recovering individual files from backups for VMs running Windows or Linux. |
| Agent based file\-level backups | The following apply to file\-level backups: ●   Backup appliance treats the VM like a physical asset. ●   All backup options are supported, including options to exclude files, directories, or volumes from backup, and run pre\- and post\-backup commands. Recommended for VMs where more granular exclusion of data is required. ●   Provide application and operating system consistent backup and recovery. ●   Support Windows replicas to quickly spin up a virtual replica of a failed Windows asset. File\-level application backups provide these benefits:  NOTE  Application backups schedules cannot be created through SLA policies. ●   SQL, Exchange, Oracle, and SharePoint backups perform application\-level post backup processing, such as log truncation. ●   Support all SQL database recovery models. Must run file\-level application backups for all recovery models other than simple. ●   Support backup of multi\-node SharePoint farms. |
| Agent based Windows image\-level backups | The following apply to Windows image\-level backups: ●   Assets are protected and the disk and volume level.  ●   Backups include the 'in use' regions of the Windows disk or volume only. Deleted regions are not included. ●   Provide application consistent backup and recovery for NTFS and ReFS filesystems.  ●   Provide crash consistent backup and recovery for FAT, FAT32, and exFAT filesystems.  ●   Opt to include or exclude volumes from backup.  ●   Opt to run commands on the asset before or after the backup job. ●   Opt to index the backup so you can search an asset's backups by filename to recover individual files. This option is set by asset (see [To edit an agent\-based asset](Managing_protected_assets.htm#To_edit_an_asset) for details). |

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)](#)[File\-level protection examples](#)

Specific instances when you might want to protect VMs at the asset level are described below. For instructions on setting up file\-level protection, see [Protected assets](Protected_Assets.htm).

citations.title: AHV virtual machines
citations.text:
AHV virtual machines

This section provides considerations and requirements for protecting virtual machines hosted in Nutanix Acropolis Hypervisor (AHV) environments.

NOTE  AHV host\-level backups include the VM file data but not the Acropolis File Services data that is internal to the Nutanix share. To protect this internal data, you can add the Nutanix share to the Unitrends appliance and run Unitrends NAS backups over the NFS protocol. Start by reviewing the requirements in [NAS protection using CIFS/NFS](NAS_Backups_Overview.htm#NAS_protection_using_CIFS/NFS). Next, add the share to the Unitrends appliance as described in [To add a NAS CIFS or NFS asset](Managing_protected_assets.htm#To_add_a_NAS_CIFS/NFS_asset). Then create a backup job as described in [Create a NAS CIFS or NFS backup job](create-nas-cifs-nfs-backup-job.htm).

NOTE  Unitrends does not backup or restore category values for Nutanix VMs.

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)Preparing for AHV backups](#)

When you add an AHV host cluster to the appliance, all VMs are discovered and available for host\-level protection. Unitrends leverages Nutanix REST APIs to communicate with AHV hosts. 

The following information summarizes the high\-level steps that protect AHV virtual machines. The steps include links to detailed instructions for each procedure.

**Step 1:** Review the [Best practices and requirements for AHV protection](#Best_practices_and_requirements_for_AHV_protection).

**Step 2:** Add the AHV host cluster to your Unitrends appliance. See [Adding a virtual host](Managing_protected_assets.htm#Adding_a_virtual_host).

**Step 3:** Create backup jobs for your VMs:

●   To create a job manually, see [Create a Nutanix AHV backup job](create-ahv-backup-job.htm).

●   To create a job by using an SLA policy, see [To create an SLA policy for AHV assets](creating_sla_policies.htm#To_create_an_SLA_policy_for_AHV).

●   For a comparison of the manual and SLA policy job creation methods, see [About creating backup and backup copy jobs](Backup_Administration_and_Procedures.htm#About_creating_backup_and_backup_copy_jobs). 

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)](#)[Best practices and requirements for AHV protection](#)

Review the information in these topics before implementing AHV host\-level protection:

[![Closed](https://help.unitrends.kaseya.com/help/Skins/Default/Stylesheets/Images/transparent.gif)](#)[AHV best practices and considerations](#)

Follow these best practices to protect your AHV virtual machines:

●   Adhere to Nutanix best practices.

●   Full and incremental backups are supported for AHV VMs.

●   A new full backup is required if the VM configuration has changed since the last backup. This includes any configuration changes made to a VM through the hypervisor, such as creating or deleting a snapshot, or adding a new disk.

If the VM configuration has changed since the last backup, the next incremental fails. After this failure, the appliance promotes the next scheduled backup to a full (or displays a message indicating a full is required if an on\-demand incremental is attempted). Once a full backup succeeds, subsequent incrementals run as scheduled.

●   Due to a Nutanix limitation, Unitrends AHV snapshots do not display in the Nutanix AHV hypervisor. Note the following:

●   The first time a VM is backed up, the job creates a new snapshot of the AHV VM that remains with the VM after the job completes. During subsequent backups, the job creates a new snapshot of the AHV VM, performs the backup, then removes either the previous snapshot (if the job was successful) or the current snapshot (if the job failed). If a job ends ungracefully (such as due to a power outage) the unneeded snapshot may remain on the hypervisor. A Unitrends cleanup process runs hourly to check for and remove any unneeded snapshots. 

●   If you are no longer protecting a VM on this Unitrends appliance, any leftover snapshot that has not been removed will remain on the hypervisor. This applies even if you begin protecting the VM with another Unitrends appliance. If you are no longer protecting a VM with the original Unitrends appliance, contact Support for assistance removing any unneeded snapshots.

●   In some cases, you may want or need to protect VMs by using agent based, file\-level or image\-level backups. For recommendations, see [Protecting AHV virtual machines with file\-level backups](Protecting_AHV_virtual_mac.htm).

●   To protect a VM with both host\-level and file\-level (agent\-based) backups, ensure that the VM's host\-level and file\-level jobs do not overlap. Running both simultaneously may lead to undesirable results.

citations.text:
Nutanix Acropolis Hypervisor (AHV)
Supported versions[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/nutanix-acropolis-ahv#supported-versions) > Proxy VM disk configuration[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/nutanix-acropolis-ahv#proxy-vm-disk-configuration)

Keep the proxy VM's disk layout simple. Where the backup destination permits staging on the destination storage, use a single local disk for the proxy VM operating system.

If local staging requires a separate disk, use a volume from Nutanix container storage. Verify device selection during a test backup, particularly when the proxy VM has multiple disks.

Configure LVM filters according to the Storware guide **LVM setup on Storware Backup & Recovery Node for disk attachment backup mode**. Include the proxy VM's own OS disks, partitions, and any required local staging devices. Reboot the proxy VM after applying the changes as directed by that guide.

**Verify the dynamically attached disks slot offset**

The **Dynamically attached disks slot offset** setting determines where the node expects dynamically attached disks. A proxy VM with several local disks may require manual adjustment.

1.  Before starting a backup, connect to the proxy VM and run:

    Copy

        lsblk

2.  Record the disks that belong to the proxy VM.

3.  Enable debug logging on the node and run a test backup of a small VM.

4.  Inspect the node logs and verify that the exported device is an attached snapshot disk.

For example, if `/dev/sda` and `/dev/sdb` belong to the proxy VM, a snapshot disk appearing as `/dev/sdc` is consistent with that layout. Device names depend on the actual environment and must be checked locally.

If the node selects one of its own disks, correct the offset using **KB10037: How to change the Dynamically attached disks slot offset parameter** before running further backups.

Multiple nodes[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/nutanix-acropolis-ahv#multiple-nodes)
You can deploy several nodes in a cluster and map individual hypervisors to them. Each node handles VMs assigned to its mapped hypervisors, providing static distribution of backup jobs. VMs without an assigned hypervisor are handled by the node configured for the virtualization provider.

Run inventory synchronization for every node to register its proxy VM UUID.

Backup and restore[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/nutanix-acropolis-ahv#backup-and-restore)
**Backup**

Storware Backup & Recovery creates a VM snapshot, exports its metadata, and attaches the snapshot disks to the proxy VM one at a time. The node reads the disk data locally. Incremental backups use Nutanix changed-region information to read only changed blocks.

If at least one schedule assigned to the VM specifies incremental backups, the latest snapshot is retained for the next incremental backup.

**Restore**

Storware Backup & Recovery creates empty disks on the proxy VM and writes the restored data to them. It then recreates the target VM and attaches the restored disks to it.

Snapshot consistency[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/nutanix-acropolis-ahv#snapshot-consistency)
Storware Backup & Recovery supports crash-consistent snapshots and optional application preparation through pre/post snapshot commands. The **QuiesceBeforeSnapshot** setting requests a quiesced snapshot and requires guest tools in the protected VM. The resulting snapshot type depends on the availability of those tools; requesting quiescing does not guarantee application consistency.

Limitations and scope[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/nutanix-acropolis-ahv#limitations-and-scope)
*   Backup of VMs with vTPM enabled is not supported.

*   Only standard VM disks are protected through the VM backup integration. Attached Nutanix Volume Group disks are not included in VM snapshots, backups, or snapshot reverts.

*   Nutanix Volume Group and Nutanix Files protection must be configured separately in the **Storage Provider** section.

*   Tag-based policy assignment requires Prism Central.

*   At least one proxy VM is required per protected cluster.

Nutanix v4[](https://docs.storware.eu/protecting-virtual-machines/virtual-machines/nutanix-acropolis-ahv#nutanix-v4)

Getting started
Topics:

- PowerProtect Data Manager for Nutanix AHV virtual machines overview
- About asset sources, assets, and protection storage

- Access the PowerProtect Data Manager UI
- Roadmap for Nutanix AHV virtual machine protection

PowerProtect Data Manager for Nutanix AHV virtual machines overview
PowerProtect Data Manager enables the protection of Nutanix Acropolis Hypervisor (AHV) workloads, which includes the backup of Nutanix virtual machine assets with local storage. PowerProtect Data Manager supports the following functionality for Nutanix AHV:

- Enable a protection engine for Nutanix clusters from the PowerProtect Data Manager UI.
- Configure Nutanix virtual machine protection policy and protection storage settings.
- Create a catalog of Nutanix virtual machine backups. Then, monitor that catalog data to determine if retention policies are being adhered to.
- Manage the life cycle of Nutanix virtual machine backups to ensure that backups are marked for garbage collection according to the rules of the retention policy.
- Image-level restore support for virtual machines to the original location or to a new virtual machine.

About asset sources, assets, and protection storage
In PowerProtect Data Manager, assets are the basic units that PowerProtect Data Manager protects. Asset sources are the mechanism that PowerProtect Data Manager uses to manage assets and communicate with the protection storage where backup copies of the assets are stored.

For Nutanix AHV, the Prism Central is the asset source and the virtual machines are the assets. Before you can add an asset source, you must enable the source within the PowerProtect Data Manager UI. You can then add and configure protection storage to use as a target for protection policies. The *Dell PowerProtect Data Manager Administrator Guide* provides instructions.

Additional information and context
This guide contains content that is specific to protecting Nutanix AHV virtual machines. It does not include information about server administration or tasks that are common to all asset types.

For important information about configuring PowerProtect Data Manager before and during use, including prerequisites such as adding protection storage and creating storage units, see the *Dell PowerProtect Data Manager Administrator Guide* .

citations.title: Backup and Restore Strategies
citations.text:
Backup and Restore Strategies

[Enterprise](https://docs.baculasystems.com/BCBEComparison/index.html)
Bacula Enterprise Only

This solution is **only** available for Bacula Enterprise. For subscription inquiries, please reach out to <sales@baculasystems.com>.

This article presents information regarding backup and restore strategies of the Nutanix\-AHV Plugin.

Installing Bacula Client on Each Guest
This strategy works by installing a Bacula Enterprise File Daemon on
every virtual machine as if they were normal physical clients. In order
to optimize the I/O usage on the [Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) hypervisor, the user will use
Bacula’s Schedules, Priorities, and Maximum Concurrent Jobs to spread
backup jobs over the backup window. Since all VMs could use the
same storage on the [Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) hypervisor, running all backup jobs
at the same time could create a bottleneck on the disk/network
subsystem since Bacula will walk through all filesystems to open/read/close/stat files.

Installing a Bacula Enterprise File Daemon on each virtual machine
permits to manage virtual servers like physical servers and
also to use all Bacula Enterprise’s features such as:

* Quick restores of individual files
* Checksum of individual files for Virus and Spyware detection
* Verify Jobs
* File/Directory exclusion (such as swap or temporary files)
* File level compression
* Accurate backups.

Image Backup With Nutanix\-AHV Plugin
With the image backup level strategy, the Bacula Enterprise
[Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) Plugin will save the Client disks at the raw level, in the
[Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) context.

Bacula’s [Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) Plugin will query the [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM) through the hypervisor API
to read and save the content of virtual machines disks using snapshots and the native Nutanix Filesystem ([NDFS](../../../../../glossary.html#term-NDFS)).
During backups, [Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) Plugin will save the integrity of disks images and also [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM)
configurations to allow [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM) restores with their original parameters.

All those operations are handled by an additional [proxy VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-proxy-VM) which is described in the next section.

citations.title: Backup and Restore Strategies
citations.text:
Backup and Restore Strategies
Ingestion

The ingestion of a single virtual disk is a specific protocol which takes the following steps:

* From [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM) snapshot find [NDFS](../../../../../glossary.html#term-NDFS) paths of all modified disks.
* Use said [NDFS](../../../../../glossary.html#term-NDFS) path to list changed regions on the disk either from its base state or from a previous snapshot.
* Use said [NDFS](../../../../../glossary.html#term-NDFS) path again to hotplug a copy of the disk onto the [proxy VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-proxy-VM).
* Export the list of changed regions and raw disk image data to a Bacula Storage Daemon
* Unplug relevant disk from [proxy VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-proxy-VM)

Backups can be performed for a [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM) in any power state (running or halted). For proper execution of Incremental or Differential backups it is required by the [Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) plugin to store previous snapshots in order to compute changed block information.

Snapshots created by the [Nutanix\-AHV](../../../../../glossary.html#term-Nutanix-AHV) plugin are identified by JobID and the UUID of the [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM). The plugin keeps track of dependencies between jobs and their respective snapshots to automatically delete snapshots that are no more relevant.

The backup will create the following backup files for each [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM):

* A single empty file to match a [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM) name to its UUID
/@nutanix\-ahv/\<vmUuid\>\_\<vmName\>.name
* A list of data regions for each virtual disk:
/@nutanix\-ahv/\<vmUuid\>/\<diskUuid\>.bmp
* A list of zeroed regions for each virtual disk:
/@nutanix\-ahv/\<vmUuid\>/\<diskUuid\>.abmp
* A raw data file for each virtual disk:
/@nutanix\-ahv/\<vmUuid\>/\<diskUuid\>.bvmdk

Note

Configuration files are not showed in this view but are still handled by the plugin.

At restore time the user can identify the [guest VM](../../../../../glossary.html#term-guest-VM) using the UUID to mark the corresponding files:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| filename                                                                                      |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| /@nutanix-ahv/690d74f9-9ce4-45fb-9b23-149afebe18f7_VmName.name                                |
| /@nutanix-ahv/690d74f9-9ce4-45fb-9b23-149afebe18f7/eef9d485-dba3-4e3f-b828-46a8c3412bec.bmp   |
| /@nutanix-ahv/690d74f9-9ce4-45fb-9b23-149afebe18f7/eef9d485-dba3-4e3f-b828-46a8c3412bec.abmp  |
| /@nutanix-ahv/690d74f9-9ce4-45fb-9b23-149afebe18f7/eef9d485-dba3-4e3f-b828-46a8c3412bec.bvmdk |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

```

citations.title: Agent-based and agentless backup
citations.text:
Agent-based and agentless backup
Agent\-based and agentless backup

Agent\-based backup requires that a protection agent is installed on each protected machine. Agent\-based backup is supported on all physical and virtual machines. 

Agentless backup is supported by some virtualization platforms and it is not available for physical machines. Agentless backup requires only one protection agent, which is installed on a dedicated machine in the virtual environment. This agent backs up all other virtual machines in this environment. For more information about the supported backup types per virtualization platform, see [Supported virtualization platforms](supported-virtualization-platforms.html).

For some virtualization platforms, virtual appliances are available. A virtual appliance (VA) is a ready\-made virtual machine that contains a protection agent. The virtual appliances are available in hypervisor\-specific formats, such as .ovf, .ova, or .qcow.

Which backup type do I need?
We recommend the agent\-based backup if you need the following:

* Additional protection functionality, such as antivirus and antimalware, patch management, or remote desktop connection.
* Separate virtual machines at the tenant level. For example, because you want to provide the users in the tenant with access only to their own backups.
* File\-level backups that you can recover to the guest operating systems.

We recommend the agentless backup if you need the following:

* Only backup, without any additional protection features.
* Simplified management—you can back up multiple virtual machines by installing and configuring only one agent.
* Minimal resource usage—one dedicated agent uses less CPU and RAM than multiple agents installed on each virtual machine in your environment.
* Specific backup setups, such as LAN\-free backup. For more information about this feature, see [LAN\-free backup](lan-free-backup.html).
* Less configuration overhead. The dedicated agent backs up the virtual machines on the hypervisor level, regardless of guest operating systems.

If any of the prerequisites are not satisfied, then only the offline backup method is used. 

The Microsoft offline backup method has two approaches \- save state approach and checkpoint approach. If the Hyper\-V host has the Windows 2012 R2 operating system with KB 2919355 or later, then the checkpoint approach is used; else the save state approach is used. 

The major difference between these two approaches is that the save state approach requires the virtual machine to be inaccessible for a short time. The virtual machine must be placed into a saved state for a few minutes while taking the snapshot.

Apart from the Microsoft native snapshot methods Arcserve Console – On\-Premises has its own snapshot method that can be used when the Microsoft native snapshot methods are not available.

VM may be Placed into Saved state before Snapshot is Taken

citations.title: AHV snapshot consistency
citations.text:
AHV snapshot consistency

With the AHV snapshot consistency feature, you can select the type of snapshot you
 want RSC to take. Depending on your specific requirements, RSC can take either application\-consistent snapshots or crash\-consistent
 snapshots.

Using the AHV snapshot consistency feature, you can select the type of snapshot that you
 want RSC to take for your AHV virtual machines.

Snapshot types
RSC supports the following snapshot types for AHV virtual machines:* Application\-consistent or automatic snapshot: A snapshot of an AHV virtual
 machine is considered application consistent if, in addition to capturing
 all of the data at the instant of the crash, the running applications have
 completed all their operations and flushed their buffers to the disk
 attached to the AHV virtual machine. Rubrik recommends using
 application\-consistent snapshots for database operating systems and
 applications such as SQL, Oracle, and Microsoft Exchange.By default, RSC takes application\-consistent snapshots for your AHV
 virtual machines.
* Crash\-consistent snapshot: A crash\-consistent snapshot captures only the
 data already written to the disks attached to the AHV virtual machine. Any
 data that is still in memory or pending I/O operations is not captured in
 the snapshot. Rubrik recommends using the crash\-consistent snapshot for
 non\-database operating systems and applications such as file servers, DHCP
 servers, or print servers.

Configuration scope
You can configure AHV snapshot consistency at the following levels:* Nutanix cluster: When you configure an application\-consistent or a
 crash\-consistent snapshot for a Nutanix cluster, RSC takes
 the configured snapshot for all the AHV virtual machines running on the
 Nutanix cluster.
Important: Configuring the AHV snapshot consistency for a
 Nutanix cluster is only available for a Rubrik cluster running
 Rubrik CDM version 9\.1 or later.
* AHV virtual machine: When you configure an application\-consistent or a
 crash\-consistent snapshot for an AHV virtual machine, RSC
 takes the configured snapshot for that AHV virtual machine. Regardless of
 the snapshot type configured at the Nutanix cluster level, the snapshot type
 you configure at the AHV virtual machine level always takes precedence.

You can configure the AHV snapshot consistency feature while adding a Nutanix cluster
 to RSC or from the Nutanix Virtual Machines inventory page.

citations.title: Recovery of AHV virtual machines
citations.text:
Recovery of AHV virtual machines

You can recover an AHV virtual machine or specific disks within a virtual machine
 from snapshots that are locally available on a Rubrik cluster.

Locally available snapshots are snapshots downloaded from archival locations or
 replication targets to a Rubrik cluster. You can recover an AHV virtual machine, or
 specific disks within a virtual machine, from these snapshots.

You cannot recover an AHV virtual machine from snapshots that are available only at
 remote archival locations or replication targets, or from local snapshots that have
 expired.

To recover AHV virtual machines, Rubrik clusters provide the following options:* Recover files: Restores the files and folders from a snapshot.
* Live mount: Creates and mounts a new virtual machine on a Nutanix cluster using
 a snapshot.
* Export: Creates a virtual machine from a point\-in\-time copy of the source
 virtual machine.
* Mount virtual disks: Attaches specific virtual disks to a virtual machine. The
 recovered virtual disks use the Rubrik cluster as their data source.
* Download virtual disks: Downloads specific virtual disks without downloading the
 entire virtual machine.
* In\-place recovery: Recovers the data by transferring only the
 changed blocks of virtual disk data directly from the Rubrik cluster data store
 to the Nutanix cluster.
* Instant recovery: Restores a virtual machine from a snapshot
 and replaces the original virtual machine with a functional point\-in\-time copy
 of the virtual machine hosted on the Rubrik cluster. The Rubrik cluster powers
 on the recovered virtual machine and connects it to the source network.

This chapter explains how to perform a backup using the Tina Nutanix AHV Agent. Full and incremental backups are supported.
